# Phase F1: the TS package mechanism and the leaf TS moves - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The graph's TypeScript gets the package shape its C++ already has. A package's `package.json` gains the
`app` and `protocol` members beside `native` and `script`, and one generator
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`) turns the root `package.json`'s product list and every listed package's
manifest into three gitignored modules under `packages/retroplug/src/generated`: the app's four registration lists in
product order, the protocol node table as data that imports only a type, and the script bundle's entry, which
cross-checks the manifests at load. Two checks hold every package to what its manifest declares, in TypeScript
(`check-boundaries.mjs`, at the start of `pnpm test` and as `pnpm check:boundaries`) and in CMake
(`retroplug_check_package_boundaries()`, at every configure), each with a fixture per refusal that it is proved to
refuse. Then the leaf code moves: `core`, `dsp` and `testing` get their TS halves, `sameboy`, `mesen` and `tracker` are
new packages, and `lsdj`, `mgb`, `risa`, `smsggdj`, `bliptoaster` (widened) and `n8` (widened) take their carts,
roles, ROM providers, tracker integrations, kit formats, protocol nodes, tests and goldens with them. **F1 changes no
behaviour:** every golden, baseline and device image holds unmodified, and nothing is re-recorded.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md), whose section 11 ("As
built") records the build and which Task 5 lands, sections 1 to 10 corrected in place to what the prototype found.
Task 1 lands the product list, the manifests' new members, the generator and its three modules, and makes the five
registry consumers read them while the lists still point at the shell's own modules. Task 2 lands both boundary checks
and their red fixtures, and the native packages' `@retroplug/node-sdk` declarations. Task 3 moves the node mechanism,
the role contract, the document, the kit chain and the test harness into `core`, `dsp` and `testing`, puts every
package on the root `tsconfig.base.json` with its own two-line `tsconfig.json`, pins the bundlers' TypeScript options,
and takes `bliptoaster`, `devtest` and `n8` off their relative reaches into the shell. Task 4 makes `sameboy`, `mesen`
and `tracker` packages, splits `settingsEnums.ts` to its owners and moves the neutral NES helpers and the `.rit` format
down. Task 5 moves the six carts, with their tests and goldens, and lands the docs. Task 6 is the acceptance run.

**Tech stack:** TypeScript 7 (`tsc -p tsconfig.json` per package, the same compiler everywhere) and the repo's
`typescript-5` alias for the checker's scanner, esbuild for every bundle with its options pinned in `tools/ts-options.js`,
zod declared by every package that imports it, pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` dependencies, Node's test harnesses
(`run-tests.mjs`, `run-ui-tests.mjs`, `run-native-tests.mjs`), CMake 3.28 with `string(JSON)` for the product list and a
deferred configure-time boundary check, Catch2 for the C++ oracles that read the TS as text, and the Pico SDK only where
Task 6 rebuilds the device images. No submodule moves, no dependency version changes.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md) and
[package-split.md](package-split.md) (the phase map F1 opens; F1 is the first of its four). The package mechanism this
extends is [modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md)'s, and
[e2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md)'s for products and providers;
[modular-graph-phase-e4-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-e4-plan.md) is the previous plan executed the way this one is.

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/f1-packages` in this worktree, on top of the design commit a085f3d6b: five commits, one per task (Task 6 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), on linux-x64 (a Ryzen 9 9950X, 32 threads, GCC 13.3, `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1
for the two device legs). A block that creates a file is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that changes a
file is the prototype's diff of it, so `git apply` it from the step's text; a move is a `git mv` block and, where the
file changed too, the prototype's diff of its new path; a deletion is a `git rm`. **This phase is mostly moves:** five
hundred files change directory in Task 3 and four hundred in Task 5, most of them with an import specifier as their only
change. Each task's verification is the stage's own runs of `/tmp/f1pro/tip-verify.sh` and the legs its fix passes
re-ran (each task's suites step says which run each figure is from); Task 5's is the final verification
(`/tmp/f1pro/s5fv-*.log`), run at the prototype's code. Every expected pass, test count and figure is quoted from the
stage reports in /tmp/f1pro, those logs, the design's record or the user's decisions, which is what the generator
checks; a figure no log records is said to be so, and the step asks for it. When this plan was generated it was
replayed in a scratch clone of a085f3d6b, every block written, moved or applied in order, and each task committed with
the command given: each commit's tree came out exactly as the prototype's, and each commit message as its. The
prototype commits, by task:

- Task 1 `b939e902e`: feat(packages): generate the TS package registries from the product list
- Task 2 `9aac3871b`: feat(packages): hold the packages to the boundaries their manifests declare
- Task 3 `bebbe6f38`: feat(packages): give core, dsp and testing their TS halves
- Task 4 `311e25f2e`: feat(packages): give SameBoy, Mesen and the tracker layer their own packages
- Task 5 `21d8e4416`: feat(packages): give the six carts their own TS packages and close the split
- Task 6 is the acceptance run and commits nothing.


**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (a085f3d6b).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 5 lands the design with section 11's record and sections 1 to 10 corrected
in place. In short (a bullet quotes the design where it uses quotation marks):

- **The product list is the order, both languages read it, and a list out of dependency order is refused.** The root
  `package.json` holds `"retroplug": { "products": { "desktop": [...] } }` = `["core", "sameboy", "mesen", "dsp",
  "mgb", "lsdj", "graph-runtime", "n8", "smsggdj", "risa", "native", "bliptoaster"]`; the root `CMakeLists.txt`
  reads it into `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES` with `string(JSON)` (a member that is not a list, an empty list and an entry
  that is not a string are each refused in words) and makes the file a configure input, and the generator emits the
  app's lists in that order with the shell last. The list is no longer `core dsp graph-runtime n8 native
  bliptoaster` with the new names appended: the new packages sit where their dependencies put them, so the native
  subsequence is unchanged and `product-registrations.json` with it. The generator refuses a listed package before
  one of its listed dependencies, so CMake's order and the TS lists' cannot disagree, and a cycle is refused by the
  same rule.
- **`retroplug.order` was tried and dropped.** A dependency order of packages cannot reproduce the interleaved role
  list (`risa-sync` sits between `n8`'s and `smsggdj`'s roles), so the first cut added an explicit order per list;
  the review found it dropped a registration silently, and that only a ROM provider's place is observable (roles
  live in a `Map` keyed by kind, the tracker markers are exclusive, the kit ids are looked up). The final form is
  the product list alone, the NES provider in `n8` so no shell block sits in the middle of the providers, and a
  **duplicate** refused by the generated module for the three lists where a duplicate is the real hazard (a role
  kind, a kit format id, a tracker marker role), each with its own message. The registry test pins the twelve role
  kinds as a set and `defaultRoles` over eight fixtures, which is what a reorder can actually move.
- **Three generated modules, not two.** `packages.ts` (the four app lists, in product order, the shell's last),
  `protocol.ts` (the node table and the role map as plain data, importing only `type { ProtocolNodeSpec }`, so
  `protocolNodes.ts` and through it `buildGraph` stay free of the app and of zod: two modules bundled, held under a
  ceiling by a test, against 174 modules and 750 KB when the data lived in `packages.ts`), and `scriptNodes.ts` (the
  script bundle's entry, which sorts the concatenated nodes by the manifests' labels and refuses at load unless the
  registered ids are exactly the declared ones and the labels are `16 + i`). All three are gitignored, written
  through a per-process temporary and a rename, and only when their bytes change.
- **The contribution kinds are typed by module augmentation, and `definePackage` is not generic.** `core`'s
  `PackageContributions` declares only the two kinds its own contract types cover (`roles`, `romProviders`);
  `tracker` augments it with `trackerIntegrations` and `dsp` with `kitFormats`, each a type-only `declare module
  "@retroplug/core/definePackage"`, so `core` imports neither package. `definePackage(p): PackageContributions` is
  the identity and its parameter's type, so a misspelt key is an excess property and a type error rather than an
  inferred type parameter (two `@ts-expect-error` cases hold it). A role is an object, not a `register*` function,
  and a package that needs a `register*` keeps it for its callers.
- **The checks are accident guards, and they say where they stop.** The TS check reads imports with TypeScript's own
  scanner (`ts.preProcessFile`, from the root's `typescript-5` alias, because TypeScript 7 exports none), not
  esbuild's metafile, because esbuild drops a type-only import; it covers `import`, `export ... from`, `import
  type`, a type-position `import("x").T`, `require` and the triple-slash `reference` path and `types` directives. It
  refuses a relative reach out of the package's `ts/`, an undeclared `@retroplug/x` or third-party module, a reach
  into a shell, a cycle in the declared `dependencies`, an `#include` that climbs out of the package, a declaration
  no package answers to a dependency spec that names another package than its key (an alias), and an `exports` entry
  that publishes a test module or a file outside `ts/`. The native check walks the build's targets, attributes each
  to the package whose directory holds its `SOURCE_DIR` (`ALIAS` resolved), and judges links (a target, a file path,
  a `-l` name), include directories, sources, compile options (`-I`, `-iquote`, `-idirafter`, `-isystem`, `/I`,
  `/external:I`, `SHELL:`) and link options (`-L`, `-l`), refusing what it cannot attribute unless the target is
  marked `RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP` with a reason. Neither is a sandbox: each header lists what it does not cover (TS:
  computed specifiers and bundler plugins, `tsconfig` `paths`/`imports`/symlinks, `peerDependencies` and
  `optionalDependencies`, an `exports` condition's resolution, the order a declaration reaches a package in; native:
  per-source properties, cache flags, `LINK_DIRECTORIES`, generator expressions only the build generator can
  evaluate, `-Xlinker`/`-Wl` wrapping, a library name matching no target, `OUTPUT_NAME`/`LINK_DEPENDS`, an
  `include()` of another package's CMake file), and a later hardening starts from those lists.
- **One `tsconfig.base.json`, a two-line `tsconfig.json` per package, and the bundlers' options pinned.**
  `tsconfig.base.json` at the root says what `tsc` accepts and nothing else; its `files` is core's `runtime.d.ts`
  through `${configDir}`, the globals a package may assume. Every package with a `ts/` tree extends it, so `pnpm
  typecheck` is `pnpm -r typecheck` and each typechecks alone. Because esbuild reads the nearest tsconfig per input
  file, giving a package one changed bundles: `strict` implies `alwaysStrict`, whose directive moved the device
  pack's bytecode. So `tools/ts-options.js` spells the options out and every bundle build passes them as
  `tsconfigRaw`, each stating its own `alwaysStrict` (on for the iife bundles that carry the directive, off for the
  device packs and the two derived tools). The UI bundle is the one exception and keeps discovery, because its
  modules come from two trees with different tsconfigs (the shell's `target: ES2020` against `lv_binding_js`'s
  define semantics) and one pin would change how every dpf.js component class initialises.
- **One TypeScript, and zod declared where it is imported.** Every package with a `typecheck` script declares the
  shell's `typescript`, so `pnpm -r typecheck` runs one compiler instead of each package falling back to the root's
  `typescript-5` alias; the checker counts a declared `typescript` a package's own script runs as used, so it does
  not warn. `core` no longer re-exports `z`: `sameboy`, `mesen`, `tracker` and the carts `import { z } from "zod"`
  and declare it, so the boundary check sees every use and reports zero warnings.
- **The NES provider is `n8`'s, and the carts declare no console they do not import.** A package-name order
  concatenates each package's block, so while two providers stayed in the shell no order could put the always-on NES
  provider first and BlipToaster's last: the NES provider moved into `n8` with its role (it attaches `nes-n8-midi`,
  which the N8 owns), one run before that package's widening. And a declared dependency nothing uses is a warning,
  so `risa`, `smsggdj`, `bliptoaster` and `n8` declare neither `mesen` nor `n8`, and `bliptoaster` not `risa`: no
  file in them imports either (the NES helpers they share are `@retroplug/tracker/nes/*`, the `.rit` format lives
  there too). The design's console edges become real in F2 if the carts take the console's enums, or never.
- **The shell bundles differ only by one wrapped array literal.** The built-in script bundle loads the same eight
  nodes in the same order with every `descriptor`, `create`, `layout` and `reshape` source identical; its text
  differs in esbuild's module-path comments, module order and the generated `lists` array. Twenty-one bundles of the
  shell's TS (control plane, render worker, the CLI and its sessions, the UI, the CLI SDK) differ from the baseline
  in nothing but the wrapping of `AUDIO_ROUTING_VALUES` in `settingsEnums.ts` and in module order, and the
  `bliptoaster` pack's lowered text is identical, byte for byte. That is why the pack-bytes and image-hash legs are
  part of every task's proof and not only Task 6's.


**The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/f-split/decisions.md`, the F1 entries; design section 2):

- **The goal is boundaries a third party could copy:** each cart's TypeScript in its own package with explicit
  dependencies, testable alone. Enforced in both languages: `package.json` declares the dependencies; a `pnpm test`
  check fails a TS import outside the package's tree or undeclared, and `packages.cmake` fails the configure on a
  native link or include from an undeclared package; cycles are refused. `packages/retroplug` is the app shell: it
  may depend on every package, and no package may depend on it.
- **The registration lists are generated from the product's package list:** roles and role kinds, ROM providers,
  `PROTOCOL_NODES`/`ROLE_NODES` (import-free), tracker integrations (smsggdj's inline `songWrites` move with it),
  kit formats. The UI (`menuDefs`, `TRACKER_UI`, the HD player, the overlays) and the stores' deep imports keep
  importing the packages directly until F4. F1 changes no behaviour: every baseline identical, no hardware leg.
- **The phase order is F1, then F3 (the Launchpad pack), then F2 (the native carve), then F4 (the UI on
  extensions).** The prototype branch is `proto/f1-packages`, thrown away after this plan; the work directories are
  `f1pro` (prototype), `f1plan` (plan) and `f1exec` (execution), all gitignored under `.superpowers/`.
- **The model routing, which this plan's execution follows:** DeepSeek Flash wrote the prototype's stages, this plan
  and the follow-ups; Flash-Next at `--thinking xhigh` (two at most) implements the plan's tasks and runs the
  acceptance; Opus reviews the prototype's stages and the final tree; the controller coordinates, reviews this plan
  and reviews the risky code.
- **What only the record backs.** The design's section 11 is the description of what was built and of what no log
  records; the stage reports in `/tmp/f1pro` are the working record (which run each figure is from, every review
  finding and its fix, the departures a fix pass forced), and `results.md` is the controller's log of them, with
  each verdict and call. Where this plan quotes a figure, it quotes the report or log that states it; where nothing
  does, it says so and asks for the count.


**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**

- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own). No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code and of the specs): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with uncommitted
  work in the tree. Never touch a submodule: `deps/dpf.js` and everything under it, `deps/sameboy`, `deps/mesen`
  and the rest stay as they are. `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (the two tracked
  patches): expected, leave it, never stage it.
- **This is a move phase: move with `git mv`, never by writing a file at its new path and deleting the old one.** A
  task's `git mv` blocks stage their moves; a moved file that also changes takes the prototype's diff of its **new**
  path right after its move, and a moved file that is byte identical takes nothing. The task's commit `git add`s only
  the files it *changed* (a move and a deletion are already staged), and its expected `git status` list is the check
  that nothing was left out: it names every move (`R  old -> new`), every moved-and-changed file (`RM old -> new`),
  every changed one (` M`), every deletion (`D `) and every new one (`??`), tracked entries first and untracked after
  them, as git prints them.
- **Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by
  the blob hash the file must have:** write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the
  step quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. A retyped slip fails there rather than in a test that never reads
  the line. **Every diff block is followed by its extraction, a `git apply --check`, and the blob hash of each file it
  changes**, so an applied diff is the prototype's bytes and not just something that applies. One new file is
  executable, and its step says so and proves it: `pico/n8-host/exporter-stale.sh`, a script `loop.sh` runs (its
  prototype mode is `100755`). `chmod +x` it where the step says, and leave every other new file `100644`.
- **The generated modules are never committed.** `packages/retroplug/src/generated/{packages,protocol,scriptNodes}.ts`
  are written by `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, gitignored from Task 1 on, and regenerated by the
  runners, `pnpm typecheck` and the CMake `retroplug-ts-packages` target. A worktree a prototype build ran in may
  hold three of them, untracked and stale; Task 1 Step 7 deletes them either way, and from then on no `git status` list
  below shows them. If one ever does, the `.gitignore` entry is wrong: stop and report it.
- **`pnpm-lock.yaml` is a manifest change's companion, and only one install runs, ever:** the steps that change a
  package's dependencies place the lockfile's diff as it stands and then run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, which must leave the lockfile's bytes alone (the step quotes its blob).
  Never run a bare `pnpm install`: offline, a non-frozen one re-resolves the lockfile and silently prunes every other
  platform's optional packages.
- **No golden, baseline, image or bytecode is re-recorded.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
  `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE` or `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE`: a golden that moves
  means the step is wrong. The two goldens that must NOT change are named in every task: the `[packages]` golden
  (`packages/native/test/engine-graph/golden/product-registrations.json`, which the native subsequence holds) and the
  skip baseline (`packages/retroplug/scripts/skip-baseline.json`, untouched because the ts tier records no case for any
  of the trees, so a moved test's slug rename needs no entry). Each task proves both: the golden does not appear in its
  expected `git status` list, `pnpm test:plugin` runs the `[packages]` cases, and `pnpm test` passes the skip baseline's
  own check.
- Every `check:docs` count below is 88: the stages' logs record 87, at the design commit and at every stage (F1 adds no
  tracked Markdown file), and this plan is the 88th tracked Markdown file `check-doc-links` walks. `docs/*-plan.md` are
  records: never edit one (Task 3 and Task 5 repoint their dead links, which is the target path in a markdown link
  and nothing else: no visible text and no line of a record changes).
- The fixture groups need `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources` on the same command line; without it their
  cases skip. A shell `export` does not survive between commands. `pnpm test:native` takes ONE filter per run (an exact
  slug like `render-baseline`, or a dash-form prefix; `risa-render` runs its three files). The CI views pass
  `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/nonexistent-rp-resources RISA_SRC=/nonexistent-rp-risa`, because without them the runners
  fall back to `../resources`, which exists beside this worktree and holds some fixtures.
- **Case counts are exact. Assertion totals are exact too, with two exceptions:** a run of
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` that includes `[engine-jobs]` reports an assertion total that moves from run to run (its
  threaded cases assert in loops), and so does the ThreadSanitizer run of `[script-pack]`; for those the case count must
  match and the total is the prototype's, quoted for scale. Catch2 pads its `test cases:` columns with spaces, which
  the quotes below collapse to one. `pnpm test`'s final line counts FILES; a case total is quoted from the reports and
  is not the runner's own line, so a task that adds cases says which file's block moved.
- **`pnpm typecheck`'s project count moves with the tree** (`Scope: 10 of 11 workspace projects` at Task 1 and 2, 11 of
  12 at Task 3, 14 of 15 at Task 4, 18 of 19 at Task 5), because each task gives another package a `typecheck` script:
  quote the line your step gives, and treat a *different* count at the same task as a finding.
- The Catch2 binaries and `retroplug-render-host-test` are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or outside the default build:
  `cmake --build build` does not rebuild them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before a run
  (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first). `tools/build-device-check.sh` and
  `tools/build-box.sh` build the exporter in the desktop build themselves. A new or removed CMake source or a manifest
  change needs `cmake -S . -B build` first, and **every task that adds a package needs that configure**, because
  `retroplug_product()` refuses a package it was never told about.
- **A `pnpm install` is needed before a configure that reads a new package's `node_modules` link:** the configure checks
  that `packages/retroplug/node_modules/@retroplug/<name>` exists for every package the shell declares and tells you to
  run `pnpm install` if not. Each task's frozen install comes before its configure.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build re-runs CMake and recompiles what
  changed; that is expected. `build-device/`, `build-box/` and `pico/n8-host/build/` hold the prototype's images and
  `build/` its pack bytecode: Tasks 3, 4 and 5 each rebuild the `bliptoaster` pack and the device check's image before
  they hash them (the check's image embeds the pack, so a stale one would prove nothing), Task 5 also rebuilds the
  box's two variants, and Task 6 rebuilds all of it from removed dirs.
- **A `-Wformat-truncation` warning** may print when `packages/native/plugin/PluginDSP.cpp` recompiles (line 176). It
  predates F1 (the baseline's tree has it) and is not a finding. F1 writes no native library code.
- The prototype branch `proto/f1-packages` is this plan's provenance, and no step reads it: every byte check is a blob
  hash, a tree hash or an image hash quoted in the step.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding. Four exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving; a predicted failure whose failing
  file, case or target is the one named but whose wording differs; a trap probe's quoted lines, whose object path and
  `(.text.startup.main+0x...)` offsets are this devcontainer's and this binutils' (the device scripts judge a probe by
  its own object and the two symbol names, `__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`, and that check is the pass criterion);
  and the figures the ground rules call derived (below). Never edit code, a test or a golden to make a step pass. In
  Tasks 1 to 5 each task's tree must equal its prototype commit, so a real defect found there is reported, not fixed; a
  fix belongs to a commit of its own after the plan.
- **Predicted figures, and how to treat them.** Almost every Expected line is quoted from a log or a report. A named
  few are predicted from the code, or from a report that measured the same thing, and the step says so where it
  happens: Task 1 Step 1's configure refusal (the report verified it by hand, no log holds the text), Task 2 Step 1's
  twelve `refused:` lines (the same twelve the log counts as allowed), Task 2's scratch-file refusal (the report
  verified it; the Expected names the message's shape, not its text), and every Task 6 leg with no `s5fv` line (the
  fresh clone, `pnpm check:boundaries` at the final tree, the `RP_PARITY_REQUIRE_TARGET` run, the CI view of the render
  baseline, `pnpm validate` and the Reaper suite). A predicted line that differs in *wording* while its exit status is
  the one predicted is recorded in the report and execution continues; a different exit status, a case count or a
  quoted figure stops it.
- **Track progress outside the committed plan:** never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does not
  show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning or error is
  a real finding to report, not a stale quote; no step below builds on Windows, and Task 6 states the owed Windows run.
  macOS and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either: `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and
  pushes to `main` only, so their first run is a dispatched run or a PR the user starts.

print `feature/modularize`, `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` must print `a085f3d6`, and `git status --short --untracked-files=all` must show
` m deps/sameboy` and nothing else, or that and the three untracked generated modules a prototype build may have
left (`packages/retroplug/src/generated/packages.ts`, `protocol.ts` and `scriptNodes.ts`, which are derived: Task 1
Step 7 deletes them). If the branch or the commit
differs, stop: every step below assumes the design commit on a tree with nothing else in it. (`git -C deps/sameboy

## File structure

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `package.json`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/packages.cmake` | the product list (both languages read it), the manifest's `app` and `protocol` members, a package with no native part, the registration loop and the deferred boundary check (Tasks 1, 2, 4, 5) |
| `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, `scripts/check-boundaries.mjs` | the generator (Task 1, widened in 3, 4, 5) and the TS boundary check (Task 2, widened in 3, 4, 5) |
| `packages/retroplug/src/generated/` | the three generated modules: gitignored, never committed, written by the generator (Task 1) |
| `packages/retroplug/src/` | the shell's app and protocol contributions, the registry doors (`appHost`, `romProviders`, `kitFormats`, `trackerRegistry`, `graph/protocolNodes`), and what no package owns (the stores, `backend`, `render/`, `buildGraph`/`directGraph`/`controller.ts`, `liveSav`, `kit/compile.ts`, the controller) |
| `packages/core/ts/` | the node mechanism, the document, the role contract, `constructSpec`, `platform`, `offlineJob`, `configFields`, the role's field builders, `runtime.d.ts`, the MIDI route node (Tasks 3, 4) |
| `packages/dsp/ts/` | the kit chain and pack, `kitEffect`, `kitContract` and the kit driver's chain half in `kitJobs` (Tasks 3, 5) |
| `packages/testing/` | the harness, the node rig, `bytes` and `deepEqual` (Tasks 3, 5) |
| `packages/{sameboy,mesen,tracker}/` | the two console packages' role kinds and enums (Task 4); the tracker layer's contracts, the neutral NES helpers and the `.rit` format (Task 4) |
| `packages/{lsdj,mgb,risa,smsggdj,bliptoaster,n8}/` | the six carts: their roles, ROM providers, catalogs, integrations, kit formats, protocol nodes, fixtures, tests and goldens (Task 5), `bliptoaster` widened beside its device script pack and `n8` widened beside its N8 pack |
| `tsconfig.base.json`, `packages/*/tsconfig.json`, `tools/ts-options.js` | the base program, one two-line tsconfig per package, and the bundlers' pinned TypeScript options (Tasks 3, 4) |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | the workspace's edges, one diff per task that changes a manifest's dependencies (Tasks 2, 3, 4, 5) |
| `packages/native/test/packages/`, `packages/retroplug/test/{packages,boundaries}/` | the configure fixtures (Tasks 1, 2) and the checker's and generator's own cases and fixture trees (Tasks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) |
| `docs/`, `spec/`, `AGENTS.md`, `packages/retroplug/README.md` | the design's as-built record and the live docs (Task 5), and the dead links each move repoints (Tasks 3, 4, 5) |

---

### Task 1: the product list, the manifests' app and protocol members, and the generator

Design sections 2, 3 and 8's first commit. The root `package.json` gains `retroplug.products.desktop`, the package
names a desktop product carries, in dependency order; the root `CMakeLists.txt` reads it into `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES` with
`string(JSON)` in place of the literal list (a member that is not a list, an empty list and an entry that is not a string
are each refused in words) and makes the file a configure input. `cmake/packages.cmake` accepts a manifest with `app`,
`protocol`, `native` or `script` (any combination), and a package with no native part registers nothing and adds no
target. The shell's manifest carries the two new members: `app` -> `src/app.ts`, `protocol` -> `src/script/shellNodes.ts`
with today's eight nodes and their labels 16 to 23. The generator,
`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, writes three gitignored modules from the list and the manifests, and the
five registry consumers read them while the contribution lists still live in the shell's own modules.

The shell's two contribution lists had to split before anything could read them: the generated module imports the
contribution modules, so a contribution module may not import the generated module (that would read an uninitialised
binding at module init). So the six ROM providers move to `src/romProviderList.ts` (their dispatcher stays
`src/romProviders.ts`, which eleven test files import), the four tracker integrations to `src/tracker/integrations.ts`
(their contract stays), and the generated registry's own reads move to two new shell modules, `src/kitFormats.ts` and
`src/trackerRegistry.ts`, because `src/kit` and `src/tracker` are directories Task 4 and Task 5 move.

The task is: the product list and the manifest's members, the generator, the shell's contributions, the consumers and
the tools that must generate first, the tests and fixtures, then the build (which generates the three modules from
nothing) and the suites. No target is built before Step 7, and only Step 1 configures before it, twice, to show the
product list's refusal: `build/bin` holds the prototype tip's binaries, and no test of this task exists in the tree yet,
so a red from them would prove nothing.

- [ ] **Step 2: The generator**

`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs` (one file, a shebang'd ES module) reads the root `package.json`'s
product list and each listed package's `package.json`, and writes the three modules into `src/generated` beside the
shell. It is the whole mechanism, so its rules are the task: - `readPackage` refuses a manifest whose `name` is not
`@retroplug/<directory>`, and a listed package with no manifest or no `retroplug` member; `unlistedContributes` reads
an unlisted dependency tolerantly (no manifest, or no member, contributes nothing). - `order` emits the list's order
exactly, then the shell (`SHELL`, one constant, derived in CMake from this file's own path), and refuses a listed
dependency that appears later than its dependent (which also refuses a cycle), a dependency on the shell, an unlisted
dependency that contributes (`app` or `protocol`), and a product list that names the shell. - `contributions` reads
each `app` module's four lists (by `exports`, not by path: `moduleSpecifier` resolves the manifest's file to the key
of its `exports` entry and refuses a file the package does not publish) and each `protocol` member's `module`, `nodes`
and `roles`; it refuses a node key no protocol node reads, a node with `midiIn` and no `writes` or the reverse, a
duplicate type, a duplicate label, a label below 16 or a gap, a role naming a type no package declares or one with no
wiring, and a role kind or kit format id two packages declare. - `renderPackages` writes `packages.ts` (the four lists
in order, the shell's last, and the three duplicate refusals in the module itself, since only the loaded module can
see a package's app lists); `renderProtocol` writes `protocol.ts` (keys in label order, importing only a type);
`renderScriptNodes` writes `scriptNodes.ts`, which sorts the concatenated nodes by the manifests' labels and refuses
at load unless the registered set is exactly the manifests' and the labels are `16 + i`. - Writes go through
`<file>.<pid>.<random>.tmp` and a rename (retried once, accepting identical content, for Windows), and a file whose
bytes would not change is not touched.

Create `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The TS package generator (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 3): from the product list and the packages'
// manifests, writes the three gitignored modules the shell builds against.
//
//   packages/retroplug/src/generated/packages.ts     the app's registrations, in product order (the list's, then the
//                                                    shell): the roles buildAppRegistry applies, the ROM providers, the
//                                                    tracker integrations and the kit formats
//   packages/retroplug/src/generated/protocol.ts     PROTOCOL_NODES and ROLE_NODES, the wiring buildGraph reads. It
//                                                    imports nothing but types, so a bundle of buildGraph carries the
//                                                    tables without a single node's code or role's schema
//   packages/retroplug/src/generated/scriptNodes.ts  the script-node bundle's entry, importing each package's node
//                                                    definitions and registering them in span-label order
//
// The product list is the root package.json's retroplug.products.desktop, the same array the root CMakeLists.txt reads
// into RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES (string(JSON)), so the two languages cannot register different products. THE LIST IS ALSO
// THE ORDER: CMake registers a package's native entries in it, and the app lists concatenate in it, so a package must
// be listed after every listed package it depends on. The generator refuses a list that breaks that (naming both
// packages) rather than sorting, because a sort here would put TS in one order and CMake in another.
//
// The shell is the one package name this script fixes rather than reads: packages/retroplug is the app itself, not a
// package a product lists (nothing calls retroplug_package(retroplug)), its own TS tree is where the generated modules
// live, and its manifest contributes the roles and protocol nodes no package owns yet. It closes the list, and no
// package may depend on it.
//
// A package's contributions are its manifest's retroplug.app (a module default-exporting definePackage's lists) and
// retroplug.protocol (its node definitions' module, the nodes' wiring and labels, and which role kind each is placed
// as). A @retroplug dependency the list does not carry is refused only when it contributes (its manifest has an app or
// protocol member), which would silently lose it; one that contributes nothing (a native library a package links, a
// pure TS library with no retroplug member) is left out of the ordering.
//
// It writes only a file whose content changed, so a build that changes nothing touches nothing (CMake and the test
// runners can call it before every bundle without churning mtimes). Run it by hand with:
//
//   node packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs [--root <dir>]
//
// --root names a tree laid out as this one is (a package.json with the same retroplug members, packages/<name>/
// package.json), which is how the generator's tests drive it over fixtures.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, renameSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = resolve(HERE, "../../../..");
// The profiler's span labels start at 16 (spec/08-profiling.md): 1 to 15 are the engine's own stages.
const FIRST_LABEL = 16;
// The shell, the app itself (see the header).
const SHELL = "retroplug";

/** The generated modules' directory inside the shell: src/generated, so a package's module is imported by a path
 *  relative to it and the shell's own contributions read as `../app`. */
const GENERATED = "src/generated";

function readJson(path) {
  let text;
  try {
    text = readFileSync(path, "utf8");
  } catch (e) {
    throw new Error(`${path} cannot be read (${e.code ?? e.message})`);
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch (e) {
    throw new Error(`${path} is not JSON (${e.message})`);
  }
}

function isObject(v) {
  return v !== null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);
}

// The protocol node fields the generated tables carry (renderProtocol's key list): anything else in a manifest's node
// entry is a knob nothing reads, which JSON cannot type-check and esbuild only warns about.
const NODE_KEYS = ["type", "label", "midiIn", "writes", "launches", "serialOut", "midiOut", "out"];

/** `@retroplug/<name>` for a dependency spec, or null for a third-party one. */
function packageOf(spec) {
  const m = /^@retroplug\/(.+)$/.exec(spec);
  return m ? m[1] : null;
}

// A file a manifest names, from the package's directory, refused by name when it is missing so a typo fails the
// generation rather than the bundler.
function entryFile(pkg, member, path) {
  const file = resolve(pkg.dir, path);
  if (!existsSync(file)) {
    throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: retroplug.${member} names ${path}, which does not exist (${file})`);
  }
  return file;
}

function readPackage(root, name) {
  const dir = join(root, "packages", name);
  const manifest = join(dir, "package.json");
  if (!existsSync(manifest)) throw new Error(`the package ${name} has no ${manifest}`);
  const json = readJson(manifest);
  if (!isObject(json.retroplug)) throw new Error(`${manifest} has no retroplug field`);
  return { name, dir, manifest, manifestJson: json, retroplug: json.retroplug };
}

/** Whether a package contributes to the app: its manifest has an `app` or a `protocol` member. */
function contributes(pkg) {
  return pkg.retroplug.app !== undefined || pkg.retroplug.protocol !== undefined;
}

/** Whether an unlisted dependency contributes to the app, judged tolerantly: a package with no manifest, or a manifest
 *  with no retroplug member (a pure TS library a package's tests use), contributes nothing, so it is no product's
 *  business and the generator has no reason to refuse it. */
function unlistedContributes(root, name) {
  const manifest = join(root, "packages", name, "package.json");
  if (!existsSync(manifest)) return false;
  const json = readJson(manifest);
  return isObject(json.retroplug) && contributes({ retroplug: json.retroplug });
}

/** The product's packages, in the list's order with the shell last. A listed package's declared @retroplug
 *  dependencies are read to hold two rules: a dependency the list does not carry is refused when it would contribute
 *  to the app (the product would lose it), and a dependency listed after the package that needs it is refused (the TS
 *  and CMake orders would disagree). Both messages name the pair. */
function order(root, names) {
  const packages = names.map((name) => readPackage(root, name));
  // The shell closes the list: it is not a package a product carries, and no package may depend on it.
  packages.push(readPackage(root, SHELL));
  const listed = new Set(names);

  for (const pkg of packages) {
    const declared = isObject(pkg.manifestJson.dependencies) ? Object.keys(pkg.manifestJson.dependencies) : [];
    const at = names.indexOf(pkg.name);
    for (const spec of declared) {
      const dep = packageOf(spec);
      if (dep === null || !listed.has(dep)) {
        if (dep === null) continue;
        // The shell is not a product's, and nothing may depend on it whatever it contributes: its own rule, so the
        // message names the rule rather than the list.
        if (dep === SHELL) {
          throw new Error(`${pkg.name} depends on the shell (@retroplug/${SHELL}); no package may`);
        }
        // Not the product's: only a package whose contribution the product would drop is refused.
        if (unlistedContributes(root, dep)) {
          throw new Error(
            `${pkg.name} depends on @retroplug/${dep}, which contributes to the app and the product does not list`,
          );
        }
        continue;
      }
      // The shell is not in the list (it closes it), so its own dependencies have no position to hold; every other
      // package must follow the dependency it names.
      if (at !== -1 && names.indexOf(dep) > at) {
        throw new Error(
          `the product lists ${pkg.name} before @retroplug/${dep}, which it depends on: a package must follow its ` +
            "dependencies",
        );
      }
    }
  }

  return packages;
}

/** What one package contributes, from its manifest: its app module and its protocol nodes, each checked for what the
 *  generated modules need. */
function contributions(pkg) {
  const out = { app: null, protocol: null, nodes: [], roles: {} };
  const retroplug = pkg.retroplug;
  if (retroplug.app !== undefined) {
    if (typeof retroplug.app !== "string" || retroplug.app === "") {
      throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: retroplug.app must be a module path, not ${JSON.stringify(retroplug.app)}`);
    }
    out.app = entryFile(pkg, "app", retroplug.app);
  }
  if (retroplug.protocol === undefined) return out;
  const protocol = retroplug.protocol;
  if (!isObject(protocol)) throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: retroplug.protocol is not an object`);
  if (typeof protocol.module !== "string" || protocol.module === "") {
    throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: retroplug.protocol needs a "module", the file that default-exports its nodes`);
  }
  out.protocol = entryFile(pkg, "protocol's module", protocol.module);
  const nodes = protocol.nodes ?? [];
  if (!Array.isArray(nodes)) throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: retroplug.protocol.nodes is not a list`);
  for (const node of nodes) {
    if (!isObject(node) || typeof node.type !== "string" || node.type === "") {
      throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: every retroplug.protocol.nodes entry needs a "type", the node's id`);
    }
    if (!Number.isInteger(node.label)) {
      throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: the node ${node.type} needs a "label", a whole number (its span label)`);
    }
    for (const key of Object.keys(node)) {
      if (!NODE_KEYS.includes(key)) {
        throw new Error(
          `${pkg.name}: the node ${node.type} has ${JSON.stringify(key)}, which no protocol node reads ` +
            `(a node's keys are ${NODE_KEYS.join(", ")})`,
        );
      }
    }
    if (node.writes !== undefined && !Array.isArray(node.writes)) {
      throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: the node ${node.type}'s writes is not a list`);
    }
    // Wired or not is one decision: renderProtocol emits a node into PROTOCOL_NODES on either field, so a node with
    // one and not the other would be placed with a hole (a MIDI route into no input, or an input nothing routes to)
    // that only tsc's `satisfies` would see, and esbuild builds through that.
    const midiIn = Object.hasOwn(node, "midiIn");
    const writes = Object.hasOwn(node, "writes");
    if (midiIn !== writes) {
      throw new Error(
        `${pkg.name}: the node ${node.type} declares ${midiIn ? "midiIn" : "writes"} without ` +
          `${midiIn ? "writes" : "midiIn"}: a wired node declares both (an unwired one neither)`,
      );
    }
    out.nodes.push(node);
  }
  out.roles = protocol.roles ?? {};
  if (!isObject(out.roles)) throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: retroplug.protocol.roles is not an object`);
  for (const [kind, type] of Object.entries(out.roles)) {
    if (typeof type !== "string") throw new Error(`${pkg.name}: the role ${kind} does not name a node type`);
  }
  return out;
}

/** Every package's nodes as one table, with the labels the manifests fix: a type declared twice, a label used twice, a
 *  label below 16 or a gap in the labels is refused here, so the bundle cannot register the wrong type under a label
 *  (spec/08-profiling.md) or leave a hole one would inherit. */
function nodeTable(packages) {
  const byType = new Map();
  const byLabel = new Map();
  for (const { pkg, nodes } of packages) {
    for (const node of nodes) {
      const at = byType.get(node.type);
      if (at) throw new Error(`two packages declare the script node ${node.type}: ${at.pkg} and ${pkg.name}`);
      byType.set(node.type, { node, pkg: pkg.name });
      const holder = byLabel.get(node.label);
      if (holder) {
        throw new Error(
          `two script nodes have the span label ${node.label}: ${holder.node.type} (${holder.pkg}) and ` +
            `${node.type} (${pkg.name})`,
        );
      }
      byLabel.set(node.label, { node, pkg: pkg.name });
    }
  }
  const labels = [...byLabel.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const gap = (why) => {
    throw new Error(
      `the script nodes' span labels must run from ${FIRST_LABEL} with no gap: ${labels.join(", ")} (${why})`,
    );
  };
  if (labels.length && labels[0] !== FIRST_LABEL) {
    gap(labels[0] < FIRST_LABEL ? `${labels[0]} is below ${FIRST_LABEL}` : `${FIRST_LABEL} is missing`);
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
    // Duplicates are refused above, so a label out of place here is one the list skipped over.
    if (labels[i] !== FIRST_LABEL + i) gap(`${FIRST_LABEL + i} is missing`);
  }
  return { byType };
}

/** The role kinds the protocol members declare, each with its node type and the package that declares it: a kind has
 *  one owner, as a node type and a span label do, since the generated ROLE_NODES object would otherwise keep whichever
 *  package came last (or fail tsc, and esbuild only warns). */
function roleTable(packages) {
  const kinds = new Map();
  for (const { pkg, roles } of packages) {
    for (const [kind, type] of Object.entries(roles)) {
      const at = kinds.get(kind);
      if (at) throw new Error(`two packages declare the role kind ${kind}: ${at.pkg} and ${pkg.name}`);
      kinds.set(kind, { kind, type, pkg: pkg.name });
    }
  }
  return kinds;
}

// A module path as the generated file imports it: relative, POSIX separators, no .ts (the bundler and tsc resolve it).
function specifier(fromDir, file) {
  let spec = relative(fromDir, file).replace(/\\/g, "/").replace(/\.ts$/, "");
  if (!spec.startsWith(".")) spec = `./${spec}`;
  return spec;
}

// A package name as an import identifier: graph-runtime -> app_graph_runtime.
function identifier(name) {
  return `app_${name.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_]/g, "_")}`;
}

function contributionLines(packages, member) {
  return packages.filter((p) => p.app).map((p) => `  ...(${identifier(p.pkg.name)}.${member} ?? []),`);
}

function renderPackages({ packages, outDir }) {
  const app = packages.filter((p) => p.app);
  const lines = [];
  lines.push(
    "// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list (the root",
    "// package.json's retroplug.products.desktop) and the packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and",
    "// rebuild.",
    "//",
    "// The app's registrations, in product order (the list's, which is a dependency order, then the shell): the roles",
    "// buildAppRegistry applies, the ROM providers it offers, the tracker integrations the Songs and Assets menus",
    "// search, and the kit formats the audio driver dispatches to. The protocol tables buildGraph reads are apart, in",
    "// ./protocol.ts, so a module that needs them imports no package's app.",
    'import type { RoleType, RomProvider } from "../systemRoles";',
    'import type { TrackerIntegration } from "../tracker/trackerIntegration";',
    'import type { KitFormat } from "../kit/compile";',
  );
  for (const p of app) lines.push(`import ${identifier(p.pkg.name)} from "${specifier(outDir, p.app)}";`);
  lines.push(
    "",
    "/** The app's roles, in product order: the role contract's objects, which the registry holds. */",
    "export const ROLES: readonly RoleType[] = [",
    ...contributionLines(app, "roles"),
    "];",
    "",
    "/** The ROM providers, in product order: a ROM's feature roles are attached by the first matches' order. */",
    "export const ROM_PROVIDERS: readonly RomProvider[] = [",
    ...contributionLines(app, "romProviders"),
    "];",
    "",
    "/** The tracker integrations, in product order: a system takes the first whose markerRole it has. */",
    "export const TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS: readonly TrackerIntegration[] = [",
    ...contributionLines(app, "trackerIntegrations"),
    "];",
    "",
    "/** The kit bank formats, by the id the audio driver dispatches with. */",
    "export const KIT_FORMATS: readonly KitFormat<any>[] = [",
    ...contributionLines(app, "kitFormats"),
    "];",
    "",
  );
  return lines.join("\n");
}

function renderProtocol({ byType, roles }) {
  const lines = [];
  lines.push(
    "// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the",
    "// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.",
    "//",
    "// The protocol tables buildGraph, the stores and a DirectGraph wire a system's roles through, as the manifests",
    "// spell them. Nothing but a type is imported here: the data is apart from the node modules it describes, so a",
    "// bundle that reads it carries no node's code, no role's schema and nothing of the app.",
    'import type { ProtocolNodeSpec } from "../graph/protocolNodes";',
    "",
    "/** How buildGraph and the stores wire each protocol node type (graph/protocolNodes.ts's ProtocolNodeSpec): the",
    " *  input its system's routed MIDI arrives on, the system inputs it writes, and the wires it takes or makes. In",
    " *  span-label order, so which package declares a node changes nothing here. */",
  );
  const specs = [...byType.values()].sort((a, b) => a.node.label - b.node.label);
  const wired = specs.filter(({ node }) => node.midiIn !== undefined || node.writes !== undefined);
  if (!wired.length) {
    lines.push("export const PROTOCOL_NODES = {} as const satisfies Record<string, ProtocolNodeSpec>;");
  } else {
    lines.push("export const PROTOCOL_NODES = {");
    for (const { node } of wired) {
      const fields = [];
      for (const key of ["midiIn", "writes", "launches", "serialOut", "midiOut", "out"]) {
        if (node[key] === undefined) continue;
        const value = Array.isArray(node[key])
          ? `[${node[key].map((v) => JSON.stringify(v)).join(", ")}]`
          : JSON.stringify(node[key]);
        fields.push(`${key}: ${value}`);
      }
      lines.push(`  ${JSON.stringify(node.type)}: { ${fields.join(", ")} },`);
    }
    lines.push("} as const satisfies Record<string, ProtocolNodeSpec>;");
  }
  lines.push(
    "",
    "/** The role kinds that have a protocol node, each with the type it is placed as (the ids PROTOCOL_NODES wires),",
    " *  in the order of the labels they are placed at. */",
    "export const ROLE_NODES: Readonly<Record<string, keyof typeof PROTOCOL_NODES>> = {",
  );
  for (const { kind, type } of roles) lines.push(`  ${JSON.stringify(kind)}: ${JSON.stringify(type)},`);
  lines.push("};", "");
  return lines.join("\n");
}

function renderScriptNodes({ packages, outDir }) {
  const spec = packages.filter((p) => p.protocol);
  const head = [
    "// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the",
    "// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.",
    "//",
    "// The script-node bundle's entry: every package's protocol node definitions, registered in span-label order",
    "// (spec/08-profiling.md: one label a type, 16 up), which the manifests' retroplug.protocol.nodes fix whatever",
    "// order a package lists its exports in. esbuilt to a global-code IIFE, compiled to QuickJS bytecode and",
    "// embedded in the backend (packages/native/cmake/bundles.cmake), so every Engine loads it into both of its",
    "// script contexts.",
  ];
  if (!spec.length) {
    return [
      ...head,
      'import { registerScriptNodes } from "../script/register";',
      "",
      "// No package in the desktop product contributes a protocol node.",
      "registerScriptNodes([]);",
      "",
    ].join("\n");
  }
  const lines = [
    ...head,
    'import type { DefinedNode } from "../graph/defineNode";',
    'import { registerScriptNodes } from "../script/register";',
  ];
  for (const p of spec) {
    const id = identifier(p.pkg.name).slice(4);
    lines.push(`import nodes_${id} from "${specifier(outDir, p.protocol)}";`);
  }
  lines.push(
    "",
    "// The host numbers the nodes it is handed from the first protocol span label up (spec/08-profiling.md).",
    `const FIRST_LABEL = ${FIRST_LABEL};`,
    "",
    "// The span label of each node type the product's manifests declare.",
    "const LABELS: Readonly<Record<string, number | undefined>> = {",
  );
  for (const p of spec) for (const node of p.nodes) lines.push(`  ${JSON.stringify(node.type)}: ${node.label},`);
  lines.push(
    "};",
    "",
    "function labelOf(node: DefinedNode<any>): number {",
    "  const label = LABELS[node.id];",
    "  if (label === undefined) {",
    "    throw new Error(`the script node ${node.id} has no span label (a package's retroplug.protocol.nodes)`);",
    "  }",
    "  return label;",
    "}",
    "",
    "// Each package's definitions, in product order; the order the bundle registers them in is the labels', below.",
    "const lists: readonly (readonly DefinedNode<any>[])[] = [",
  );
  for (const p of spec) lines.push(`  nodes_${identifier(p.pkg.name).slice(4)},`);
  lines.push(
    "];",
    "",
    "const nodes: DefinedNode<any>[] = [];",
    "for (const list of lists) for (const node of list) nodes.push(node);",
    "nodes.sort((a, b) => labelOf(a) - labelOf(b));",
    "",
    "// A label is not a node's own: the host numbers what it is handed, in order (ScriptHost's spanLabelFor), so a",
    "// manifest node its module does not export would shift every later type one label down, and a node no manifest",
    "// declares would take the label of one that is missing. Refuse the bundle unless what the modules define is",
    "// exactly the manifests' declarations, each at its own label.",
    "const declared = Object.keys(LABELS);",
    "const missing = declared.filter((type) => !nodes.some((node) => node.id === type));",
    "const extra = nodes.filter((node) => LABELS[node.id] === undefined).map((node) => node.id);",
    "if (missing.length || extra.length) {",
    "  throw new Error(",
    "    `the script bundle's nodes are not the manifests': ${nodes.length} defined, ${declared.length} declared; ` +",
    "      (missing.length",
    "        ? `${missing.join(\", \")} has no definition`",
    "        : `${extra.join(\", \")} is declared by no manifest`),",
    "  );",
    "}",
    "for (let i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) {",
    "  if (labelOf(nodes[i]) !== FIRST_LABEL + i) {",
    "    throw new Error(",
    "      `the script node ${nodes[i].id} would take the span label ${FIRST_LABEL + i}, ` +",
    "        `not its ${labelOf(nodes[i])}`,",
    "    );",
    "  }",
    "}",
    "registerScriptNodes(nodes);",
    "",
  );
  return lines.join("\n");
}

// One file's content, written only when it differs from what is there: through a per-run temporary name (two
// generators can run at once: two build trees, or `pnpm test` beside `pnpm test:native`) and a rename.
function writeIfChanged(path, content, stamp) {
  let current = null;
  try {
    current = readFileSync(path, "utf8");
  } catch {
    // no file yet
  }
  if (current === content) return false;
  const temporary = `${path}.${process.pid}.${stamp}.tmp`;
  writeFileSync(temporary, content);
  try {
    renameSync(temporary, path);
  } catch (e) {
    // Windows refuses a rename onto a file another process holds open, which is the other generator of a parallel
    // run: when it has already written these bytes, this one's copy is spent; otherwise try the rename once more.
    let same = false;
    try {
      same = readFileSync(path, "utf8") === content;
    } catch {
      // the file is gone, so the rename is worth another try
    }
    if (same) rmSync(temporary, { force: true });
    else renameSync(temporary, path);
  }
  return true;
}

/** Generate the three modules under `<root>/packages/<shell>/src/generated`. Returns the ordered package names and, for
 *  each file, whether it was written (it is not, when its content is unchanged). */
export function generate({ root = REPO } = {}) {
  const manifestPath = join(root, "package.json");
  const manifest = readJson(manifestPath);
  const retroplug = isObject(manifest.retroplug) ? manifest.retroplug : {};
  const products = isObject(retroplug.products) ? retroplug.products : {};
  const names = products.desktop;
  if (!Array.isArray(names) || !names.length) {
    throw new Error(`${manifestPath} has no retroplug.products.desktop list of package names`);
  }
  if (names.some((name) => typeof name !== "string" || name === "")) {
    throw new Error(`${manifestPath} lists a package name that is not a name in retroplug.products.desktop`);
  }
  if (new Set(names).size !== names.length) {
    throw new Error(`${manifestPath} lists a package twice in retroplug.products.desktop`);
  }
  if (names.includes(SHELL)) {
    throw new Error(`${manifestPath} lists the shell (${SHELL}) in retroplug.products.desktop`);
  }

  const ordered = order(root, names);
  const shell = ordered[ordered.length - 1];
  const outDir = join(shell.dir, GENERATED);
  const contributionsOf = ordered.map((pkg) => ({ pkg, ...contributions(pkg) }));
  const { byType } = nodeTable(contributionsOf);
  const kinds = roleTable(contributionsOf);

  // A role's node must be one PROTOCOL_NODES wires, or buildGraph would place a node it cannot lay out.
  for (const { kind, type, pkg } of kinds.values()) {
    if (!byType.has(type)) throw new Error(`${pkg}: the role ${kind} names ${type}, which no package declares`);
    if (!wiresNode(type, byType)) {
      throw new Error(`${pkg}: the role ${kind} names ${type}, which declares no midiIn and writes to wire it`);
    }
  }
  const roles = [...kinds.values()]
    .map((role) => ({ ...role, label: byType.get(role.type).node.label }))
    .sort((a, b) => a.label - b.label || (a.kind < b.kind ? -1 : a.kind > b.kind ? 1 : 0));

  const files = [
    { path: join(outDir, "packages.ts"), content: renderPackages({ packages: contributionsOf, outDir }) },
    { path: join(outDir, "protocol.ts"), content: renderProtocol({ byType, roles }) },
    { path: join(outDir, "scriptNodes.ts"), content: renderScriptNodes({ packages: contributionsOf, outDir }) },
  ];
  mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
  const stamp = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10);
  const written = files.map((file) => ({ path: file.path, changed: writeIfChanged(file.path, file.content, stamp) }));
  return { packages: ordered.map((p) => p.name), files: written };
}

// Whether `type` is a node type PROTOCOL_NODES wires: a role is placed as one, so its manifest entry carries its
// midiIn and writes.
function wiresNode(type, byType) {
  const entry = byType.get(type);
  return entry !== undefined && (entry.node.midiIn !== undefined || entry.node.writes !== undefined);
}

if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const at = process.argv.indexOf("--root");
  const root = at === -1 ? REPO : resolve(process.argv[at + 1] ?? "");
  try {
    generate({ root });
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`packages.mjs: ${e.message}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
````

// The shell's own app contribution, its package.json's retroplug.app: the lists the app hardcoded in appHost.ts,
// romProviders.ts, tracker/trackerIntegration.ts and kit/compile.ts until the generated registry
// (src/generated/packages.ts) concatenated every package's. The shell carries what no package owns yet, in the order
// the app registered it; a package that grows an app module contributes its own list from there.
import { definePackage } from "./core/definePackage";
import { CORE_ROLES } from "./coreRoles";
import { DSP_ROLES } from "./dspRoles";
import { LSDJ_ASSETS_ROLE } from "./lsdjAssetsRole";
import { RISA_ROLE } from "./risaRole";
import { RISA_ASSETS_ROLE } from "./risaAssetsRole";
import { BLIPTOASTER_ROLE } from "./bliptoasterRole";
import { BLIPTOASTER_ASSETS_ROLE } from "./bliptoasterAssetsRole";
import {
  BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PROVIDER,
  LSDJ_ROM_PROVIDER,
  MGB_ROM_PROVIDER,
  NES_ROM_PROVIDER,
  RISA_ROM_PROVIDER,
  SMSGGDJ_ROM_PROVIDER,
} from "./romProviderList";
import { blipToasterIntegration, lsdjIntegration, risaIntegration, smsggdjIntegration } from "./tracker/integrations";
import { LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT, RISA_KIT_FORMAT } from "./kit/compile";
// The keys the owner packages add to the contract (their modules augment PackageContributions): type-only, so nothing
// loads at run time.
import type {} from "./tracker/packageContributions";
import type {} from "./kit/packageContributions";

export default definePackage({
  // The backend "system" roles (coreRoles), the feature roles that have a protocol node (dspRoles), and those that
  // have none (asset overrides, a ROM's facts), in the order buildAppRegistry registered them.
  roles: [
    ...CORE_ROLES,
    ...DSP_ROLES,
    LSDJ_ASSETS_ROLE,
    RISA_ROLE,
    RISA_ASSETS_ROLE,
    BLIPTOASTER_ROLE,
    BLIPTOASTER_ASSETS_ROLE,
  ],
  // The providers attach a ROM's feature roles by its identity, in the order the registry offers them.
  romProviders: [
    MGB_ROM_PROVIDER,
    LSDJ_ROM_PROVIDER,
    NES_ROM_PROVIDER,
    SMSGGDJ_ROM_PROVIDER,
    RISA_ROM_PROVIDER,
    BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PROVIDER,
  ],
  // The Songs and Assets menus' consoles, in the order they are searched (a system's first match wins).
  trackerIntegrations: [lsdjIntegration, risaIntegration, smsggdjIntegration, blipToasterIntegration],
  // The kit bank compilers the audio driver dispatches to by id.
  kitFormats: [LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT, RISA_KIT_FORMAT],
});

````ts
// The app-contribution contract a package's `app` module default-exports (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md
// section 3): the pure registrations a package adds to the app, as lists rather than as calls into a registry. Every
// list is optional, and a list's order is the order its contributions register in, so the shell's registry, the ROM
// sniffer, the Songs menu and the kit compiler see the same sequence whatever package they came from.
//
// What this file declares is the part core owns: the lists whose types core knows (a role, a ROM provider). A package
// that owns another kind augments PackageContributions from its own module, so core imports nothing above itself - the
// tracker its trackerIntegrations (src/tracker/packageContributions.ts), dsp its kitFormats
// (src/kit/packageContributions.ts). Those two files move with their packages to
// packages/tracker/ts/packageContributions.ts and packages/dsp/ts/packageContributions.ts, and this file to
// packages/core/ts/definePackage.ts, where its imports come from core's own role contract.
//
// definePackage holds no registry and does nothing at run time: it is the identity function with types, so a package
// states its contributions where they are defined and the generated registry (src/generated/packages.ts) only has to
// concatenate them in product order. It is deliberately not generic: a type parameter inferred from the literal would
// swallow a misspelt key, where the parameter's own type refuses it (test/packages/define-package.test.ts).
import type { RoleType, RomProvider } from "../systemRoles";

/** A package's contributions as core knows them: the role contract's objects and the ROM providers. */
export interface PackageContributions {
  readonly roles?: readonly RoleType[];
  readonly romProviders?: readonly RomProvider[];
}

/** The identity function with types: an app module's default export, checked against what a package may contribute. */
export function definePackage(contributions: PackageContributions): PackageContributions {
  return contributions;
}
````

````ts
// The tracker integrations themselves, one per console: the catalogs, detectors and layouts a cart's Songs and Assets
// menus are built over, as the pure list the app's contributions carry (app.ts). trackerIntegration.ts holds the
// contract and resolves a system's roles through this list; the objects are here rather than there so the generated
// registry can import them without the module that reads it (src/generated/packages.ts).
import type { TrackerIntegration, RamWrite } from "./trackerIntegration";
import { lsdjSongCatalog } from "./lsdjSongCatalog";
import { risaSongCatalog } from "./risaSongCatalog";
import { lsdjAssetCatalog } from "./lsdjAssetCatalog";
import { risaAssetCatalog } from "./risaAssetCatalog";
import { smsggdjSongCatalog } from "./smsggdjSongCatalog";
import { smsggdjAssetCatalog } from "./smsggdjAssetCatalog";
import { identifySmsggdjVersion } from "../smsggdj/romDetect";
import { resolveSmsggdjLayout } from "../smsggdj/runtime/layout";
import type { SmsggdjLayout } from "../smsggdj/runtime/types";
import {
  readSongBlock,
  readSongName,
  readSongEcho,
  sanitizeEcho,
  songLengthRows,
  isGrooveEmpty,
  GLIDE_GROOVE_SEL,
} from "../smsggdj/codec/sav";
import { bliptoasterAssetCatalog } from "./bliptoasterAssetCatalog";
import { blipToasterInfo, BLIPTOASTER_MARKER } from "../bliptoaster/romDetect";
import { identifyLsdj } from "../lsdj/runtime/identify";
import { identifyRisaVersion } from "../risa/runtime/identify";
import { resolveRisaLayout } from "../risa/runtime/layout";

export const lsdjIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "lsdj",
  label: "LSDj",
  markerRole: "lsdj-sync",
  songs: lsdjSongCatalog,
  assets: lsdjAssetCatalog,
  romName: (rom) => {
    const v = identifyLsdj(rom); // parses the GB cartridge title at 0x134 ("LSDJ-Vx.y.z")
    return v ? `LSDj v${v.major}.${v.minor}.${v.patchLabel}${v.build ? ` ${v.build}` : ""}` : null;
  },
};

export const risaIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "risa",
  label: "Risa",
  markerRole: "risa",
  songs: risaSongCatalog,
  assets: risaAssetCatalog,
  romName: (rom) => {
    const v = identifyRisaVersion(rom); // scans the PRG for the ASCII "RISA V<major>.<minor>.<patch>" marker
    return v ? `risa v${v}` : null;
  },
  // Only versions with a bundled RAM layout (2.2.0 / 2.2.1 / 2.3.0) are driveable; an unknown / unmarked
  // version resolves no layout. See supportedRisaVersions() in ../risa/runtime/layout.
  isVersionSupported: (rom) => resolveRisaLayout(identifyRisaVersion(rom)) !== null,
};

/** The writes that put a song block (and the metadata SMDJ4 keeps beside it) into a running smsggdj -
 *  shared by a Load (from a slot) and a reset's carry (from an image). The block alone is not enough:
 *  SMDJ4 keeps the NAME and the ECHO settings in the directory entry (src/rle.asm:34 - "metadata, not in
 *  the block"), and echo is audible, so loading without it would play the new song through the old
 *  song's delay taps. `edited` is what `song_edited` should read afterwards. */
function songWrites(
  layout: SmsggdjLayout,
  block: Uint8Array,
  name: Uint8Array | null,
  echo: Uint8Array | null,
  edited: boolean,
  ram?: Uint8Array,
): RamWrite[] {
  const writes: RamWrite[] = [{ offset: layout.song, bytes: block }];
  if (name) writes.push({ offset: layout.name, bytes: name.subarray(0, layout.nameLen) });
  // Sanitized as the cart's PROJECT-screen load does (`song_load` runs echo_sanitize; its FILES-screen
  // load does not), so a corrupt or foreign directory entry cannot put an out-of-range echo mode or a
  // zero delay tap into the live engine. Slot matching compares echo sanitized, so this costs nothing.
  if (echo) writes.push({ offset: layout.echo, bytes: sanitizeEcho(echo.subarray(0, layout.echoLen)) });
  writes.push({ offset: layout.edited, bytes: Uint8Array.of(edited ? 1 : 0) });
  // `prj_slot` is deliberately NOT written. The cart's own load READS it (you move the PROJECT cursor
  // to a slot, then press LOAD) rather than writing it, and its legacy meaning is a 6-slot SMDJ3 index
  // that the PROJECT screen may still clamp - so pointing it at a directory index up to 31 risks a
  // confused UI for no real gain. It stays in the layout because it costs nothing to know.

  // --- the cart's `load_rebase`, for a load that lands while the transport is RUNNING --------------
  // load_rebase opens with `ret z` on play_state, so a load made while stopped needs none of this and
  // gets none of it. While playing, the engine is caching state derived from the OLD song, and leaving
  // it is not a passing glitch: eng_len is the wrap point, so the sequencer would loop at the previous
  // song's length forever. Three effects are reproduced; the fourth, load_carry_post's CONT beat-carry
  // (which replants the carried phrase in the reserved slots), is NOT - that is a musical feature of
  // the cart's own CONT load, and synthesizing it from out here would be re-implementing the tracker.
  if (ram && ram.length > layout.playState && ram[layout.playState] !== 0) {
    writes.push({ offset: layout.engLen, bytes: Uint8Array.of(songLengthRows(block)) });
    // Queued LIVE cells address the old song's grid, and a pending chain-end stop would fire against
    // the carried chain.
    writes.push({ offset: layout.liveQ, bytes: new Uint8Array(layout.liveQLen).fill(0xff) });
    // An empty groove gives the clock nothing to advance on, so the cart falls back to groove 0. The
    // cart asks through `groove_base`, which resolves the glide sentinel to `glide_scratch` in work
    // RAM - so mid-glide the question is about RAM the load leaves alone. Asked of the block instead,
    // groove 16 starts exactly at the block's end, read as "empty", and EVERY mid-glide load aborted it.
    const sel = ram[layout.grooveSel];
    // Any other value is a block groove, and `groove_base` indexes it as `sel * 16` in 8 bits - so a stray
    // sel above 16 wraps to groove `sel & 15` there, and here.
    const empty = sel === GLIDE_GROOVE_SEL ? ram[layout.glideScratch] === 0 : isGrooveEmpty(block, sel & 0x0f);
    if (empty) {
      writes.push({ offset: layout.grooveSel, bytes: Uint8Array.of(0) });
      writes.push({ offset: layout.groovePos, bytes: Uint8Array.of(0) });
    }
  }

  // --- and repaint, which unlike load_rebase is needed whether or not the transport is running -----
  // The cart only redraws rows flagged in `dirty_rows`, and every one of its OWN load paths ends in
  // `mark_all_dirty` (fpx_close, cont_load_fire). Writing the song without this loads it correctly and
  // leaves the PREVIOUS song on screen: the notes change, the display does not, until the user nudges
  // something. Measured before the fix - a load moved exactly 0 of 48,903 non-animating pixels.
  // `mark_all_dirty` is literally "1 into all 16 flags", so reproducing it is one write.
  writes.push({ offset: layout.dirtyRows, bytes: new Uint8Array(layout.dirtyRowsLen).fill(1) });
  writes.push({ offset: layout.labelDirty, bytes: Uint8Array.of(1) });
  return writes;
}

export const smsggdjIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "smsggdj",
  label: "SMSGGDJ",
  markerRole: "sms-sync", // overloaded as the menu gate, as LSDj overloads lsdj-sync
  songs: smsggdjSongCatalog,
  assets: smsggdjAssetCatalog, // empty for now; the ROM-asset half is its own slice
  romName: (rom) => {
    const v = identifySmsggdjVersion(rom); // scans for the version string near the SMSGGDJ marker
    return v ? `smsggdj v${v}` : null;
  },
  // Supported = we have this build's work-RAM layout, exactly as risa gates on a bundled symbol
  // snapshot. NOT whether the CART restores a song at boot (cur_slot), which is the ROM's own concern
  // and only one of several ways to load. Gating the whole submenu on that greyed out
  // Export / Replace / Delete / Move / Add / Import too, none of which need the cart's help at all.
  // An unknown build still greys out - the failure mode is unchanged, only the question is right now.
  isVersionSupported: (rom) => resolveSmsggdjLayout(identifySmsggdjVersion(rom)) !== null,

  // This cart's working song is work RAM, so a load is a poke rather than a byte transform on the sav -
  // and more than the block (see songWrites).
  liveLoad: (rom, sav, index, ram) => {
    const layout = resolveSmsggdjLayout(identifySmsggdjVersion(rom));
    if (!layout) return null;
    const block = readSongBlock(sav, index); // null on a free slot / bad checksum / malformed stream
    if (!block) return null;
    // The cart clears `song_edited` on its own load ("loaded block matches the slot: clean"), and leaving
    // it set would tell the cart the freshly loaded song has unsaved edits.
    return songWrites(layout, block, readSongName(sav, index), readSongEcho(sav, index), false, ram);
  },

  restoreWorkingSong: (rom, song, ram) => {
    const layout = resolveSmsggdjLayout(identifySmsggdjVersion(rom));
    return layout ? songWrites(layout, song.block, song.name, song.echo, song.edited, ram) : null;
  },
};

// BlipToaster: an NES MIDI synth (not a tracker), so it has NO song battery: only ROM assets (a baked DMC kit
// + the CHR font). An asset-only integration: `songs` is omitted, so only the asset submenus are built.
export const blipToasterIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "bliptoaster",
  label: "BlipToaster",
  markerRole: "bliptoaster",
  assets: bliptoasterAssetCatalog,
  romName: (rom) => {
    const info = blipToasterInfo(rom); // decoded bliptoaster SIG block (null when the marker is absent)
    if (!info) return null;
    return `${BLIPTOASTER_MARKER} v${info.semver.join(".")}`; // marker doubles as the display name
  },
};
````

import type { DefinedNode } from "../graph/defineNode";

// (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md section 2), and LSDj's serial-out decoder, which buildGraph places after
// the systems (docs/lsdj-serial-out-design.md). Nothing here registers roles or imports zod: a node's settings are
