````ts
// The built-in ROM providers: the TS replacement for the deleted C++ RomSniffer's default-role step. Given a
// freshly-classified ROM, they attach the FEATURE roles that give it behaviour - mGB gets the `mgb` MIDI-to-serial
// passthrough, LSDj gets `lsdj-sync`. Registered into the CONTROL-PLANE registry only by registerRomProviders
// (romProviders.ts), which buildAppRegistry calls; the bare DSP-context bundle never sees them. Feature roles are
// matched by ROM identity (cartridge title at 0x134, or the embedded marker for a baked-in synth whose bytes never
// reach TS) - the same "meaning lives in TS" split the generic RoleRegistry is built around.
//
// The list is the shell's app contribution (app.ts), so the generated registry holds it in product order and a
// package that brings its own console registers it there rather than here.
import type { RoleInstance, RomProvider } from "./systemRoles";
import { LsdjSyncMode } from "./settingsEnums";
import { isRisaRomHeader, isRisaSyncRom } from "./risa";
import { isBlipToasterRomHeader, blipToasterChip } from "./bliptoaster/romDetect";
import { isSmsggdjRom } from "./smsSync";

// The Game Boy cartridge title field is 0x134..0x143. Decode it to an uppercase ASCII
// string, stopping at the first NUL - case-insensitive so both "LSDj-v9.4.2" and older
// "LSDJ" uppercase titles match the same prefix.
function title(header: Uint8Array): string {
  let s = "";
  for (let i = 0x134; i < 0x144 && i < header.length; i++) {
    const c = header[i];
    if (c === 0) break;
    s += String.fromCharCode(c);
  }
  return s.toUpperCase();
}

// mGB: the embedded synth (marker "mgb") or a file-backed mGB cart -> MIDI-to-serial passthrough.
export const MGB_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) =>
  rom.embeddedRom === "mgb" || title(rom.header).startsWith("MGB") ? [{ kind: "mgb", config: {} }] : [];

// LSDj (stock or arduinoboy build) -> the lsdj-sync role (defaulting to MidiSync) plus the lsdj-assets
// role that carries any non-destructive kit/palette/font overrides (empty until the user replaces one).
export const LSDJ_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) =>
  title(rom.header).startsWith("LSDJ")
    ? [
        { kind: "lsdj-sync", config: { mode: LsdjSyncMode.MidiSync } },
        { kind: "lsdj-assets", config: { overrides: [] } },
      ]
    : [];

// Any NES ROM -> host-MIDI passthrough to the core (the always-attached N8 FIFO). Match the PLATFORM
// (core is "mesen"); always-on, mirroring the native role - benign for a ROM that ignores $40F0.
export const NES_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) =>
  rom.platform === "nes" ? [{ kind: "nes-n8-midi", config: {} }] : [];

// smsggdj (the LSDj-style Master System / Game Gear tracker) -> the `sms-sync` role that clocks it
// from the DAW transport. Matched on the ROM's build MARKER, not the platform: on SMS the transport
// rides Player 2's button lines, so attaching this to every SMS cart would inject phantom presses
// into any game that reads the port.
//
// `machine` carries the wire format, because the two builds read different pins - SMS controller
// port 2 ($DD) versus the GG EXT parallel port ($01). Both work: the GG path needs Mesen to honour
// the $02 direction mask on an $01 read rather than looping the port straight back, which is the
// vendored SmsMemoryManager edit.
export const SMSGGDJ_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) => {
  if ((rom.platform !== "sms" && rom.platform !== "gg") || !isSmsggdjRom(rom.header)) return [];
  return [{ kind: "sms-sync", config: { machine: rom.platform } }];
};

// risa (the LSDj-style NES/MMC5 tracker) -> the `risa` marker role that gates the Songs menu, plus the
// `risa-assets` role holding non-destructive theme/font ROM overrides. Detected by its iNES 2.0 header
// fingerprint (MMC5 + 64 KB battery) since NES ROMs carry no title field. A sync-capable build (the
// "RISA-SYNC" header marker) additionally gets the `risa-sync` DSP role that drives its N8-FIFO host-sync
// receive path from the DAW transport; older risa builds without the marker are unaffected.
export const RISA_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom): RoleInstance[] => {
  if (rom.platform !== "nes" || !isRisaRomHeader(rom.header)) return [];
  const roles: RoleInstance[] = [{ kind: "risa", config: {} }, { kind: "risa-assets", config: { overrides: [] } }];
  if (isRisaSyncRom(rom.header)) roles.push({ kind: "risa-sync", config: {} });
  return roles;
};

// BlipToaster (the NES MIDI synth) -> the `bliptoaster` marker role that gates its asset menu, plus the
// `bliptoaster-assets` role holding non-destructive DMC-kit/CHR-font ROM overrides. Detected by the
// "bliptoaster" ASCII marker baked into the ROM head (NROM has no distinguishing header). It has no song
// battery, so there is no song marker - the tracker integration is asset-only.
export const BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom): RoleInstance[] =>
  rom.platform === "nes" && isBlipToasterRomHeader(rom.header)
    ? [
        { kind: "bliptoaster", config: { chip: blipToasterChip(rom.header) } },
        { kind: "bliptoaster-assets", config: { overrides: [] } },
      ]
    : [];
````

````ts
// The kit bank formats this product compiles (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 3): which formats exist is
// the packages' business (each cart's app contribution registers its own, src/generated/packages.ts), so the id to
// format lookup is the shell's, beside src/romProviders.ts and src/trackerRegistry.ts, and the kit compile driver
// (./kit) compiles the format it is handed.
import { KIT_FORMATS } from "./generated/packages";
import type { KitFormat } from "./kit/compile";

/** The product's kit formats, in package order: what kitFormat resolves an id through. */
export { KIT_FORMATS };

/** The kit bank format `id` names, as the product's packages registered it; a driver refuses an id no package
 *  registers, naming it, rather than compiling a bank nothing assembles. */
export function kitFormat<S>(id: string): KitFormat<S> {
  return resolveKitFormat(id, KIT_FORMATS) as KitFormat<S>;
}

/** The format `id` names among `formats`, or refused: an id no format names, or one two formats name (two packages
 *  would otherwise compile their bank or the other's by the list's order alone). Exported so the refusal is held
 *  without two packages actually registering one id. */
export function resolveKitFormat(id: string, formats: readonly KitFormat<any>[]): KitFormat<any> {
  const named = formats.filter((f) => f.id === id);
  if (named.length > 1) throw new Error(`two packages register the kit format "${id}"`);
  if (!named.length) throw new Error(`no package registers the kit format "${id}"`);
  return named[0];
}
````

````ts
// The product's tracker integrations (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 3): which consoles this build
// searches songs and assets on, and the resolvers a system's roles are read through. Each console's integration is its
// package's app contribution, so the list is src/generated/packages.ts and this module is the shell's - beside
// src/romProviders.ts, for the same reason: a package exports to the registry, never the other way. What an
// integration IS is tracker's contract (./tracker/trackerIntegration.ts), which reads nothing here.
import type { RoleInstance } from "./systemRoles";
import type { AssetCatalog } from "./tracker/assetCatalog";
import type { SongCatalog } from "./tracker/songCatalog";
import type { TrackerIntegration } from "./tracker/trackerIntegration";
import { TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS } from "./generated/packages";

// The integrations themselves are the app contributions (./tracker/integrations), re-exported here because a leaf
// imports this module for an integration (render.ts) and the tests reach one by its name on this path.
export { lsdjIntegration, risaIntegration, smsggdjIntegration, blipToasterIntegration } from "./tracker/integrations";

/** Every registered tracker integration, in the product's package order: a system takes the first whose markerRole
 *  it has. The generated list, re-exported below as a live binding. */
export { TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS };

/** The tracker integration for a system, resolved from its attached roles (the first role whose kind is an
 *  integration's markerRole). undefined for a non-tracker system. */
export function resolveTracker(roles: RoleInstance[]): TrackerIntegration | undefined {
  return TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS.find((t) => roles.some((r) => r.kind === t.markerRole));
}

/** The song catalog for a system (convenience over resolveTracker) - used by the recent list. */
export function resolveSongCatalog(roles: RoleInstance[]): SongCatalog | undefined {
  return resolveTracker(roles)?.songs;
}

/** The asset catalog for a system (convenience over resolveTracker). */
export function resolveAssetCatalog(roles: RoleInstance[]): AssetCatalog | undefined {
  return resolveTracker(roles)?.assets;
}
````

objects and the `KitFormat` type. The rest is the call sites: `tracker/index.ts`, the two catalog contracts' headers,

doors, and `tracker/liveSav.ts` resolves its tracker and catalog through `src/trackerRegistry.ts` (it is re-exported
by `src/tracker/index.ts`, so reading the leaf would have been the wrong door). Nothing but import specifiers and the
two lists' construction changed.

- [ ] **Step 5: The UI, the runners, the tools and the ignore list**

Every bundle step whose esbuild inputs reach `src` is ordered after the generator:
`packages/native/cmake/bundles.cmake` adds one always-run `retroplug-ts-packages` target (the generator, every product
manifest, the shell's manifest and the root `package.json` as its `SOURCES`) and an `add_dependencies` per bundle
target (control plane, UI, script nodes, render worker, the CLI dispatcher, its sessions and the CLI SDK assets). The
standalone esbuild entries over `src` call the generator themselves first (`tools/build-cli-sdk.mjs`,
`tools/bundle-native-test.mjs`, `packages/retroplug/scripts/gen-lsdj-offsets.mjs`, and the five
`tools/author-*-rplg.js`, which reach the registries through `test-native/author-*.ts`), and the three runners and the
shell's `typecheck` script do too. `.gitignore` lists `/packages/retroplug/src/generated/`; `.gitattributes` holds the
fixture's expected modules to LF, as the graph goldens are; the shell's `tsconfig.json` excludes the fixture trees
(their expected modules import a fixture tree).


````ts
// The kit bank formats a product registers (src/kitFormats.ts, docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 3).
// Which format an id names is a package's app contribution, so the driver resolves it through the generated list
// rather than importing a cart's assembler; here: the two ids the driver dispatches with resolve to the shell's
// formats, an id nothing registers is refused, and an id two formats name is refused rather than resolved by luck.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { KIT_FORMATS, kitFormat, resolveKitFormat } from "../../src/kitFormats";
import { LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT, RISA_KIT_FORMAT, type KitFormat } from "../../src/kit/compile";

test("the driver's two ids resolve to the shell's kit formats", () => {
  expect(KIT_FORMATS.length).toBe(2);
  expect(kitFormat("lsdj") === LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT).toBe(true);
  expect(kitFormat("risa") === RISA_KIT_FORMAT).toBe(true);
});

test("an id no package registers is refused, naming it", () => {
  expect(() => kitFormat("nope")).toThrow('no package registers the kit format "nope"');
});

test("an id two formats name is refused, naming it", () => {
  const format: KitFormat<unknown> = {
    id: "risa",
    compile: async () => ({ bytes: new Uint8Array(), errors: [] }),
  };
  expect(() => resolveKitFormat("risa", [RISA_KIT_FORMAT, format])).toThrow(
    'two packages register the kit format "risa"',
  );
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/packages/define-package.test.ts`:

````ts
// The app-contribution contract (src/core/definePackage.ts, docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 3):
// definePackage is the identity with types, and the types are CHECKED rather than inferred. A generic parameter
// inferred from the literal would swallow a misspelt key - `romProvider` for `romProviders` - and the contribution
// would silently never register; the parameter's own type refuses it. The `@ts-expect-error` lines below are what
// holds that, since tsc fails an unused directive: if one of these calls compiles again, `pnpm typecheck` does.
//
// The four lists a package may contribute come from two owners: core declares `roles` and `romProviders`, and the
// tracker and dsp modules augment the interface with `trackerIntegrations` and `kitFormats`.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { definePackage } from "../../src/core/definePackage";
import { CORE_ROLES } from "../../src/coreRoles";
import { lsdjIntegration } from "../../src/tracker/integrations";
import { LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT } from "../../src/kit/compile";

test("definePackage is the identity", () => {
  const contributions = definePackage({ roles: CORE_ROLES });
  expect(contributions.roles === CORE_ROLES).toBe(true);
});

// Every owner's keys are part of the contract, so a package's app module may list all four kinds...
const accepted = definePackage({
  roles: CORE_ROLES,
  trackerIntegrations: [lsdjIntegration],
  kitFormats: [LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT],
});

// ...and any other key is an excess property of the parameter's type.
const misspeltCoreKey = () =>
  definePackage({
    // @ts-expect-error: the contract's key is `roles`, not `role`
    role: CORE_ROLES,
  });

const misspeltAugmentedKey = () =>
  definePackage({
    // @ts-expect-error: the tracker's key is `trackerIntegrations`, not `trackerIntegration`
    trackerIntegration: [lsdjIntegration],
  });

test("a contribution key's name is checked, not inferred", () => {
  console.log(`# the contract takes roles, romProviders, trackerIntegrations and kitFormats`);
  expect(typeof accepted).toBe("object");
  expect(typeof misspeltCoreKey).toBe("function");
  expect(typeof misspeltAugmentedKey).toBe("function");
});
````

````ts
// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list (the root
// package.json's retroplug.products.desktop) and the packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and
// rebuild.
//
// The app's registrations, in product order (the list's, which is a dependency order, then the shell): the roles
// buildAppRegistry applies, the ROM providers it offers, the tracker integrations the Songs and Assets menus
// search, and the kit formats the audio driver dispatches to. The protocol tables buildGraph reads are apart, in
// ./protocol.ts, so a module that needs them imports no package's app.
import type { RoleType, RomProvider } from "../systemRoles";
import type { TrackerIntegration } from "../tracker/trackerIntegration";
import type { KitFormat } from "../kit/compile";
import app_alpha from "../../../alpha/ts/app";
import app_beta from "../../../beta/ts/app";
import app_retroplug from "../app";

/** The app's roles, in product order: the role contract's objects, which the registry holds. */
export const ROLES: readonly RoleType[] = [
  ...(app_alpha.roles ?? []),
  ...(app_beta.roles ?? []),
  ...(app_retroplug.roles ?? []),
];

/** The ROM providers, in product order: a ROM's feature roles are attached by the first matches' order. */
export const ROM_PROVIDERS: readonly RomProvider[] = [
  ...(app_alpha.romProviders ?? []),
  ...(app_beta.romProviders ?? []),
  ...(app_retroplug.romProviders ?? []),
];

/** The tracker integrations, in product order: a system takes the first whose markerRole it has. */
export const TRACKER_INTEGRATIONS: readonly TrackerIntegration[] = [
  ...(app_alpha.trackerIntegrations ?? []),
  ...(app_beta.trackerIntegrations ?? []),
  ...(app_retroplug.trackerIntegrations ?? []),
];

/** The kit bank formats, by the id the audio driver dispatches with. */
export const KIT_FORMATS: readonly KitFormat<any>[] = [
  ...(app_alpha.kitFormats ?? []),
  ...(app_beta.kitFormats ?? []),
  ...(app_retroplug.kitFormats ?? []),
];
````

````ts
// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the
// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.
//
// The protocol tables buildGraph, the stores and a DirectGraph wire a system's roles through, as the manifests
// spell them. Nothing but a type is imported here: the data is apart from the node modules it describes, so a
// bundle that reads it carries no node's code, no role's schema and nothing of the app.
import type { ProtocolNodeSpec } from "../graph/protocolNodes";

/** How buildGraph and the stores wire each protocol node type (graph/protocolNodes.ts's ProtocolNodeSpec): the
 *  input its system's routed MIDI arrives on, the system inputs it writes, and the wires it takes or makes. In
 *  span-label order, so which package declares a node changes nothing here. */
export const PROTOCOL_NODES = {
  "rp.alpha.midi": { midiIn: "midi", writes: ["serialIn"] },
} as const satisfies Record<string, ProtocolNodeSpec>;

/** The role kinds that have a protocol node, each with the type it is placed as (the ids PROTOCOL_NODES wires),
 *  in the order of the labels they are placed at. */
export const ROLE_NODES: Readonly<Record<string, keyof typeof PROTOCOL_NODES>> = {
  "alpha-midi": "rp.alpha.midi",
};
````

````ts
import nodes_alpha from "../../../alpha/ts/nodes";
import nodes_retroplug from "../script/nodes";

// The host numbers the nodes it is handed from the first protocol span label up (spec/08-profiling.md).
const FIRST_LABEL = 16;

// The span label of each node type the product's manifests declare.
const LABELS: Readonly<Record<string, number | undefined>> = {
  "rp.alpha.midi": 16,
  "rp.fixture.shell": 17,
};

function labelOf(node: DefinedNode<any>): number {
  const label = LABELS[node.id];
  if (label === undefined) {
    throw new Error(`the script node ${node.id} has no span label (a package's retroplug.protocol.nodes)`);
  }
  return label;
}

// Each package's definitions, in product order; the order the bundle registers them in is the labels', below.
const lists: readonly (readonly DefinedNode<any>[])[] = [
  nodes_alpha,
  nodes_retroplug,
];

const nodes: DefinedNode<any>[] = [];
for (const list of lists) for (const node of list) nodes.push(node);
nodes.sort((a, b) => labelOf(a) - labelOf(b));

// A label is not a node's own: the host numbers what it is handed, in order (ScriptHost's spanLabelFor), so a
// manifest node its module does not export would shift every later type one label down, and a node no manifest
// declares would take the label of one that is missing. Refuse the bundle unless what the modules define is
// exactly the manifests' declarations, each at its own label.
const declared = Object.keys(LABELS);
const missing = declared.filter((type) => !nodes.some((node) => node.id === type));
const extra = nodes.filter((node) => LABELS[node.id] === undefined).map((node) => node.id);
if (missing.length || extra.length) {
  throw new Error(
    `the script bundle's nodes are not the manifests': ${nodes.length} defined, ${declared.length} declared; ` +
      (missing.length
        ? `${missing.join(", ")} has no definition`
        : `${extra.join(", ")} is declared by no manifest`),
  );
}
for (let i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) {
  if (labelOf(nodes[i]) !== FIRST_LABEL + i) {
    throw new Error(
      `the script node ${nodes[i].id} would take the span label ${FIRST_LABEL + i}, ` +
        `not its ${labelOf(nodes[i])}`,
    );
  }
}
registerScriptNodes(nodes);
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/packages/packages-generator.test.ts`:

````ts
// The TS package generator (packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs, docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md
// section 3): the product list and the packages' manifests become the three generated modules. Here:
//
// - a fixture product list and fixture manifests give the expected modules byte for byte: packages.ts, protocol.ts
//   and scriptNodes.ts, the shell last;
// - the generated entry, bundled and loaded, registers the manifest's nodes in span-label order, and refuses when what
//   the modules define is not the manifests' declarations;
// - each of the generator's refusals is exercised with its own message: a list that puts a package before a dependency
//   (a cycle is one), an unlisted dependency that would contribute, a dependency on the shell, a node key no protocol
//   node reads, a node wired on one side only, a shared span label, a shared node type, a shared role kind, a label
//   below 16, a gap, a role naming an undeclared or an unwired type, and a named module that does not exist. A
//   dependency that contributes nothing, and one whose manifest has no retroplug member, are left out of the ordering
//   rather than refused;
// - an unchanged input leaves the generated files untouched, mtime and all, so a build that changes nothing rewrites
//   nothing.
//
// The generator is Node's (it reads and writes the filesystem), so the test runs it in a node child: the runner's own
// node (RP_NODE, which scripts/run-tests.mjs sets), else the node on the PATH when run by hand. test/packages/
// run-generator.mjs does the copying, mutating and reporting.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn, a child's pipe and its file reads, declared locally as bundle-no-zod.test.ts does.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  readFile(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

/** The driver's report for one mode, parsed. */
async function drive(mode: string): Promise<Record<string, any>> {
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "test/packages/run-generator.mjs", mode], {
    stdout: "pipe",
    stderr: "pipe",
  });
  // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`the generator driver failed: ${err || out}`);
  return JSON.parse(out) as Record<string, any>;
}

/** The expected module a fixture records, read beside the fixtures. */
async function expected(name: string): Promise<string> {
  return new TextDecoder().decode(await tjs.readFile(`test/packages/fixtures/expected/${name}`));
}

/** The first line two modules disagree on, or null: a byte comparison of two ~3 KB files says nothing useful when it
 *  fails, and a line names the mistake. */
function difference(generated: string, want: string): string | null {
  const a = generated.split("\n");
  const e = want.split("\n");
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.max(a.length, e.length); i++) {
    if (a[i] !== e[i]) {
      return `line ${i + 1}: generated ${JSON.stringify(a[i] ?? null)}, expected ${JSON.stringify(e[i] ?? null)}`;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

async function matchesFixture(mode: string, name: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const generated = (await drive(mode)).files as Record<string, string>;
  const diff = difference(generated[name]!, await expected(name));
  if (diff) console.log(`# ${name}: ${diff}`);
  return diff === null;
}

test("the fixture product list and manifests generate the expected packages.ts", async () => {
  const report = await drive("generate");
  // The list is the order (alpha, then beta, which depends on it), and the shell closes the app: no package may depend
  // on it.
  expect(report.packages).toEqual(["alpha", "beta", "retroplug"]);
  expect(await matchesFixture("generate", "packages.ts")).toBe(true);
});

test("the fixture product list and manifests generate the expected protocol.ts", async () => {
  expect(await matchesFixture("generate", "protocol.ts")).toBe(true);
});

test("the fixture product list and manifests generate the expected scriptNodes.ts", async () => {
  expect(await matchesFixture("generate", "scriptNodes.ts")).toBe(true);
});

test("the generated entry bundles and registers the manifests' nodes in span-label order", async () => {
  const { registered } = await drive("run");
  console.log(`# registered: ${(registered as string[]).join(", ")}`);

});

  expect(changedFirst).toEqual([true, true, true]);
  expect(changedSecond).toEqual([false, false, false]);
  // The driver aged the files by a minute before the second run, so a rewrite would show: these are the same stamps.
  expect(after).toEqual(before);
````

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Drives packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs over its fixture tree for
// test/packages/packages-generator.test.ts.
// The generator is Node's (it reads and writes the filesystem), so a test that runs under txiki spawns this instead of
// importing it, as bundle-no-zod.test.ts and device-pack.test.ts run their Node toolchains.
//
//   node test/packages/run-generator.mjs <mode>
//
// Each mode copies fixtures/tree to a fresh directory (so a refusal cannot leave the fixtures mutated and a mode can
// edit what it needs), edits it where the mode is a refusal, runs the generator and prints one JSON line:
//
//   generate        { files: { "packages.ts": <text>, "protocol.ts": <text>, "scriptNodes.ts": <text> },
//                     packages: [...] }
//   twice           { mtimes: [<after one run>, <after a second>], changed: [<first run>, <second run>] }
//   run             { registered: [<the ids the generated entry registers, in order>] }
//   missing-node    { error: <the generated entry's own refusal> }
//   order | cycle | unlisted-contributes | unlisted-plain | depends-on-shell | duplicate | duplicate-type |
//   duplicate-role | gap | low-label | role-undeclared | role-unwired | missing-module | unknown-key | half-wired
//                   { error: <the generator's message, or null when it did not refuse> }
//                   (unlisted-plain generates, and reports files like generate)
//
// The run, missing-node and extra-node modes bundle the generated entry with the same esbuild options the build uses
// and load it, so the entry's own checks are what is exercised, not a copy of them.
import { cpSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, statSync, utimesSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { generate } from "../../scripts/lib/packages.mjs";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const { buildOptions } = require("../../../../tools/build-session.js");

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const FIXTURES = join(HERE, "fixtures");
const MODE = process.argv[2];

const work = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "rp-packages-"));
const root = join(work, "tree");
cpSync(join(FIXTURES, "tree"), root, { recursive: true });

const generated = join(root, "packages/retroplug/src/generated");

function editManifest(name, edit) {
  const path = join(root, "packages", name, "package.json");
  const json = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
  edit(json);
  writeFileSync(path, `${JSON.stringify(json, null, 2)}\n`);
}

function editList(...names) {
  const path = join(root, "package.json");
  const json = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
  json.retroplug.products.desktop = names;
  writeFileSync(path, `${JSON.stringify(json, null, 2)}\n`);
}

function outputs() {
  return {
    "packages.ts": readFileSync(join(generated, "packages.ts"), "utf8"),
    "protocol.ts": readFileSync(join(generated, "protocol.ts"), "utf8"),
    "scriptNodes.ts": readFileSync(join(generated, "scriptNodes.ts"), "utf8"),
  };
}

function refusal() {
  try {
    generate({ root });
  } catch (e) {
    return { error: e.message };
  }
  return { error: null };
}

// The generated entry, bundled and loaded as the build loads it. Loading it runs its checks and registers.
async function loadEntry() {
  const out = join(work, "scriptNodes.mjs");
  const { buildSync } = require("esbuild");
  buildSync(buildOptions(join(generated, "scriptNodes.ts"), out, "esm"));
  await import(pathToFileURL(out).href);
  return { registered: globalThis.__rp_registered };
}

// A file in the fixture tree, rewritten for a mode.
function writeTree(relative, text) {
  writeFileSync(join(root, relative), text);
}

let result;
try {
  switch (MODE) {
    case "generate": {
      const ran = generate({ root });
      result = { files: outputs(), packages: ran.packages };
      break;
    }
    case "twice": {
      const first = generate({ root });
      const files = ["packages.ts", "protocol.ts", "scriptNodes.ts"].map((name) => join(generated, name));
      // An old, fixed mtime makes "the second run wrote it again" visible without depending on clock granularity: a
      // write replaces it with the run's time, a run that leaves the file alone leaves this.
      const old = new Date(Date.now() - 60000);
      for (const file of files) utimesSync(file, old, old);
      const before = files.map((file) => statSync(file).mtimeMs);
      const second = generate({ root });
      const after = files.map((file) => statSync(file).mtimeMs);
      result = {
        mtimes: [before, after],
        changed: [first.files.map((f) => f.changed), second.files.map((f) => f.changed)],
      };
      break;
    }
    case "run":
      generate({ root });
      result = await loadEntry();
      break;
    case "missing-node":
      // A manifest node its module does not export: the entry must refuse rather than let every later type take the
      // label below its own.
      generate({ root });
      writeTree("packages/alpha/ts/nodes.ts", "export default [];\n");
      try {
        result = await loadEntry();
      } catch (e) {
        result = { error: e.message };
      }
      break;
    case "order":
      // beta depends on alpha, and the list puts beta first: the order is the list's, so this is refused rather than
      // re-sorted.
      editList("beta", "alpha");
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "cycle":
      // beta already depends on alpha; alpha depending on beta closes the loop, which the order rule sees as alpha
      // preceding a dependency.
      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
        json.dependencies = { "@retroplug/beta": "workspace:*" };
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "unlisted-contributes":
      // gamma is not the product's and would contribute a list, so carrying beta without it would silently drop it.
      editManifest("beta", (json) => {
        json.dependencies = { ...json.dependencies, "@retroplug/gamma": "workspace:*" };
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "unlisted-plain":
      // delta contributes nothing (a native library to link) and plain has no retroplug member at all (a pure TS
      // library), so neither is a product's business: both are left out of the ordering rather than refused.
      writeTree(
        "packages/beta/package.json",
        `${JSON.stringify(
          {
            name: "@retroplug/beta",
            private: true,
            dependencies: {
              "@retroplug/alpha": "workspace:*",
              "@retroplug/delta": "workspace:*",
              "@retroplug/plain": "workspace:*",
            },
            retroplug: { app: "ts/app.ts" },
          },
          null,
          2,
        )}\n`,
      );
      {
        const ran = generate({ root });
        result = { files: outputs(), packages: ran.packages };
      }
      break;
    case "depends-on-shell":
      // The shell is the app itself: nothing may depend on it, whatever it contributes.
      editManifest("beta", (json) => {
        json.dependencies = { ...json.dependencies, "@retroplug/retroplug": "workspace:*" };
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "unknown-key":
      // A misspelt wiring knob (here `launchs` for `launches`) would drop out of PROTOCOL_NODES without a word.
      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes[0].launchs = true;
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "half-wired":
      // A node with midiIn and no writes is placed into PROTOCOL_NODES with half its wiring.
      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
        delete json.retroplug.protocol.nodes[0].writes;
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "extra-node":
      // No manifest declares a node, and a module exports one: the entry must name it rather than complain about a
      // node defined twice.
      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes = [];
        json.retroplug.protocol.roles = {};
      });
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes = [];
      });
      writeTree("packages/retroplug/src/script/nodes.ts", "export default [];\n");
      generate({ root });
      try {
        result = await loadEntry();
      } catch (e) {
        result = { error: e.message };
      }
      break;
    case "duplicate":
      // The shell's only node takes the label alpha's node has.
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes[0].label = 16;
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "duplicate-type":
      // Two packages declare one node type.
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes[0].type = "rp.alpha.midi";
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "duplicate-role":
      // Two packages declare one role kind (through a type both declare, so only the kind is wrong).
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.roles = { "alpha-midi": "rp.fixture.shell" };
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "gap":
      // 17 is the shell's, so moving it to 18 leaves 17 unclaimed.
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes[0].label = 18;
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "low-label":
      // The first protocol label is 16 (spec/08-profiling.md): 15 is the engine's own.
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.nodes[0].label = 15;
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "role-undeclared":
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.roles = { "shell-role": "rp.nope" };
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "role-unwired":
      // A node with no midiIn and no writes is not in PROTOCOL_NODES, so a role cannot be placed as it.
      editManifest("retroplug", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.roles = { "shell-role": "rp.fixture.shell" };
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    case "missing-module":
      editManifest("alpha", (json) => {
        json.retroplug.protocol.module = "ts/nope.ts";
      });
      result = refusal();
      break;
    default:
      console.error(`run-generator.mjs: unknown mode "${MODE}"`);
      process.exit(2);
  }
} finally {
  rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/bundle-protocol.test.ts`:

````ts
// The protocol tables are import-free (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 3): buildGraph, both stores and a
// DirectGraph read the wiring with or without a role registry, and a bundle of the planner must not pull in a node's
// code, a role's zod schema or the app. The tables are generated into src/generated/protocol.ts, a module that imports
// nothing but a type, and graph/protocolNodes.ts reads only that one (src/generated/packages.ts, which imports every
// package's app module, is where they used to live and must not be in this graph).
//
// The bundle is built here as the build builds it, in memory through tools/build-session.js, and esbuild's metafile
// says which modules went in: a zod module, the app or the generated app registries among them fails the test, and
// says which. The build is Node's (esbuild is not a txiki module), so the test runs it in a node child, as
// test/script/bundle-no-zod.test.ts does.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn and a child's pipe, declared locally as bundle-no-zod.test.ts declares them.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

/** One entry's inputs and size, bundled as the build bundles a session (the suite runs from packages/retroplug). */
async function bundle(entry: string): Promise<{ inputs: string[]; bytes: number }> {
  const script =
    `const r = require("../../tools/build-session.js").bundleInputs(${JSON.stringify(entry)}, "esm");` +
    "process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(r));";
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "-e", script], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`bundling ${entry} failed: ${err}`);
  return JSON.parse(out) as { inputs: string[]; bytes: number };
}

/** The modules a bundle of the protocol data may not carry: zod, the app, and the generated registries importing it. */
function forbidden(inputs: readonly string[]): string[] {
  return inputs.filter(
    (path) =>
      /(^|[\\/])zod(@[^\\/]*)?[\\/]/.test(path) ||
      /src\/app\.ts$/.test(path) ||
      /src\/appHost\.ts$/.test(path) ||
      /src\/generated\/packages\.ts$/.test(path) ||
      /src\/(configSchema|systemRoles)\.ts$/.test(path),
  );
}

test("graph/protocolNodes.ts reads the generated protocol data and nothing else", async () => {
  const { inputs, bytes } = await bundle("src/graph/protocolNodes.ts");
  console.log(`# protocolNodes.ts: ${inputs.length} modules, ${bytes} bytes: ${inputs.join(", ")}`);
  expect(inputs.includes("src/generated/protocol.ts")).toBe(true);
  // The module and the data it reads: the tables are apart from the node modules that describe them.
  expect(inputs.length).toBe(2);
  expect(forbidden(inputs)).toEqual([]);
});

test("graph/buildGraph.ts carries the protocol tables but neither zod nor the app", async () => {
  const { inputs, bytes } = await bundle("src/graph/buildGraph.ts");
  console.log(`# buildGraph.ts: ${inputs.length} modules, ${bytes} bytes`);
  expect(inputs.includes("src/generated/protocol.ts")).toBe(true);
  // The planner and its own helpers: 8 modules today; the ceiling keeps a whole package's app out of a quiet arrival.
  expect(inputs.length < 20, `${inputs.length} modules went in`).toBe(true);
  expect(bytes < 64 * 1024, `the bundle is ${bytes} bytes`).toBe(true);
  expect(forbidden(inputs)).toEqual([]);
});
````

````bash
feat(packages): generate the TS package registries from the product list

The desktop product's package list moves into the root package.json (retroplug.products.desktop, the names in
registration order), which CMake reads with string(JSON) into RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES in place of the literal, so one
list serves both languages and the registration order, its golden and the [packages] cases are unchanged. The list
is the order in both languages: a package must follow the ones it depends on, which the generator refuses otherwise
(naming the pair), so CMake's registration order and the app's concatenation cannot diverge. A manifest may now
carry `app` (a module default-exporting definePackage's lists) and `protocol` (its node definitions' module, the
nodes' wiring and span labels, and which role kind each is placed as) beside `native` and `script`; a package with
neither native nor script part registers nothing and adds no target, and retroplug_product skips it.

packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs is the one generator. It reads the product list, each listed package's
manifest and its @retroplug dependencies - a dependency the list does not carry is refused when it would contribute
a list and ignored when it contributes nothing (a package with no manifest, or a manifest with no retroplug member,
contributes nothing) - and writes the three gitignored modules under
packages/retroplug/src/generated. packages.ts holds the app's lists in product order: roles, ROM providers, tracker
integrations, kit formats. protocol.ts holds PROTOCOL_NODES and ROLE_NODES and imports nothing but a type, so
buildGraph reads the wiring without a node's code, a role's schema or the app, which is the property
protocolNodes.ts is import-free for. scriptNodes.ts is the script bundle's entry: it registers in span-label order
and refuses, at load, a set that is not the manifests' declarations (a missing type would shift every later label,
and a node no manifest declares would take a missing one's) or a node that would not take its own label. The
generator refuses a duplicate node type, span label or role kind, a label below 16, a gap, a module that does not
exist, a role naming an undeclared or unwired type, a node key no protocol node reads, a node wired on one side only
(midiIn without writes, or the reverse), a dependency on the shell, and a list out of dependency order. It writes
only a file whose content changed, through a per-run temporary name, so a build that changes nothing touches nothing
and two generators beside each other (two build trees, pnpm test beside pnpm test:native) do not race.

The shell is the one name the generator fixes: packages/retroplug is the app itself, not a package a product lists,
and its own tree is where the modules land, so the root manifest names no separate key and the bundle steps derive
the shell from the generator's path.

The code does not move: the contributions stay in the shell, and its app module lists today's roles, ROM providers,
tracker integrations and kit formats in the order appHost.ts, romProviders.ts, tracker/trackerIntegration.ts and
kit/compile.ts held them. A role is now the RoleType object itself, exported by the module that registered it
(coreRoles' CORE_ROLES, dspRoles' DSP_ROLES, and the asset and marker roles' own), and the register*Role functions
stay for their callers, one line over those objects. Modules split inside the shell, for two reasons: the
generated module imports the lists and a contribution module may not import it back, and a generated read belongs
to the shell once a package owns the module around it. So the ROM providers themselves are romProviderList.ts
(romProviders.ts registers the generated list, as its importers expect); the four integrations are
tracker/integrations.ts and the registry that resolves a system through them is src/trackerRegistry.ts, which leaves
tracker/trackerIntegration.ts the contract an integration satisfies and nothing else; and the kit formats' id lookup
and its refusal are src/kitFormats.ts, which leaves src/kit the compilers a format is handed. Both registries sit

split moves. definePackage is core's, non-generic so a misspelt key fails tsc rather than being inferred and

kitFormat (which now refuses an id registered twice) and protocolNodes.ts's PROTOCOL_NODES/ROLE_NODES read the
generated modules. Every name the
app registered under reads the same, and what an importer sees moved only where the containers widened: the
````

### Task 2: the two boundary checks, and the fixtures that prove them

Design section 4 and section 8's second commit. A package's boundaries become checkable: `check-boundaries.mjs` reads
every file of every package's `ts/` tree with TypeScript's scanner and holds it to its manifest, and
`retroplug_check_package_boundaries()` walks the build's targets at the end of the configure and holds each to its
package's declaration. Both are accident guards, not sandboxes: each header lists what it does not cover, and Task 5's
fix pass is where that list was written down.

The TS half is `packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs`, run at the start of `pnpm test` (quiet unless
`RP_BOUNDARIES_VERBOSE`) and as `pnpm check:boundaries`. The native half is a pure function over plain lists in
`cmake/packages.cmake` (`_retroplug_check_native_boundaries`), driven by `cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake` in script
mode so a configure fixture can exercise it without a target, and by a deferred gatherer that attributes every target of
the build to the package whose directory holds its `SOURCE_DIR`.

**The checks are built red first.** The twelve relative reaches the packs and `n8`'s tests make into the shell are
allowed by `EXCEPTIONS` only because their fix is Task 3's, so Step 1 empties that list for one run (a temporary
mutation, reversed at once) and the checker refuses all twelve and stops `pnpm test` before a test file: a real red, on
the real tree, before anything depends on it. An entry that stops matching is itself a failure, which is what makes
"Task 3 deletes them" mechanical. The native rule's refusals are configure fixtures that run at every configure, so a
rule that stopped refusing would fail `cmake -S . -B build`.

Two of the fixture trees also prove a rule *has* teeth in the other direction: `fixtures/allowed` declares everything
it reaches and must hold with no refusal and no warning, and `read/DeclaredBoundaries.json` and
`read/TestDevDependency.json` hold natively. A check that refused everything would fail those.

- [ ] **Step 1: The TS check**

`check-boundaries.mjs` (one file, ~500 lines: `node packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs [--root <dir>]`,
`refused:`/`warning:`/`allowed:`/`stale:` lines, exit 1 on a refusal or a stale exception, 2 when the tree cannot be
read). For each package with a `ts/` tree it reads every file's imports with TypeScript's scanner
(`ts.preProcessFile(text, true, true)` from the root's `typescript-5` alias, because TypeScript 7 exports none), which
covers `import`, `export ... from`, `import type`, a type-position `import("x").T`, `require` and the triple-slash
`reference` path and `types` directives; a relative specifier resolves against the importing file's directory, and an
unresolvable import is reported without hiding the rest. `packages/retroplug` and `packages/native` are the shells
(one `SHELLS` constant): not judged, and any reach into either is refused. The refusals, each with its own message
naming the file, the import and the owner, are the eight Task 5 documents: a relative import or a `reference path` out
of the package's `ts/`; an `@retroplug/x` the package does not declare (a test file under `ts/test/` or named
`*.test.ts(x)` may also use `devDependencies`); a third-party import it does not declare (`zod/v4` is `zod`); a
dependency on a shell (declared, imported or aliased); a cycle in the declared `dependencies`; an `#include`, quoted
or angled, that climbs out of the package; a declared `@retroplug/x` naming no package, a dependency spec naming
another package than its key and an alias of a package under another key; and an `exports` entry publishing a file
outside `ts/`, a test module, a pattern that can name either, or a file that does not exist. A declared dependency no
file uses is a warning (a dependency whose CMake target the package's native sources name counts as used, and so does
`typescript` when the package's `typecheck` script runs it). `EXCEPTIONS` is one list in the file, each entry naming
the file, the import, the rule and the stage that deletes it; the list applies to the repo tree only.

Create `packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The workspace packages' boundary check (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 4), the TS half: every package
// imports what it declares and nothing else, and no package imports the shell.
//
// What it judges: every workspace package that has a ts/ tree, which means every file under packages/<name>/ts, sources
// and tests alike. packages/retroplug (the app) and packages/native (the engine's own tree) are the shells: they may
// import anything and are not judged, and nothing may import them.
//
// Each file's imports come from TypeScript's own scanner (ts.preProcessFile), so every form a compiler follows is
// judged: a value import, an `import type`, an `export type ... from`, a type-position `import("x").T` and a
// `require`. A relative specifier is resolved against the importing file; a bare one is a package (nameOf) or a
// third-party module, judged against the package's manifest. Type-only imports count on purpose: a package's boundary
// is what it needs to compile on its own, not what survives a bundler.
//
//   1. a relative import that leaves the package's own tree (a ../../retroplug/... reach into the shell, a
//      ../other/ts/... reach into another package's files);
//   2. an @retroplug/<name> the package does not declare in its dependencies (a test file's devDependencies count);
//   3. a third-party module (zod, anything under node_modules) the package does not declare; a subpath ("zod/v4") is
//      judged by its package ("zod");
//   4. a dependency on the shell, @retroplug/retroplug or @retroplug/native, imported or declared: no package may;
//   5. a cycle in the declared dependencies;
//   6. an #include in the package's native sources that has a `..` segment and climbs out of the package, quoted or
//      angled, or a declared @retroplug dependency that names no package.
//
// A declared dependency no file uses is a warning, not a refusal: the native check (cmake/packages.cmake) reads the same
// declaration, so a package whose native targets link a dependency's library declares it without its TS importing
// anything of it. A dependency's target named in the package's native/CMakeLists.txt counts as that use (a textual
// search: CMake is the truthful source, but this warning does not deserve the machinery to ask it).
//
// packages/retroplug/src/generated is the shell's (the generator writes it from the manifests, packages.mjs), so a
// generated module is not judged either, and the shell is where a generated read lives.
//
//   node packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs [--root <dir>] [--quiet]
//
// --root names a tree laid out as this one is (packages/<name>/package.json, packages/<name>/ts, packages/<name>/native),
// which is how the check's own tests drive it over the fixture packages that break one rule each (test/boundaries).
// The command line prints the exceptions' allowed lines, as the maintainer running it wants them; the test runner
// passes verbose only when RP_BOUNDARIES_VERBOSE asks, so `pnpm test` says what it found, not what it forgave.
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = resolve(HERE, "../../..");
const PACKAGES = "packages";
// The shells, by package name: the app, whose own tree holds the generated registries and every module F1 has not moved
// yet, and the engine's tree (packages/native), which holds the node types no package owns. Both may import anything;
// neither may be imported.
const SHELLS = ["retroplug", "native"];

// TypeScript's scanner, resolved from the workspace root's devDependency. The package's own `typescript` (7) works too,
// but its API is the one the typechecker runs, so the check reads imports with the compiler that will see them.
const ts = createRequire(import.meta.url)("typescript-5");

/** Imports that break a rule today and are allowed until the stage that moves the code they reach. Each entry names the
 *  file, the specifier, the rule it breaks and the stage that deletes it; the stage deletes the entry in the same
 *  change as the import, and an entry no refusal matches fails this check, so a fixed line cannot outlive its fix. */
const EXCEPTIONS = [
  // Stage 3 carves core's TS half (defineNode, settingsSchema, script/register) into @retroplug/core.
  {
    file: "packages/bliptoaster/ts/index.ts",
    import: "../../retroplug/src/graph/defineNode",
    rule: "relative",
    removedBy: "stage 3 (core's TS half)",
  },
  {
    file: "packages/bliptoaster/ts/index.ts",
    import: "../../retroplug/src/script/register",
    rule: "relative",
    removedBy: "stage 3 (core's TS half)",
  },
  {
    file: "packages/devtest/ts/index.ts",
    import: "../../retroplug/src/graph/defineNode",
    rule: "relative",
    removedBy: "stage 3 (core's TS half)",
  },
  {
    file: "packages/devtest/ts/index.ts",
    import: "../../retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema",
    rule: "relative",
    removedBy: "stage 3 (core's TS half)",
  },
  {
    file: "packages/devtest/ts/index.ts",
    import: "../../retroplug/src/script/register",
    rule: "relative",
    removedBy: "stage 3 (core's TS half)",
  },
  // Stage 3 makes packages/retroplug/testing a package of its own, @retroplug/testing.
  ...["link-client", "mapConfig", "menuImage", "saveState", "session-client", "sniffer", "sysInfo"].map((name) => ({
    file: `packages/n8/ts/test/${name}.test.ts`,
    import: "../../../retroplug/testing/harness",
    rule: "relative",
    removedBy: "stage 3 (@retroplug/testing)",
  })),
];

function readJson(path) {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
  } catch (e) {
    throw new Error(`${path} cannot be read as JSON (${e.code ?? e.message})`);
  }
}

/** Every file under `dir` whose name `test` accepts, as absolute paths, in a stable order. */
function walk(dir, test, out = []) {
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return out;
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => (a.name < b.name ? -1 : 1))) {
    const path = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(path, test, out);
    else if (test(entry.name)) out.push(path);
  }
  return out;
}

// TypeScript and the JavaScript a package may hold beside its tests (a runner a test spawns, as this repo's own
// test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs is). The fixtures' runners are outside packages/<name>/ts, so this judges a package's.
const isTypeScript = (name) => /\.(ts|tsx|mts|cts|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$/.test(name);
const isNativeSource = (name) => /\.(c|cc|cpp|cxx|h|hh|hpp|hxx|inl|ipp)$/.test(name);

/** The package name a bare specifier names: the scoped pair ("@retroplug/core" -> "@retroplug/core") or the first
 *  segment ("zod/v4" -> "zod", "@types/node" -> "@types/node"). The one spelling every comparison uses, so a subpath
 *  is never a package of its own. */
function nameOf(specifier) {
  const parts = specifier.split("/");
  if (specifier.startsWith("@")) return parts.length > 1 ? `${parts[0]}/${parts[1]}` : specifier;
  return parts[0];
}

/** `@retroplug/<name>`'s short package name, or null for a third-party specifier. */
function packageOf(specifier) {
  const name = nameOf(specifier);
  return name.startsWith("@retroplug/") ? name.slice("@retroplug/".length) : null;
}

/** The workspace's packages, by name, in name order: the ones with a manifest under packages/. */
function workspace(root) {
  const base = join(root, PACKAGES);
  const packages = new Map();
  if (!existsSync(base)) return packages;
  for (const entry of readdirSync(base, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const manifestPath = join(base, entry.name, "package.json");
    if (!entry.isDirectory() || !existsSync(manifestPath)) continue;
    const manifest = readJson(manifestPath);
    const native = manifest.retroplug?.native;
    const entries = native === undefined ? [] : Array.isArray(native) ? native : [native];
    packages.set(entry.name, {
      name: entry.name,
      dir: join(base, entry.name),
      ts: join(base, entry.name, "ts"),
      native: join(base, entry.name, "native"),
      manifestPath,
      // The manifest's names, as nameOf spells them: a declared "@retroplug/beta" is "beta"'s package, and a declared
      // "zod" is the package "zod/v4" names too.
      dependencies: Object.keys(manifest.dependencies ?? {}).map(nameOf),
      devDependencies: Object.keys(manifest.devDependencies ?? {}).map(nameOf),
      // The CMake targets its manifest names: one way a dependency counts as used.
      targets: entries.map((entry) => entry.target).filter((target) => typeof target === "string"),
    });
  }
  return new Map([...packages.entries()].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)));
}

const isShell = (name) => SHELLS.includes(name);
/** Whether a specifier is a module name rather than a path. */
const isBare = (specifier) => !(specifier.startsWith(".") || specifier.startsWith("/") || /^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/.test(specifier));
/** A path as the reports name it: from the tree's root, in the build's slash spelling. */
const shown = (root, path) => relative(root, path).split("\\").join("/");

/** Whether `path` is `dir` itself or under it. Both are absolute. */
function under(dir, path) {
  const rel = relative(dir, path);
  return rel === "" || (!rel.startsWith("..") && !/^[A-Za-z]:/.test(rel));
}

/** The workspace package a resolved path belongs to, or null when it is outside every package (deps/, tools/). */
function ownerOf(packages, root, path) {
  const [first, name] = shown(root, path).split("/");
  if (first !== PACKAGES || name === undefined) return null;
  return packages.has(name) ? name : null;
}

/** How a report names a place an import reaches: the shell, a package, or nothing of the tree's. */
function describeOwner(name) {
  if (name === null) return "a file outside every package";
  return isShell(name) ? `the shell (packages/${name})` : `the ${name} package (packages/${name})`;
}

/** A test file may use its package's devDependencies: a file under ts/test, or one named *.test.ts(x). */
function isTestFile(pkg, file) {
  const rel = relative(pkg.dir, file).split("\\").join("/");
  return rel.startsWith("ts/test/") || /\.test\.(ts|tsx)$/.test(rel);
}

/** Whether an import of `name` (a nameOf name) by `file` is declared: dependencies everywhere, devDependencies in a
 *  test file. */
function declares(pkg, file, name) {
  if (pkg.dependencies.includes(name)) return true;
  return pkg.devDependencies.includes(name) && isTestFile(pkg, file);
}

// A relative import's target, tried the way TypeScript and esbuild resolve one: the specifier itself, then each
// extension, then each directory's index. A `.js` specifier that names a `.ts` source resolves, as the bundlers do.
const EXTENSIONS = [".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".d.ts", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".json"];

function resolveRelative(dir, specifier) {
  const base = resolve(dir, specifier);
  const candidates = [base, ...EXTENSIONS.map((ext) => base + ext)];
  for (const ext of EXTENSIONS) candidates.push(join(base, `index${ext}`));
  return candidates.find((candidate) => existsSync(candidate)) ?? null;
}

/** The line and column of a scanner position, one-based, for the unresolvable report. */
function lineAndColumn(text, pos) {
  const before = text.slice(0, pos);
  const line = before.split("\n").length;
  const column = pos - before.lastIndexOf("\n");
  return { line, column };
}

/** Every import in a package's TS, from TypeScript's scanner: the specifier as written, and for a relative one the
 *  file it names (or null, reported as unresolvable). Type-only forms are included: the scanner lists an `import type`,
 *  an `export type ... from` and an `import("x").T` alike. A file that cannot be read is a problem of its own.
 *  The rest of the package is still judged when one import does not resolve. */
function importsOf(root, pkg, files, problems) {
  const imports = [];
  for (const file of files) {
    let text;
    try {
      text = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
    } catch (e) {
      problems.push({ file, message: `${shown(root, file)}: cannot be read (${e.code ?? e.message})` });
      continue;
    }
    const scanned = ts.preProcessFile(text, true, true);
    for (const found of scanned.importedFiles) {
      const specifier = found.fileName;
      if (isBare(specifier)) {
        imports.push({ file, specifier, target: null });
        continue;
      }
      const target = resolveRelative(dirname(file), specifier);
      if (target === null) {
        const { line, column } = lineAndColumn(text, found.pos);
        problems.push({
          file,
          message: `${shown(root, file)}:${line}:${column}: cannot be resolved: ${specifier} names no file`,
        });
        continue;
      }
      imports.push({ file, specifier, target });
    }
  }
  return imports;
}

/** The cycles in the packages' declared `dependencies`, each as the package names in order. A devDependency edge does
 *  not order anything (the generator's product order reads `dependencies` alone, and pnpm allows a dev cycle), so it
 *  takes no part here. */
function cycles(packages) {
  const edges = new Map();
  for (const pkg of packages.values()) {
    edges.set(
      pkg.name,
      pkg.dependencies.map(packageOf).filter((name) => name !== null && packages.has(name)),
    );
  }
  const found = [];
  const state = new Map(); // name -> "open" | "done"
  const stack = [];
  const visit = (name) => {
    if (state.get(name) === "done") return;
    if (state.get(name) === "open") {
      found.push(stack.slice(stack.indexOf(name)));
      return;
    }
    state.set(name, "open");
    stack.push(name);
    for (const next of edges.get(name) ?? []) visit(next);
    stack.pop();
    state.set(name, "done");
  };
  for (const name of edges.keys()) visit(name);
  return found;
}

/** The check, over one tree: the refusals (each with the rule it broke and its message, which names the file, the import
 *  and the owner), the warnings, the exceptions that matched a refusal, and the exception lines nothing matches. */
export function checkBoundaries({ root = REPO } = {}) {
  const packages = workspace(root);
  const refusals = [];
  const warnings = [];
  const used = new Map(); // a package's name -> the dependency names some file of it (or a native target) uses
  // The exceptions are this tree's: a fixture tree has its own rules to break, and one of our stale entries would fail
  // every fixture run for a reason that is not the fixture's.
  const exceptions = root === REPO ? EXCEPTIONS : [];
  const refuse = (rule, file, specifier, message) => refusals.push({ rule, file, import: specifier, message });
  const markUsed = (pkg, name) => {
    if (!used.has(pkg.name)) used.set(pkg.name, new Set());
    used.get(pkg.name).add(name);
  };

  for (const pkg of packages.values()) {
    for (const name of [...pkg.dependencies, ...pkg.devDependencies]) {
      // Rule 4, the declared half: the shell is no package a product lists, so no package may name it.
      if (isShell(packageOf(name))) {
        refuse(
          "shell",
          shown(root, pkg.manifestPath),
          name,
          `${shown(root, pkg.manifestPath)}: declares ${name} in its dependencies, which is ` +
            `${describeOwner(packageOf(name))}: no package may depend on the shell`,
        );
      } else if (packageOf(name) !== null && !packages.has(packageOf(name))) {
        refuse(
          "declaration",
          shown(root, pkg.manifestPath),
          name,
          `${shown(root, pkg.manifestPath)}: declares ${name}, which is not a package in ${PACKAGES}`,
        );
      }
    }
    if (isShell(pkg.name)) continue;

    // Rules 1 to 4, the import half.
    const problems = [];
    const imports = importsOf(root, pkg, walk(pkg.ts, isTypeScript), problems);
    for (const problem of problems) refuse("unresolvable", shown(root, problem.file), "", problem.message);
    for (const { file, specifier, target } of imports) {
      if (!isBare(specifier)) {
        // A relative import, resolved against the importing file: it must stay in the package's own tree, so a package
        // reaches another as a declared @retroplug/<name> and the shell not at all.
        if (target !== null && under(pkg.ts, target)) continue;
        refuse(
          "relative",
          shown(root, file),
          specifier,
          `${shown(root, file)}: imports "${specifier}", which resolves into ` +
            `${describeOwner(ownerOf(packages, root, target ?? ""))}, outside ${shown(root, pkg.ts)}: a package ` +
            "reaches another as @retroplug/<name>, and the shell not at all",
        );
        continue;
      }
      if (specifier.startsWith("node:")) continue;
      const name = nameOf(specifier);
      markUsed(pkg, name);
      const owner = packageOf(specifier);
      if (owner === null) {
        if (!declares(pkg, file, name)) {
          refuse(
            "third-party",
            shown(root, file),
            specifier,
            `${shown(root, file)}: imports "${specifier}", a third-party module, which ${pkg.name} does not ` +
              "declare in its dependencies (its tests may also use devDependencies)",
          );
        }
        continue;
      }
      if (owner === pkg.name) continue; // a package's own name is its to import
      if (isShell(owner)) {
        refuse(
          "shell",
          shown(root, file),
          specifier,
          `${shown(root, file)}: imports "${specifier}", which is ${describeOwner(owner)}: no package may depend on ` +
            "the shell",
        );
        continue;
      }
      if (!declares(pkg, file, name)) {
        refuse(
          "package",
          shown(root, file),
          specifier,
          `${shown(root, file)}: imports "${specifier}", which is ${describeOwner(owner)}, and ${pkg.name} does not ` +
            "declare it in its dependencies (its tests may also use devDependencies)",
        );
      }
    }

    // Rule 6, the native half: an #include with a `..` segment that climbs out of the package, quoted or angled. A bare
    // include name is an include directory's (node-sdk's graph/node.hpp), which the configure check rules on.
    for (const file of walk(pkg.native, isNativeSource)) {
      const text = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
      for (const match of text.matchAll(/^[ \t]*#[ \t]*include[ \t]*(?:"([^"]+)"|<([^>]+)>)/gm)) {
        const specifier = match[1] ?? match[2];
        if (!specifier.split(/[\\/]/).includes("..")) continue;
        const target = resolve(dirname(file), specifier);
        if (under(pkg.dir, target)) continue;
        refuse(
          "include",
          shown(root, file),
          specifier,
          `${shown(root, file)}: includes "${specifier}", which resolves into ` +
            `${describeOwner(ownerOf(packages, root, target))}, outside packages/${pkg.name}: a package's native ` +
            "sources include their own by path",
        );
      }
    }

    // A dependency the package's native tree links counts as used: one of its CMakeLists names one of the dependency's
    // targets, and the configure check reads the same declaration for the same reason. Every CMakeLists under the
    // package counts (a tool in a subdirectory is the package's too). The search is textual.
    const text = walk(pkg.dir, (name) => name === "CMakeLists.txt")
      .map((file) => readFileSync(file, "utf8"))
      .join("\n");
    for (const name of pkg.dependencies) {
      const short = packageOf(name);
      const targets = short === null ? [] : (packages.get(short)?.targets ?? []);
      if (targets.some((target) => new RegExp(`(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${target}([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)`, "m").test(text))) {
        markUsed(pkg, name);
      }
    }
  }

  // Rule 5: a cycle in the declared dependencies, over every package (the shell's declarations can close a loop too).
  for (const cycle of cycles(packages)) {
    const path = [...cycle, cycle[0]].join(" -> ");
    refuse(
      "cycle",
      `${PACKAGES}/${cycle[0]}/package.json`,
      "",
      `the packages' declared dependencies are a cycle: ${path}`,
    );
  }

  // The warnings: a declared dependency nothing uses.
  for (const pkg of packages.values()) {
    if (isShell(pkg.name)) continue;
    for (const name of [...pkg.dependencies, ...pkg.devDependencies]) {
      if (!used.get(pkg.name)?.has(name)) {
        warnings.push(`${pkg.name}: declares ${name}, which no file of its imports and no native target of it names`);
      }
    }
  }

  // The exceptions: a refusal an entry names is allowed, and an entry nothing matches is itself a failure (the stage it
  // names has removed the import, so its line must go). An entry names the rule it allows, so it cannot allow the same
  // line for a different reason.
  const allowed = [];
  const spent = new Set();
  const allowedRefusals = new Set();
  for (const refusal of refusals) {
    const at = exceptions.findIndex(
      (exception, index) =>
        !spent.has(index) &&
        exception.file === refusal.file &&
        exception.import === refusal.import &&
        exception.rule === refusal.rule,
    );
    if (at === -1) continue;
    spent.add(at);
    allowedRefusals.add(refusal);
    allowed.push({ ...refusal, removedBy: exceptions[at].removedBy });
  }
  const stale = exceptions.filter((_, index) => !spent.has(index)).map(
    (exception) =>
      `the exception for ${exception.file}'s "${exception.import}" matches nothing: ${exception.removedBy} removed it, ` +
      "so delete the entry",
  );

  return { refusals: refusals.filter((refusal) => !allowedRefusals.has(refusal)), allowed, warnings, stale };
}

/** The check, printed as the command line shows it: what the exceptions allow (when `verbose`), the warnings, the stale
 *  exception lines and the refusals. Returns the failure count, so a caller (the test runner) fails on it without
 *  re-reading the report. */
export function reportBoundaries({ root = REPO, verbose = false, log = console.log, error = console.error } = {}) {
  const report = checkBoundaries({ root });
  if (verbose) {
    for (const allowed of report.allowed) log(`allowed: ${allowed.message} [${allowed.removedBy}]`);
  }
  for (const warning of report.warnings) log(`warning: ${warning}`);
  for (const stale of report.stale) error(`stale: check-boundaries: ${stale}`);
  for (const refusal of report.refusals) error(`refused: ${refusal.message}`);
  if (report.refusals.length || report.stale.length) {
    error(
      `check-boundaries: ${report.refusals.length} refusal(s), ${report.stale.length} stale exception(s) under ` +
        `${shown(REPO, root) || "."}`,
    );
    return report.refusals.length + report.stale.length;
  }
  log(
    `check-boundaries: the packages hold their boundaries (${report.allowed.length} allowed by EXCEPTIONS, ` +
      `${report.warnings.length} warning(s))`,
  );
  return 0;
}

if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const at = process.argv.indexOf("--root");
  const root = at === -1 ? REPO : resolve(process.argv[at + 1] ?? "");
  const verbose = !process.argv.includes("--quiet");
  let failed;
  try {
    failed = reportBoundaries({ root, verbose });
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(`check-boundaries: ${e.message}`);
    process.exit(2);
  }
  if (failed) process.exit(1);
}
````
