- [ ] **Step 2: The TS check's own cases and fixture trees**

`test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts` (12 cases) drives `test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs`, which spawns Node on
the checker over a fixture root and returns its output as JSON (through `RP_NODE`, as the generator's driver does).
The trees are one root per rule, so a failure names exactly one package and one rule, plus the positive tree: an
undeclared package, a relative reach into a shell, an undeclared third-party module, a cycle, a climbing `#include`, a
declared and an imported dependency on a shell, an unresolvable import, type-only imports in three forms, a
`devDependency` from a source file, a declared package that names no package, and `allowed` (a declared package
import, a declared third-party subpath, a devDependency from a test, and the package's own interface). The fixtures
are excluded from `tsconfig.json`.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts`:

````ts
// The boundary check over its fixture packages (packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs, docs/modular-graph-
// phase-f1-design.md section 4): one fixture tree per refusal, each breaking exactly one rule, and the check fails it
// with that rule's message, naming the file, the import and the owner:
//
// - an @retroplug import the package does not declare;
// - a relative reach into the shell;
// - a third-party module (zod) the package does not declare;
// - a cycle in the declared dependencies;
// - an #include that climbs out of the package;
// - a dependency on the shell, declared and imported (the two halves of one rule);
// - an import nothing resolves, which is reported by the file and the specifier rather than as a bundler failure, and
//   does not hide the rest of the package's refusals;
// - a type-only reach into the shell (`import type`, `export type ... from`, `import("x").T`);
// - a devDependency a source file imports, which only a test file may;
// - a declared package that does not exist;
//
// and two positive trees: one where a package declares a package it imports by name, a declared third-party subpath, a
// devDependency from a test file and its own interface by a relative path, and the real tree, where the imports the
// check knows about are the EXCEPTIONS list's: the ones stage 3 removes.
//
// The checker is Node's (it reads TypeScript's scanner), so the test spawns test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs, which runs
// it over a fixture root and gives back its output as JSON, as test/packages/packages-generator.test.ts runs the
// generator.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn, a child's pipe and its file reads, declared locally as bundle-no-zod.test.ts does.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

/** The checker's report for one tree, parsed. */
async function drive(which: string): Promise<Record<string, any>> {
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs", which], {
    stdout: "pipe",
    stderr: "pipe",
  });
  // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`the checker driver failed: ${err || out}`);
  return JSON.parse(out) as Record<string, any>;
}

test("an @retroplug import a package does not declare is refused, naming the file, the import and the owner", async () => {
  const report = await drive("undeclared-package");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/alpha/ts/index.ts: imports "@retroplug/beta", which is the beta package (packages/beta), and alpha ' +
      "does not declare it in its dependencies (its tests may also use devDependencies)",
  ]);
});

test("a relative reach into the shell is refused, naming the file, the import and the shell", async () => {
  const report = await drive("relative-reach");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/gamma/ts/index.ts: imports "../../retroplug/src/shell", which resolves into the shell ' +
      "(packages/retroplug), outside packages/gamma/ts: a package reaches another as @retroplug/<name>, and the shell " +
      "not at all",
  ]);
});

test("a third-party module a package does not declare is refused", async () => {
  const report = await drive("undeclared-third-party");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/delta/ts/index.ts: imports "zod", a third-party module, which delta does not declare in its ' +
      "dependencies (its tests may also use devDependencies)",
  ]);
});

test("a cycle in the declared dependencies is refused, naming the path", async () => {
  const report = await drive("cycle");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual(["the packages' declared dependencies are a cycle: epsilon -> zeta -> epsilon"]);
});

test("an #include that climbs out of the package is refused, naming the file, the include and the owner", async () => {
  const report = await drive("climbing-include");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/theta/native/src/x.cpp: includes "../../../other/native/src/y.hpp", which resolves into the other ' +
      "package (packages/other), outside packages/theta: a package's native sources include their own by path",
  ]);
});

test("a dependency on the shell is refused, declared in the manifest and imported alike", async () => {
  const report = await drive("shell-dependency");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    "packages/iota/package.json: declares @retroplug/retroplug in its dependencies, which is the shell " +
      "(packages/retroplug): no package may depend on the shell",
    'packages/iota/ts/index.ts: imports "@retroplug/retroplug", which is the shell (packages/retroplug): no package ' +
      "may depend on the shell",
  ]);
});

test("an import nothing resolves is reported by its file and specifier, and the package is still judged", async () => {
  const report = await drive("unresolvable");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/kappa/ts/index.ts:3:22: cannot be resolved: ./nope names no file',
    'packages/kappa/ts/other.ts: imports "zod", a third-party module, which kappa does not declare in its ' +
      "dependencies (its tests may also use devDependencies)",
  ]);
});

test("a package that declares everything it reaches holds, its own interface and a third-party subpath included", async () => {
  const report = await drive("allowed");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(0);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([]);
  expect(report.warnings).toEqual([]);
  expect(report.stale).toEqual([]);
});

test("type-only imports are judged: an import type, an export type ... from and an import(\"x\").T alike", async () => {
  const report = await drive("type-only-reach");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/alpha/ts/index.ts: imports "../../retroplug/src/a", which resolves into the shell ' +

      "not at all",
    'packages/alpha/ts/index.ts: imports "../../retroplug/src/b", which resolves into the shell ' +
      "(packages/retroplug), outside packages/alpha/ts: a package reaches another as @retroplug/<name>, and the shell " +
      "not at all",
    'packages/alpha/ts/index.ts: imports "../../retroplug/src/c", which resolves into the shell ' +

test("a devDependency is a test file's: a source file that imports one is refused", async () => {
  const report = await drive("dev-dependency-source");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    'packages/alpha/ts/index.ts: imports "@retroplug/testing", which is the testing package (packages/testing), and ' +
      "alpha does not declare it in its dependencies (its tests may also use devDependencies)",
  ]);
});

test("a declared package that does not exist is refused on its own", async () => {
  const report = await drive("declared-missing");
  console.log(`# ${(report.refused as string[]).join("\n# ")}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(1);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([
    "packages/alpha/package.json: declares @retroplug/ghost, which is not a package in packages",
  ]);
});

test("the real tree holds its boundaries through the EXCEPTIONS stage 3 removes", async () => {
  const report = await drive("--tree");
  const allowed = report.allowed as string[];
  console.log(`# ${allowed.length} allowed by EXCEPTIONS:`);
  for (const line of allowed) console.log(`#   ${line}`);
  expect(report.status).toBe(0);
  expect(report.refused).toEqual([]);
  expect(report.stale).toEqual([]);
  // Every entry is the shell reached by a relative path from a package's TS: core's half (bliptoaster, devtest) and the
  // test harness (n8's tests).
  expect(allowed.length).toBe(12);
  expect(allowed.every((line) => line.includes("resolves into the shell (packages/retroplug), outside"))).toBe(true);
  expect(allowed.filter((line) => line.includes("stage 3 (core's TS half)")).length).toBe(5);
  expect(allowed.filter((line) => line.includes("stage 3 (@retroplug/testing)")).length).toBe(7);
});
````

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Runs packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs over a fixture tree, for
// test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts.
//
// The checker is Node's (it reads TypeScript's scanner and the filesystem), so a test that runs under txiki spawns this
// instead of importing it, as test/packages/run-generator.mjs runs the generator.
//
//   node test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs <case>          one tree: fixtures/<case>/, a workspace root of its own
//   node test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs --tree          the real tree
//
// Prints one JSON line: { status, refused: [<the checker's "refused:" lines>], allowed: [...], warnings: [...],
// stale: [...] }, which is the checker's own output read back, so a test holds the message a user would see.
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = resolve(HERE, "../../../..");
const CHECKER = join(REPO, "packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs");
const caseName = process.argv[2];
if (!caseName) {
  console.error("run-checker.mjs: name a fixture case, or --tree for the real tree");
  process.exit(2);
}
const root = caseName === "--tree" ? REPO : join(HERE, "fixtures", caseName);

const child = spawnSync(process.execPath, [CHECKER, "--root", root, "--verbose"], { encoding: "utf8" });
const lines = `${child.stdout ?? ""}${child.stderr ?? ""}`.split("\n");
const pick = (prefix) =>
  lines
    .filter((line) => line.startsWith(`${prefix}: `))
    .map((line) => line.slice(prefix.length + 2))
    .filter((line) => !line.startsWith("check-boundaries:"));
console.log(
  JSON.stringify({
    status: child.status,
    refused: pick("refused"),
    allowed: pick("allowed"),
    warnings: pick("warning"),
    stale: pick("stale"),
  }),
);
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The native check**

`cmake/packages.cmake` gains `_retroplug_read_declarations` (a manifest's `@retroplug` entries from `dependencies` and
`devDependencies`, kept apart so a library cannot lean on a test's), `_retroplug_check_native_boundaries` (the rule,
over plain lists: `LINKS`, `LINK_PATHS`, `LINK_DIRS`, `LIBS`, `INCLUDES`, `DECLARED`, `DEV_DECLARED ... [TEST]`,
`OWNERS`, `UNJUDGED`), `_retroplug_unwrap_item` and `_retroplug_unwrap_option` (the generator expressions the check
can evaluate, and a refusal for those it cannot), `_retroplug_gather_package_links` and
`retroplug_check_package_boundaries`, deferred to the end of the root `CMakeLists` with `cmake_language(DEFER ...)` so
every target exists. It walks the build's targets, resolves an `ALIAS` to its real target and attributes each target
to the package whose directory holds its `SOURCE_DIR`, then judges each of the package's targets: a link (a target
name, a file path, or a `-l` name the build's targets answer to), an include directory, a source, a compile option's
directory (`-I`, `-iquote`, `-idirafter`, `-isystem`, `/I`, `/external:I`, `SHELL:`) and a link option's (`-L<dir>`,
`-l<name>`). A link to another package's target or a path in its tree, an include or source or search directory in
another package's tree, and a link to a target of a shell are refused, each naming the package, the target and the
dependency; an item the check cannot evaluate is refused as unjudged unless the target carries `RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP` with
a reason. A product target is not judged (its `PACKAGES` list is the declaration) and neither is a `-device` twin.
`node-sdk` is always allowed. `cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake` is the script-mode driver, the twin of
`check-manifest.cmake`, and `cmake/test-binary.cmake` marks a test binary so `devDependencies` count for it alone.

Create `cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake`:

````cmake
# cmake -DRP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE=<fixture.json> -P cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake: runs one package's native
# boundary check (cmake/packages.cmake's _retroplug_check_native_boundaries) in script mode, over the scratch package a
# fixture describes, and fails as the configure would. The configure runs it over the fixtures a package must be refused
# for (packages/native/test/packages/refused-native, held by packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake), so the rule cannot stop
# firing unnoticed.
#
# A fixture is plain data, because the real check reads target properties and script mode has no target:
#
#   { "package": "scratch", "declared": ["node-sdk"], "devDeclared": ["testing"], "test": false,
#     "links": ["scratch-nodes=retroplug-graph"], "includes": ["scratch-nodes=@PACKAGES@/graph-runtime/native/src"],
#     "owners": ["retroplug-graph=graph-runtime", "retroplug-node-sdk=node-sdk"] }
#
# "test" marks the fixture's target a test binary (retroplug_add_test_binary's): only one may link a devDependency.
#
# "@PACKAGES@" is the packages directory, so a fixture's include directory is a real path under this tree's packages/.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
if(NOT RP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "check-native-boundaries.cmake: pass -DRP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE=<fixture.json>")
endif()
include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/packages.cmake")

file(READ "${RP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE}" _json)

# One member of the fixture as a CMake list: an array of strings, or "" when the fixture leaves it out.
function(_rp_fixture_list out json member)
    string(JSON _count ERROR_VARIABLE _none LENGTH "${json}" ${member})
    set(_values "")
    if(NOT _none)
        if(_count GREATER 0)
            math(EXPR _last "${_count} - 1")
            foreach(_i RANGE ${_last})
                string(JSON _value GET "${json}" ${member} ${_i})
                string(REPLACE "@PACKAGES@" "${RP_PACKAGES_DIR}" _value "${_value}")
                list(APPEND _values "${_value}")
            endforeach()
        endif()
    endif()
    set(${out} "${_values}" PARENT_SCOPE)
endfunction()

string(JSON _package GET "${_json}" package)
_rp_fixture_list(_declared "${_json}" declared)
_rp_fixture_list(_dev "${_json}" devDeclared)
_rp_fixture_list(_links "${_json}" links)
_rp_fixture_list(_includes "${_json}" includes)
_rp_fixture_list(_owners "${_json}" owners)
string(JSON _test ERROR_VARIABLE _noTest GET "${_json}" test)
set(_test_arg "")
if(NOT _noTest AND _test)
    set(_test_arg TEST)
endif()
_retroplug_check_native_boundaries(${_package} LINKS ${_links} INCLUDES ${_includes} DECLARED ${_declared}
                                   DEV_DECLARED ${_dev} ${_test_arg} OWNERS ${_owners})
message(STATUS "check-native-boundaries.cmake: ${RP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE} holds")
````

````diff
+# _retroplug_read_declarations(<package> <json>): the packages a manifest declares, from its `dependencies` and its
+# `devDependencies` (`@retroplug/<name>` entries only), into RP_PACKAGE_<package>_DECLARATIONS and
+# RP_PACKAGE_<package>_DEV_DECLARATIONS. `dependencies` are what the package's library targets may link and include from
+# (the boundary check below), and what its TS may import (the TS check,
+# packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs); `devDependencies` are its test targets' and its test files' alone:
+# ONE reading for both languages, which is why it is read here and not spelled again in a CMakeLists.
+function(_retroplug_read_declarations package json)
+    set(_declared "")
+    set(_dev "")
+    foreach(_member dependencies devDependencies)
+        string(JSON _deps ERROR_VARIABLE _none GET "${json}" ${_member})
+        if(_none)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        string(JSON _count ERROR_VARIABLE _err LENGTH "${_deps}")
+        if(_err OR _count EQUAL 0)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        math(EXPR _last "${_count} - 1")
+        foreach(_i RANGE ${_last})
+            string(JSON _specifier MEMBER "${_deps}" ${_i})
+            if(_specifier MATCHES "^@retroplug/(.+)$")
+                if(_member STREQUAL "dependencies")
+                    list(APPEND _declared "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
+                else()
+                    list(APPEND _dev "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
+                endif()
+            endif()
+        endforeach()
+    endforeach()
+    set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_${package}_DECLARATIONS "${_declared}")
+    set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_${package}_DEV_DECLARATIONS "${_dev}")
+endfunction()
+
+# _retroplug_check_native_boundaries(<package> LINKS <target=linked>... INCLUDES <target=dir>...
+#                                    DECLARED <package>... DEV_DECLARED <package>... [TEST]
+#                                    OWNERS <target=package>...): a package's native targets may link the targets of the
+# packages its manifest declares, and add include directories inside its own tree or a declared package's. A TEST target
+# (retroplug_add_test_binary's) may also link its package's devDependencies, as a test file may import them; a library
+# target may not. Nothing may link the shell (packages/native, packages/retroplug). Anything else is refused, naming the
+# package, the target and the dependency, because a package that reaches past its manifest makes the split a convention
+# again (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 4).
+#
+# It takes plain lists so a configure-time fixture can drive it (cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake, held by
+# packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake): a target's real properties need a target, which script mode has none of.
+function(_retroplug_check_native_boundaries package)
+    cmake_parse_arguments(B "TEST" "" "LINKS;INCLUDES;DECLARED;DEV_DECLARED;OWNERS" ${ARGN})
+    if(B_UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "_retroplug_check_native_boundaries(${package}): unrecognised argument(s): "
+                            "${B_UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS}")
+    endif()
+    set(_allowed ${B_DECLARED} node-sdk)  # the SDK, which every package's library is built on
+    if(B_TEST)
+        list(APPEND _allowed ${B_DEV_DECLARED})
+    endif()
+    set(_shells native retroplug)
+    # The package that owns each target, by where its directory lies. A target with no package's directory (a vendored
+    # library, an imported one) is nobody's to judge here.
+    foreach(_pair IN LISTS B_OWNERS)
+        string(FIND "${_pair}" "=" _at)
+        string(SUBSTRING "${_pair}" 0 ${_at} _owned)
+        math(EXPR _at "${_at} + 1")
+        string(SUBSTRING "${_pair}" ${_at} -1 _owner)
+        set(_owner_of_${_owned} "${_owner}")
+    endforeach()
+    foreach(_pair IN LISTS B_LINKS)
+        string(FIND "${_pair}" "=" _at)
+        string(SUBSTRING "${_pair}" 0 ${_at} _target)
+        math(EXPR _at "${_at} + 1")
+        string(SUBSTRING "${_pair}" ${_at} -1 _linked)
+        if(NOT DEFINED _owner_of_${_linked} OR "${_owner_of_${_linked}}" STREQUAL "${package}")
+            continue()  # not a package's target, or this package's own
+        endif()
+        if(_owner_of_${_linked} IN_LIST _shells)
+            message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_package(${package}): ${_target} links ${_linked}, a target of the shell "
+                                "(packages/${_owner_of_${_linked}}): no package may use the shell")
+        endif()
+        if(NOT _owner_of_${_linked} IN_LIST _allowed)
+            message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_package(${package}): ${_target} links ${_linked}, a target of the "
+                                "${_owner_of_${_linked}} package, which ${package} does not declare (its package.json "
+                                "dependencies)")
+        endif()
+    endforeach()
+    foreach(_pair IN LISTS B_INCLUDES)
+        string(FIND "${_pair}" "=" _at)
+        string(SUBSTRING "${_pair}" 0 ${_at} _target)
+        math(EXPR _at "${_at} + 1")
+        string(SUBSTRING "${_pair}" ${_at} -1 _dir)
+        file(RELATIVE_PATH _rel "${RP_PACKAGES_DIR}" "${_dir}")
+        if(IS_ABSOLUTE "${_rel}" OR _rel MATCHES "^\\.\\.")
+            continue()  # outside the packages' trees: a vendored dep's headers, or the build's own
+        endif()
+        string(REGEX REPLACE "/.*$" "" _owner "${_rel}")
+        if(_owner STREQUAL package OR _owner IN_LIST _allowed)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        if(_owner IN_LIST _shells)
+            message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_package(${package}): ${_target} adds the include directory ${_dir}, which "
+                                "is in the shell (packages/${_owner}): no package may use the shell")
+        endif()
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_package(${package}): ${_target} adds the include directory ${_dir}, which is "
+                            "in the ${_owner} package's tree, which ${package} does not declare (its package.json "
+                            "dependencies)")
+    endforeach()
+endfunction()
+
+# retroplug_check_package_boundaries(): the boundary check over every package's native targets, from what the build
+# holds. Deferred to the end of the root's CMakeLists (cmake_language(DEFER), as retroplug_check_products is), because a
+# package's check run while it is configured sees only the targets defined before it: a link to a later package's
+# target, or to the shell added last, would pass. Every target is attributed to the package whose directory holds its
+# SOURCE_DIR, so a helper a manifest never names (retroplug-dsp-kernels, retroplug-graph-exec, retroplug-mqjs-host)
+# belongs to its package and is judged like the rest.
+#
+# A device build defines a manifest's `device` targets alone, so a target it does not define is skipped; a target
+# marked RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP (a `-device` twin, a script pack's generated registration) is not judged of its own. A
+# `-device` twin copies its target's include directories through a generator expression and links the SDK's headers
+# alone, and a script pack's registration targets are generated by this file and link the engine's MicroQuickJS host by
+# construction (a pack's own boundary is its TypeScript's, which the TS check holds).
+#
+# A PRODUCT target is not judged either: retroplug_product() links every listed package's targets into it, and its
+# PACKAGES is that link's declaration. The device check's case generator is the one product in a package's directory, and
+# it carries the device check's own package list rather than its directory package's manifest.
+function(retroplug_check_package_boundaries)
+    get_property(_packages GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGES)
+    if(NOT _packages)
+        return()
+    endif()
+    get_property(_product_targets GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PRODUCT_TARGETS)
+    get_property(_device_products GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_DEVICE_PRODUCTS)
+    _retroplug_build_targets(_targets "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
+    set(_owners "")
+    foreach(_target IN LISTS _targets)
+        get_target_property(_skip ${_target} RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP)
+        if(_skip OR _target IN_LIST _product_targets OR _target IN_LIST _device_products)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        get_target_property(_dir ${_target} SOURCE_DIR)
+        if(NOT _dir OR _dir MATCHES "-NOTFOUND$")
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        file(RELATIVE_PATH _rel "${RP_PACKAGES_DIR}" "${_dir}")
+        if(IS_ABSOLUTE "${_rel}" OR _rel MATCHES "^\\.\\.")
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        string(REGEX REPLACE "/.*$" "" _owner "${_rel}")
+        if(NOT _owner IN_LIST _packages)
+            continue()
+        endif()
+        list(APPEND _owners "${_target}=${_owner}")
+        list(APPEND _targets_of_${_owner} "${_target}")
+    endforeach()
+    foreach(_package IN LISTS _packages)
+        if(_package STREQUAL "native" OR _package STREQUAL "retroplug")
+            continue()  # the shells: they may use every package
+        endif()
+        get_property(_declared GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_${_package}_DECLARATIONS)
+        get_property(_dev GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_${_package}_DEV_DECLARATIONS)
+        foreach(_target IN LISTS _targets_of_${_package})
+            get_target_property(_test ${_target} RP_TEST_BINARY)
+            set(_links "")
+            set(_includes "")
+            foreach(_property LINK_LIBRARIES INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES)
+                get_target_property(_value ${_target} ${_property})
+                foreach(_item IN LISTS _value)
+                    # A generator expression resolves per configuration (the device twin's copies), and only a target
+                    # can be attributed to a package.
+                    if(_item MATCHES "^\\$<" OR NOT TARGET ${_item})
+                        continue()
+                    endif()
+                    list(APPEND _links "${_target}=${_item}")
+                endforeach()
+            endforeach()
+            get_target_property(_value ${_target} INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES)
+            foreach(_item IN LISTS _value)
+                if(_item MATCHES "^\\$<" OR NOT IS_ABSOLUTE "${_item}")
+                    continue()
+                endif()
+                list(APPEND _includes "${_target}=${_item}")
+            endforeach()
+            set(_test_arg "")
+            if(_test)
+                set(_test_arg TEST)
+            endif()
+            _retroplug_check_native_boundaries(${_package} LINKS ${_links} INCLUDES ${_includes}
+                                               DECLARED ${_declared} DEV_DECLARED ${_dev} ${_test_arg}
+                                               OWNERS ${_owners})
+        endforeach()
+    endforeach()
+endfunction()

--- a/packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake

+# What a package's native targets may not reach (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 4,
+# cmake/packages.cmake's _retroplug_check_native_boundaries): a target of a package its manifest does not declare, and an
+# include directory in such a package's tree, are each refused with the package, the target and the dependency named.
+# Held the way the manifest rules above are: cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake runs one fixture package in script mode
+# (a real target's properties need a target, which script mode has none of), each must be refused with its own reason,
+# and one that declares what it reaches must hold, so a rule that started refusing everything fails the configure too.
+set(_rp_refused_native
+    "UndeclaredLink|links retroplug-graph, a target of the graph-runtime package, which scratch does not declare"
+    "UndeclaredInclude|which is in the graph-runtime package's tree, which scratch does not declare"
+    "DevDependencyLink|links retroplug-testing, a target of the testing package, which scratch does not declare"
+    "ShellLink|links retroplug-backend, a target of the shell (packages/native): no package may use the shell"
+    "ShellInclude|which is in the shell (packages/native): no package may use the shell")
+foreach(_rp_refused IN LISTS _rp_refused_native)
+    string(REPLACE "|" ";" _rp_refused "${_rp_refused}")
+    list(GET _rp_refused 0 _rp_fixture)
+    list(GET _rp_refused 1 _rp_reason)
+    execute_process(
+        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DRP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/packages/refused-native/${_rp_fixture}.json
+                -P ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake
+        RESULT_VARIABLE _rp_result OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_output ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_output)
+    if(_rp_result EQUAL 0)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/refused-native/${_rp_fixture}.json was accepted; the configure must refuse it")
+    endif()
+    string(REGEX REPLACE "[ \t\r\n]+" " " _rp_folded "${_rp_output}")
+    string(FIND "${_rp_folded}" "${_rp_reason}" _rp_at)
+    if(_rp_at EQUAL -1)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/refused-native/${_rp_fixture}.json was refused, but not with \"${_rp_reason}\":\n"
+                            "${_rp_output}")
+    endif()
+endforeach()
+foreach(_rp_read IN ITEMS DeclaredBoundaries TestDevDependency)
+    execute_process(
+        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -DRP_BOUNDARY_FIXTURE=${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/packages/read/${_rp_read}.json
+                -P ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake
+        RESULT_VARIABLE _rp_result OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_output ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_output)
+    if(NOT _rp_result EQUAL 0)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/read/${_rp_read}.json did not hold:\n${_rp_output}")
+    endif()
+endforeach()
+
+# The gatherer itself (cmake/packages.cmake's retroplug_check_package_boundaries), which the rule fixtures above cannot
+# reach: it reads targets and their SOURCE_DIR. A project of its own under test/packages/gather, configured here, defines
+# alpha before beta, so a link from alpha to beta's helper is to a target defined later, and attributes a helper its
+# manifest never names to beta. Each case is one shape; a refusal case must fail with its reason, a read case must hold.
+set(_rp_gather_cases
+    "later|refused|links retroplug-beta-helper, a target of the beta package"
+    "shell|refused|a target of the shell (packages/native)"
+    "dev-library|refused|links retroplug-testing, a target of the testing package"
+    "declared|holds|"
+    "test-dev|holds|")
+foreach(_rp_case IN LISTS _rp_gather_cases)
+    string(REPLACE "|" ";" _rp_case "${_rp_case}")
+    list(GET _rp_case 0 _rp_name)
+    list(GET _rp_case 1 _rp_expect)
+    list(GET _rp_case 2 _rp_reason)
+    execute_process(
+        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -S ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/packages/gather
+                -B ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/packages/gather-${_rp_name}
+                -DRP_GATHER_CASE=${_rp_name} -DRP_ROOT=${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}
+        RESULT_VARIABLE _rp_result OUTPUT_VARIABLE _rp_output ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_output)
+    if(_rp_expect STREQUAL "refused")
+        if(_rp_result EQUAL 0)
+            message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/gather (${_rp_name}) held; the configure must refuse it:\n${_rp_output}")
+        endif()
+        string(REGEX REPLACE "[ \t\r\n]+" " " _rp_folded "${_rp_output}")
+        string(FIND "${_rp_folded}" "${_rp_reason}" _rp_at)
+        if(_rp_at EQUAL -1)
+            message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/gather (${_rp_name}) was refused, but not with \"${_rp_reason}\":\n"
+                                "${_rp_output}")
+        endif()
+    elseif(NOT _rp_result EQUAL 0)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/gather (${_rp_name}) did not hold:\n${_rp_output}")
+    endif()
+endforeach()
+

 # detection, registered-ROM parent-dir watches, and the unregistered-file filter.
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The native check's fixtures**

`packages/native/test/packages/gather` is a project of its own, configured in `tests.cmake`: it defines targets in one
package and links them from another so the gatherer is judged with targets in hand (alpha defined before beta, a link
to beta's later-defined helper refused, a link to the shell's target refused, a library linking a devDependency
refused, the same link from a test binary allowed, and a declared link allowed). The rule's own fixtures are plain
JSON, one per door: `UndeclaredLink`, `UndeclaredInclude`, `ShellLink`, `ShellInclude`, `DevDependencyLink`, and the
two that must hold, `DeclaredBoundaries` and `TestDevDependency`. A fixture whose reason does not come out as written
`FATAL_ERROR`s the configure, so `cmake -S . -B build` exit 0 is the proof that all of them held. The first two, as
the stage's report quotes them: `retroplug_package(scratch): scratch-nodes links retroplug-graph, a target of the
graph-runtime package, which scratch does not declare (its package.json dependencies)` and `adds the include directory
<packages>/graph-runtime/native/src, which is in the graph-runtime package's tree, which scratch does not declare (its
package.json dependencies)` (the report elides the message's opening, which is the one above's).

Create `packages/native/test/packages/gather/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The native boundary gatherer's own fixture (cmake/packages.cmake's retroplug_check_package_boundaries), driven by
# packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake at every configure. It is a project of its own, configured as a child process, with
# INTERFACE targets under a packages/ tree of its own: the gatherer is the part a plain rule fixture cannot reach, because
# it reads SOURCE_DIR and the build's targets, and script mode has none.
#
# RP_GATHER_CASE picks the shape:
#
#   later        alpha links a helper beta defines AFTER alpha, which alpha does not declare: refused
#   shell        alpha links the shell's backend: refused
#   dev-library  alpha's library links its devDependency: refused
#   declared     alpha links beta's manifest target, declared: holds
#   test-dev     alpha's TEST target links its devDependency: holds
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
project(retroplug_package_gather NONE)

if(NOT RP_GATHER_CASE)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "gather/CMakeLists.txt: pass -DRP_GATHER_CASE=<case>")
endif()
if(NOT RP_ROOT)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "gather/CMakeLists.txt: pass -DRP_ROOT=<the repository root>")
endif()

include("${RP_ROOT}/cmake/packages.cmake")
# The fixture's packages tree, not this checkout's: the gatherer attributes a target by its SOURCE_DIR under this.
set(RP_PACKAGES_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/packages")
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGES alpha beta testing native)
if(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "later")
    set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_DECLARATIONS "")
else()
    set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_DECLARATIONS beta)
endif()
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_alpha_DEV_DECLARATIONS testing)
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_beta_DECLARATIONS "")
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGE_beta_DEV_DECLARATIONS "")

add_subdirectory(packages/alpha)
add_subdirectory(packages/beta)
add_subdirectory(packages/testing)
add_subdirectory(packages/native)

retroplug_check_package_boundaries()
message(STATUS "gather/${RP_GATHER_CASE} holds")
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The native packages declare what they link**

A package that links another's target must declare it, and `node-sdk` is the one every package may link without being
refused (declaring it is still what the TS check and the "one list for both languages" want). The six native packages
declare `"@retroplug/node-sdk": "workspace:*"`; `node-sdk` itself declares nothing (what it links,
`reflectcpp::reflectcpp`, is no workspace package), `bliptoaster` has no native target and no TS import of another
package, and `native` is a shell. The lockfile's diff follows the six manifests, and the frozen install is what proves
it agrees with them.

````bash
feat(packages): hold the packages to the boundaries their manifests declare

The TS check is packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs, run as `pnpm check:boundaries` and first in `pnpm
test` (scripts/run-tests.mjs, before anything bundles). Each file under packages/<name>/ts, sources and tests alike,
has its imports read from TypeScript's own scanner (ts.preProcessFile), so every form a compiler follows is judged:
a value import, an `import type`, an `export type ... from`, a type-position `import("x").T` and a `require`. A
type-only import counts on purpose: the boundary is what a package needs to compile on its own, not what survives a
bundler. A relative specifier is resolved against the importing file (the specifier, then each extension, then each
directory's index), and a bare one is a package name (nameOf: the scoped pair, or the first segment, so "zod/v4" is
zod's) compared with the package's manifest. It refuses, each with its own message naming the file, the import and
the owner: a relative import that leaves the package's own tree (a ../../retroplug/... reach into the shell, a
../other/ts reach into another package's files); an @retroplug/<name> the package does not declare in its
dependencies, where a test file may also use its devDependencies; a third-party module it does not declare, by the
package a subpath names; a dependency on a shell, @retroplug/retroplug or @retroplug/native, imported or declared
(packages/retroplug is the app and packages/native the engine's own tree: they may import anything and nothing may
import them); a cycle in the declared dependencies (over `dependencies` alone: a dev edge orders nothing); an
#include that has a `..` segment and climbs out of the package, quoted or angled; and an import nothing resolves,
reported by file, line and specifier, after which the rest of the package is still judged. A declared dependency no
file uses is a warning, not a refusal: the native check reads the same declaration for the same purpose, so a
dependency whose target a CMakeLists under the package names counts as used (a textual search), which is what keeps
the packages' node-sdk declarations quiet. packages/retroplug/src/generated is the shell's, so a generated module is
not judged either.

The known exceptions are ONE list in the checker, each entry naming the file, the import, the rule it breaks and the
stage that deletes it, and an entry no refusal matches fails the check (and so `pnpm test`), so stage 3 cannot leave
one behind. `pnpm check:boundaries` prints the allowed lines; `pnpm test` prints the summary alone unless
RP_BOUNDARIES_VERBOSE asks.

The native half is cmake/packages.cmake's. _retroplug_read_declarations records a manifest's `dependencies` as
RP_PACKAGE_<name>_DECLARATIONS and its `devDependencies` as RP_PACKAGE_<name>_DEV_DECLARATIONS: a library target may
link only the former (and node-sdk), and a test target (retroplug_add_test_binary marks one RP_TEST_BINARY) may link
both, the reading the TS check gives a file. _retroplug_check_native_boundaries is that rule over plain lists, and
it refuses a link to the shell by name. The gatherer, retroplug_check_package_boundaries, runs ONCE at the end of the
root's CMakeLists (cmake_language(DEFER), as the product check does): a check run inside retroplug_package() saw only
the targets defined before that package, so a link to a later package or to the shell (added last) passed unseen.
It attributes every target to the package whose directory holds its SOURCE_DIR, so a helper no manifest names
(retroplug-dsp-kernels, retroplug-graph-exec, retroplug-mqjs-host) belongs to its package and is judged like the
rest. The documented skips stay: a `-device` twin and a script pack's generated registration carry RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP,
and a product target is not judged because retroplug_product() links its PACKAGES into it and that list is the
declaration. graph-runtime is not exempt, a deliberate departure from the brief's "graph-runtime as the engine's":
nothing needs the exemption now that the gatherer skips products, and a package that links the engine declares it.
packages/native is the shell.

What the real tree needed: the six packages with native targets declare the SDK in `dependencies`
(@retroplug/node-sdk, workspace:*: core, dsp, graph-runtime, n8, device-io, devtest; node-sdk itself links only
reflectcpp, and bliptoaster has no native targets at all), which is the whole of what any of them links natively
today. The check found exactly three breaks, the design's two and one more: bliptoaster's and devtest's script packs
import core's defineNode, settingsSchema and script/register by a relative path (five imports), and n8's seven tests
import ../../retroplug/testing/harness (seven), all stage 3's. The native check found nothing on the real tree.

Red first: the rule fixtures and the gatherer's own. Under packages/retroplug/test/boundaries/fixtures, each tree
breaks one rule (an undeclared @retroplug import, a relative reach into the shell, an undeclared zod, a declared
cycle, a climbing #include, a declared and an imported shell dependency, an unresolvable import beside an undeclared
one, a type-only reach in all three forms, a devDependency a source file imports, a declared package that does not
exist), and two hold: everything a package declares, an interface of its own included, and the real tree. They are
run by test/boundaries/run-checker.mjs and held by test/boundaries/boundaries-checker.test.ts to the check's own
output. The native fixtures (packages/native/test/packages/refused-native/{UndeclaredLink,UndeclaredInclude,
DevDependencyLink,ShellLink,ShellInclude}.json and read/{DeclaredBoundaries,TestDevDependency}.json, driven in
script mode by cmake/check-native-boundaries.cmake) hold the rule, and test/packages/gather, a project of its own
configured by packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake, holds the gatherer: alpha defined before beta, a link to beta's
later-defined helper refused, a link to the shell refused, a library linking a devDependency refused and the same
link from a test target allowed, and a declared link allowed. Every fixture runs inside `cmake -S . -B build`.

F1 changes no behaviour: no golden, baseline or image moves, no RP_*_UPDATE is set, and the skip baseline is
untouched.
EOF
````

### Task 3: core's, dsp's and testing's TS halves, and a tsconfig per package

Design sections 2, 3 and 4 and section 8's third commit. This is a move, not a rewrite: the node mechanism
(`defineNode`, `descriptor`, `settingsSchema`, `graphDocument`, `canonicalJson`, `register`), the role contract
(`systemRoles`), `definePackage`, the MIDI route node with the routing enum it switches on, `clock`, `ports` and `ticks`
move out of the shell into `packages/core/ts`; the kit chain, the packing and the `kitFormats` augmentation into
`packages/dsp/ts`, with the effect union, the offline-job types and the format contract beside them; and the test harness
into `packages/testing`, which every package's tests import by name instead of reaching into the shell.

Twenty-four files move, seven of them byte identical (`canonicalJson`, `defineNode`, `descriptor`, `graphDocument`,
`settingsSchema`, `pack` and the harness), so those seven are only `git mv`; the other seventeen carry a diff of their new
path, which is mostly an import specifier and a header comment. Around the moves: the modules that must be new
(`constructSpec`, `platform`, `offlineJob`, core's barrel and its protocol member, `runtime.d.ts`, dsp's `kitEffect` and
`kitContract`), a two-line `tsconfig.json` per package extending the new root `tsconfig.base.json`, and `runtime.d.ts`
replacing the shell's `src/env.d.ts` as the globals a package may assume. Then every importer in the tree names the
package: about 470 files change an import specifier and nothing else, and they are the bulk of this task's diff.

**The bundlers' options are pinned because this task changed bundle bytes.** Giving `packages/bliptoaster` its own
`tsconfig.json` made esbuild, which reads the nearest tsconfig per input file, apply it to the device pack's entry;
`strict` implies `alwaysStrict`, so the pack's iife bundle gained a `"use strict";` directive, and the pack's bytecode
moved (38,688 to 38,728 bytes at 64 bits, and both device-runtime widths with it). The fix is `tools/ts-options.js`,
passed to every bundle build as `tsconfigRaw`, each build stating its own `alwaysStrict`; the UI bundle is the one
exception, because its modules come from two trees with different tsconfigs. The `packbytes` leg below is the proof, and
it is the reason this task's proof includes an image and a bytecode hash.

The task's first step moves; nothing is built until Step 12, because no step before it leaves a tree that compiles.

`constructSpec.ts` is `ConstructSpec` moved down (a TypeScript-only data shape that names no shell runtime; the

not the protocol node, the routing or the tick clock, so a MicroQuickJS pack that imports the barrel never drags them
in), `protocol.ts` core's protocol member (the MIDI route node), and `runtime.d.ts` the runtime contract: `console`,
`TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder`, the globals the shell's `src/env.d.ts` used to supply. `packages/core/package.json`
gains `"type": "module"`, an explicit `exports` entry per module, `@retroplug/node-sdk` (its native target) and the

integration or kit format.

Create `packages/core/ts/constructSpec.ts`:

````ts
// What TS has to boot a system from (docs/modular-graph-phase-c3-design.md section 6), a type only:
// graph/systemResources.ts (the shell's) turns it into the engine's resources, and nothing native reads it. It lives
// here rather than in the shell's backend because the role contract's onConstruct hook takes and returns one
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md section 9 question 1), and a package's role may not name the shell.
import type { Core, Platform } from "./platform";

export interface ConstructSpec {
  /** The ROM file to read; `""` when an embedded ROM is used instead. */
  romPath: string;
  /** What the ROM targets (TS classifies it via platform.ts). It picks the node the system is placed as
   *  (systemNodeTypeFor), and with it the console its core is built as. */
  platform: Platform;
  /** The kind of core whose role config `coreConfig` is (platform.ts's `Core`): the store keys a system's roles by it.
   *  It selects no core: the platform picks the node type the system is placed as (systemNodeTypeFor), and with it the
   *  console its core is built as. */
  core: Core;
  /** A binary-baked ROM marker (e.g. `"mgb"`); `""` for a file-backed ROM. */
  embeddedRom: string;
  /** Exact battery file: its bytes seed the battery when the file is there, and it is the auto-save target. `null` =
   *  fresh, and a path whose file is absent is fresh too (a missing save is not a failure). */
  savPath: string | null;
  /** Exact savestate file to boot from when the file is there. `null` = cold boot (the systems domain always passes
   *  null; present for the later Project domain). */
  statePath: string | null;
  /** Effective ROM bytes to boot INSTEAD of reading `romPath` - a load-time role's patched image (e.g. LSDj asset
   *  overrides applied non-destructively). `romPath` still names the system (its stem, its sav resolution); only the
   *  bytes differ. */
  romBytes?: Uint8Array;
  /** Seed SRAM bytes (a zip-import blob, a carried battery, or a load-time role's synthesized sav). When set they seed
   *  the battery instead of `savPath`'s file, which stays the auto-save target. */
  sramBytes?: Uint8Array;
  /** Seed savestate bytes (a zip-import blob or a duplicate's captured state). When set the core boots from these
   *  instead of `statePath`'s file; a savestate wins over a battery, as it does at the core. */
  stateBytes?: Uint8Array;
  /** The system's backend ("system"-role) config, in the labels its node reads (the role's schema, which a console
   *  package owns): its construct-time fields (a NES's SD root and FIFO, an SMS's FM) and its live knobs, each left out
   *  of the node's settings where it is absent or a value the node would refuse. Only a caller placing a literal spec
   *  (DirectGraph) writes it; the store reads the core role's config from the entry's own roles and never this field.
   *  Omitted for a system with no core-config role. */
  coreConfig?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}
````

Create `packages/core/ts/offlineJob.ts`:

````ts
// The shape of an offline graph job (docs/modular-graph-phase-d2-design.md section 5): a graph document run to
// completion on a host of its own. It is the engine's job API (the backend's offlineRun, native's OfflineJobs), so it
// lives here beside the graph document, which a package that runs a job has anyway; the queue that runs them, with its
// limits and its wait hooks, stays the shell's (src/offline.ts re-exports these names), and dsp's kit compilers take it
// as what they run their chains on. Nothing here imports anything: a job is data.

/** How a file input's frame cap scales a frame count at a kit rate to the decoded rate: LSDj's window computes it in
 *  float with the ratio first ("float-ratio"), risa's in double with the product first ("double-scale"). */
export type OfflineCapArithmetic = "float-ratio" | "double-scale";

/** A file input's cap: at most `frames` frames at `rate`, scaled to the decoded rate as `arithmetic` says. */
export interface OfflineCap {
  frames: number;
  rate: number;
  arithmetic: OfflineCapArithmetic;
}

/** Audio the call carries: interleaved, `channels` wide, at `rate`. */
export interface OfflineSamplesInput {
  samples: Float32Array;
  channels: number;
  rate: number;
}

/** A file native decodes (the kit compiler's decode: mono, at the file's own rate) and windows: from `offset`
 *  (clamped to the end), `length` frames (absent or 0: to the end), at most the cap. */
export interface OfflineFileInput {
  path: string;
  offset?: number;
  length?: number;
  cap?: OfflineCap;
}

export type OfflineInput = OfflineSamplesInput | OfflineFileInput;

/** An empty buffer the document's recorder writes. */
export interface OfflineOutput {
  channels: number;
  frames: number;
  rate: number;
}

/** A job: `document` (a graph document's JSON, as setGraph takes it; absent for none, so the job returns its inputs)
 *  run for `frames` frames at `rate`, over its inputs then its outputs, which the document names res:1, res:2 and on
 *  (offlineInputRef, offlineOutputRef). `returns` names the handles whose buffers come back, every output by
 *  default. */
export interface OfflineRunRequest {
  document?: string;
  inputs?: OfflineInput[];
  outputs?: OfflineOutput[];
  returns?: number[];
  frames: number;
  rate: number;
}

/** A returned buffer: interleaved, `channels` x `frames` at `rate`, and whether any sample is not finite (native reads
 *  it as it copies the samples out, which is far cheaper than a scan here). */
export interface OfflineBuffer {
  handle: number;
  channels: number;
  frames: number;
  rate: number;
  samples: Float32Array;
  nonFinite: boolean;
}

/** What a file input decoded to and kept: the decoded rate and length, the window's length (0: an empty window, an
 *  input no resource names), and whether a sample the window kept is not finite. */
export interface OfflineInputReport {
  handle: number;
  decodedRate: number;
  decodedFrames: number;
  frames: number;
  nonFinite: boolean;
}

/** A finished job: the buffers `returns` named, in that order, and the file inputs' reports. */
export interface OfflineRunResult {
  buffers: OfflineBuffer[];
  inputs: OfflineInputReport[];
  /** How many times a node's guard replaced what its kernel would have computed during the run (a biquad reset, a
   *  dither restart; native's rp.host.guards/1), and the first one's reason ("" for none). The job completed either
   *  way: whether a guard's output is acceptable is the caller's call (a kit compile refuses it). */
  guardsFired: number;
  guardReason: string;
}

/** The handle input `i` gets in a document, as a resource reference ("res:<n>"). */
export function offlineInputRef(i: number): string {
  return `res:${i + 1}`;
}

/** The handle output `j` gets in a document of `inputCount` inputs, as a resource reference. */
export function offlineOutputRef(inputCount: number, j: number): string {
  return `res:${inputCount + j + 1}`;
}
````

````ts
// The runtime's ambient globals: what the txiki/QuickJS runtime provides and the ES2020 lib does not. This is
// @retroplug/core's runtime contract, which every package and the shell compile against (tsconfig.base.json's `files`

  warn(...args: unknown[]): void;

  decode(input?: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView, options?: { stream?: boolean }): string;
}
````

````ts
// What a kit compiler is and what it runs on (docs/modular-graph-phase-d2-design.md section 5), apart from the
// compilers themselves: the audio driver dispatches by `KitFormat`'s id to a format a cart's app module contributed, and
// a compiler takes a `KitJobRunner` (a host's offline jobs) rather than a backend, so nothing here names the shell.
// compile.ts, which stays the shell's with the formats registered, re-exports these names.
import type { OfflineRunRequest, OfflineRunResult } from "@retroplug/core/offlineJob";

/** A compiled kit: the bank, and each spec sample's reason in spec order, null exactly when the bank holds that
 *  sample whole. A reason is a failure (the slot is empty), or why a slot that compiled is still empty or short (an
 *  LSDj window with nothing to pack, a bank that ran out of room); a sample past the bank's slot count is not
 *  compiled, and its reason says so. */
export interface KitCompileResult {
  bytes: Uint8Array;
  errors: (string | null)[];
}

/** What the compilers run their jobs on: a backend's offline jobs (every native host has them; the mock rejects), of
 *  which the compilers need only the promise, not the handle's cancel.
 *  The promises settle only in a host that pumps or waits for its offline jobs (src/offline.ts): one with a UI tick
 *  pumps from it, and one without needs the poll's native wait, which createAudioDriver turns on as it is made (or
 *  setOfflineWait). In a host with neither, a compile never settles. */
export interface KitJobRunner {
  offlineRun(request: OfflineRunRequest): Promise<OfflineRunResult>;
}

/** One kit bank format a cart contributes (its package's app's `kitFormats`): the compiler an id names, so the
 *  driver dispatches by what the product registered rather than by importing a cart's assembler itself. `id` is the
 *  format's, not the cart's: risa and BlipToaster share "risa", one DMC bank. */
export interface KitFormat<S = unknown> {
  readonly id: string;
  compile(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: S): Promise<KitCompileResult>;
}
````

````ts
// The kit chain's effect spec (docs/modular-graph-phase-d2-design.md section 5), as a kit compiler's spec carries it:
// discriminated on `type`, applied per sample in the chain's order. A field a spec leaves out takes the node's default
// (chain.ts). The shell's audioDriver re-exports these types, so its compile specs and the kit callers keep one spelling.

export type KitFilterEffect = {
  type: "filter";
  filterType?: "LowPass" | "HighPass" | "BandPass" | "BandStop" | "Peak" | "LowShelf" | "HighShelf" | "AllPass";
  frequency?: number;
  q?: number;
  gain?: number;
};
export type KitDitherEffect = {
  type: "dither";
  ditherType?: "HighPassTPDF" | "ShapedTPDF" | "ErrorDiffusion" | "JJN" | "SierraLite";
};
export type KitEffect = KitGainEffect | KitFilterEffect | KitDitherEffect;
````

Create `packages/testing/ts/rig.ts`:

````ts
// A script node driven as the script host drives one (packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.cpp), over a stand-in
// for its Block: settings parsed on the control side and crossed as JSON, a plan swap's onSettings only when they
// changed, and a block that holds the node to its layout. What the stand-in models:
//
// - messages, send and control take only a port the layout has, of the method's kind, and throw a TypeError for
//   another, as the host does; every Block method throws once the process call it was handed to has returned.
// - send copies the data (each value & 0xff) and records the frame twice: as sent, and as the port's queue holds it,
//   raised to the last frame sent on that port this block. It keeps what it was handed too (`sources`), so a test can
//   tell an array a node reuses from one it makes.
// - The messages a block hands out are the node's for that call only: their bytes are scribbled over once it returns,
//   so a node that kept a view past the block reads garbage, as it would from the host's refilled buffers.
import type { Block, ControlStream, DefinedNode, Message, NodeInstance } from "@retroplug/core/defineNode";
import type { Layout } from "@retroplug/core/descriptor";

/** An input message as a test writes it. */
export interface In {
  frame: number;
  data: number[];
  flags?: number;
}

/** One send, in the order the node made it. */
export interface Sent {
  port: string;
  /** The frame the node sent. */
  frame: number;
  /** The frame the port's queue holds it at: raised to the last one sent on the port this block. */
  queued: number;
  data: number[];
  flags: number;
}

export interface BlockSpec {
  frames: number;
  playing?: boolean;
  ppq?: number;
  tempo?: number;
  sampleRate?: number;
  inputs?: Record<string, readonly In[]>;
  controls?: Record<string, ControlStream>;
}

const json = <T>(v: T): T => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v)) as T;

export class NodeRig<S> {
  node: NodeInstance<S>;
  settings: S;
  private layout: Layout;
  /** How many instances create made: 1, and one more for each settings change the definition does not reshape. */
  creates = 1;
  /** The last block's sends, kept when its process threw. */
  last: Sent[] = [];
  /** What each of the last block's sends was handed, index for index with `last`. */
  sources: ArrayLike<number>[] = [];

  constructor(
    readonly def: DefinedNode<S>,
    raw: unknown = {},
    readonly sampleRate = 44100,
    readonly maxFrames = 8192,
  ) {
    this.settings = json(def.parseSettings(raw));
    this.layout = def.layout(this.settings);
    this.node = def.create({ settings: this.settings, sampleRate, maxFrames });
  }

  /** New settings at a plan swap. Unchanged ones (by their JSON) are no change, and reach no hook; a changed layout
   *  without `reshapes` is a new instance. True when the node saw the change. */
  set(raw: unknown): boolean {
    const next = json(this.def.parseSettings(raw));
    if (JSON.stringify(next) === JSON.stringify(this.settings)) return false;
    const layout = this.def.layout(next);
    const reshaped = JSON.stringify(layout) !== JSON.stringify(this.layout);
    this.settings = next;
    this.layout = layout;
    if (reshaped && this.def.reshapes !== true) {
      this.node = this.def.create({ settings: json(next), sampleRate: this.sampleRate, maxFrames: this.maxFrames });
      this.creates++;
    } else {
      this.node.onSettings?.(json(next));
    }
    return true;
  }

  /** The layout's port ids, as `dir kind id`. */
  ports(): string[] {
    return this.layout.ports.map((p) => `${p.dir} ${p.kind} ${p.id}`);
  }

  /** One block, and every send it made. A throw from process is the caller's, the sends before it kept in `last`. */
  run(spec: BlockSpec): Sent[] {
    const sent: Sent[] = [];
    const sources: ArrayLike<number>[] = [];
    this.last = sent;
    this.sources = sources;
    const ports = this.layout.ports;
    const port = (id: unknown, dir: "in" | "out", kinds: readonly string[], what: string) => {
      const p = ports.find((q) => q.id === id && q.dir === dir && kinds.includes(q.kind));
      if (!p) throw new TypeError(`${this.def.id} has no ${what} ${String(id)}`);
      return p;
    };
    let live = true;
    const alive = () => {
      if (!live) throw new TypeError("a block is used only during its node's process call");
    };
    const handedOut: Uint8Array[] = [];
    const lastFrame = new Map<string, number>();
    const block: Block = {
      frames: spec.frames,
      transport: { sampleRate: spec.sampleRate ?? 44100, tempo: spec.tempo ?? 120, ppq: spec.ppq ?? 0, playing: spec.playing ?? false },
      audio: () => {
        throw new TypeError("no audio ports here");
      },
      messages: (id) => {
        alive();
        port(id, "in", ["events", "bytes"], "events or bytes input");
        return (spec.inputs?.[id] ?? []).map((m): Message => {
          const data = Uint8Array.from(m.data);
          handedOut.push(data);
          return { frame: m.frame, data, flags: m.flags ?? 0 };
        });
      },
      send: (id, frame, data, flags = 0) => {
        alive();
        port(id, "out", ["events", "bytes"], "events or bytes output");
        const at = frame >>> 0;
        const queued = Math.max(at, lastFrame.get(id) ?? 0);
        lastFrame.set(id, queued);
        sent.push({ port: id, frame: at, queued, data: Array.from(data, (v) => v & 0xff), flags: flags >>> 0 });
        sources.push(data);
        return true;
      },
      forward: (id, message) => block.send(id, message.frame, message.data, message.flags),
      control: (id) => {
        alive();
        port(id, "in", ["control"], "control input or param");
        return spec.controls?.[id] ?? { start: 0, changes: [] };
      },
      emit: () => {
        throw new TypeError("no control outputs here");
      },
    };
    try {
      this.node.process(block);
    } finally {
      live = false;
      for (const d of handedOut) d.fill(0xee);
    }
    return sent;
  }
}

/** The sends on `port`, each as [queued frame, ...bytes]. */
export const on = (sent: readonly Sent[], port: string): number[][] => sent.filter((s) => s.port === port).map((s) => [s.queued, ...s.data]);

/** The bytes sent on `port`, each as [queued frame, byte]: how a serial-in port is compared, byte by byte. */
export const bytesOn = (sent: readonly Sent[], port: string): [number, number][] => {
  const out: [number, number][] = [];
  for (const s of sent) if (s.port === port) for (const b of s.data) out.push([s.queued, b]);
  return out;
};
````

Create `tsconfig.base.json`:

````json
{
  // The compiler options every workspace package's TS half is checked with: the shell's tsconfig extends this, and so
  // does each package's own, so `pnpm typecheck` (pnpm -r typecheck) checks every package with the options the shell
  // checks it with. Target ES2020 and the bundler resolution the shell bundles with, so a package's nodes compile the
  // same inside a device pack, the script bundle and the UI.
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ES2020",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "strict": true,
    // Off on purpose, and not to loosen any check below: `strict` implies `alwaysStrict`, and a package's own
    // tsconfig.json is what esbuild reads when it bundles that package's TS into a device pack (it discovers the
    // nearest one per entry point). An implied `alwaysStrict` therefore makes esbuild head the pack's iife bundle with
    // a "use strict" directive, and that directive is bytes of the pack's bytecode. TypeScript's own checks are
    // `strict`'s and unaffected; the shell opts back in, where the bundle esbuild builds from it already carries one.
    "alwaysStrict": false,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noImplicitOverride": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    // ES2022.Array only, for Array.prototype.at() in the UI tests. NOT the whole of ES2022: the app runs on QuickJS,
    // and a blanket lib bump would let src reach for APIs the runtime may not have.
    "lib": ["ES2020", "ES2022.Array"],
    "types": [],
    "noEmit": true
  },
  // The runtime's ambient globals (console, TextEncoder, TextDecoder), declared by @retroplug/core as its runtime
  // contract: `lib` stays minimal and `types` empty so a browser or Node global a package did not mean to use is an
  // error. `${configDir}` is the extending tsconfig's directory, so the one entry reaches core from the shell and from
  // every package. `files` is inherited by a config that does not set its own, which is why each package's tsconfig
  // only sets `include`.
  "files": ["${configDir}/../core/ts/runtime.d.ts"]
}
````

- [ ] **Step 10: The generator, the checker and the device toolchain follow the move**

The generator imports a package's contribution by its **exported specifier**, not by a path: it reads the manifest's
`exports` (plain string targets) and imports `@retroplug/<name>/<module>` for the key whose target is the manifest's
file, refusing one the package does not publish; it refuses a manifest whose `name` is not its directory's, and a
contributing package the shell's manifest does not declare. The checker gains the two rules above and the
`typescript`-is-used warning. `build-device-pack.mjs`'s SDK allowlist names core's modules (repo paths), and
`pico/n8-host/exporter-stale.sh` is new: `loop.sh`'s inline staleness list (which still named the shell's `src/graph`
and a `src/script/register.ts` that no longer exists) becomes a script that derives the SDK paths from
`build-device-pack.mjs`'s own `SDK` array and exits 2 when an entry lies outside `packages/core/ts`, so moving an SDK
file without extending the list fails loudly instead of silently unwatching it. `cmake/packages.cmake` gains the
deferred gatherer's unwrapping and the unjudged refusal, and `CMakeLists.txt` the configure's `pnpm install` check.

````diff
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index b369ead74..45263d7ee 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -428,6 +428,28 @@ foreach(_rp_i RANGE ${_rp_products_last})
     list(APPEND RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES "${_rp_package}")
 endforeach()
 
+# A package that contributes an app module or protocol nodes is imported by the shell's generated modules BY ITS PACKAGE
+# NAME (packages/retroplug/src/generated, packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs), and pnpm links it into the
+# shell's node_modules only when the shell declares it. The generator refuses a contribution the shell does not declare;
+# the LINK can still be missing in a checkout pulled before that declaration, and the bundler's bare "Could not resolve"
+# is no help there, so configure says what to do. A package that contributes nothing is not imported, so it needs no link.
+foreach(_rp_ts_package IN LISTS RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES)
+    set(_rp_ts_manifest "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/${_rp_ts_package}/package.json")
+    file(READ "${_rp_ts_manifest}" _rp_ts_json)
+    set(_rp_ts_contributes FALSE)
+    foreach(_rp_ts_member app protocol)
+        string(JSON _rp_ts_kind ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_ts_error TYPE "${_rp_ts_json}" retroplug ${_rp_ts_member})
+        if(NOT _rp_ts_error)
+            set(_rp_ts_contributes TRUE)
+        endif()
+    endforeach()
+    if(_rp_ts_contributes AND NOT EXISTS
+       "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/node_modules/@retroplug/${_rp_ts_package}")
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "packages/retroplug/node_modules/@retroplug/${_rp_ts_package} is missing: the shell's "
+                            "generated modules import ${_rp_ts_package}'s contribution by name, so run `pnpm install`")
+    endif()
+endforeach()
+
 # --- the native package: retroplug-core (shared emulator/Project lib) + the Backend / txiki host
 # + the DPF plugin + the test host / cli / ui-test.
````

Create `pico/n8-host/exporter-stale.sh`:

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Is the plan exporter older than a source it was built from? pico/n8-host/loop.sh refuses to export a firmware's plan
# through an exporter built before a source changed, and this is that comparison, alone so it can be tested without the
# rig:
#
#   ./exporter-stale.sh <stamp> [<repo>]
#
# <stamp> is the file retroplug-export-plan-current leaves beside the tool (retroplug-export-plan.current). Prints the
# first source newer than it and exits 1; prints nothing and exits 0 when the exporter is current; exits 2 on a usage
# error, a missing stamp, or a toolchain whose node SDK this list does not cover.
#
# The list is the exporter's whole build, not the tool's own mtime (a desktop-only source it does not link is newer than
# the tool after a build with nothing to relink):
#
#   - every package's native sources (the exporter links graph-runtime and the SDK, and its device-mode objects compile
#     every package's device entries and script packs' registrations), the exporter's own directory among them;
#   - the TypeScript a device pack is bundled from: each script pack's own ts/ tree, its toolchain
#     (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs) and the portable node SDK;
#   - the CMake that builds either (cmake/, the root CMakeLists.txt);
#   - MicroQuickJS and its generated 32-bit tables, which the image takes from the same desktop build.
#
# The SDK is derived where it can be: build-device-pack.mjs names its files in SDK, and every one must lie under
# packages/core/ts, which this list names as a whole. Moving one without extending the list then fails here (exit 2)
# instead of silently leaving the pack's inputs unwatched.
set -u

usage() { sed -n '3,/^set -u/{/^#/p}' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 2; }

if [ $# -lt 1 ] || [ $# -gt 2 ]; then usage; fi
stamp=$1
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
repo=${2:-$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)}
[ -f "$stamp" ] || { echo "exporter-stale.sh: no stamp at $stamp" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -d "$repo/packages" ] || { echo "exporter-stale.sh: $repo holds no packages/" >&2; exit 2; }

toolchain=$repo/packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs
sdk=$(sed -n '/^const SDK = \[/,/^\];/p' "$toolchain" 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"[^"]*"' | tr -d '"')
for entry in $sdk; do
	case $entry in
		packages/core/ts/*) ;;
		*) echo "exporter-stale.sh: the toolchain's SDK names $entry, which this list does not cover: add its" \
		        "directory to the roots below" >&2; exit 2 ;;
	esac
done

roots=(
	"$repo"/packages/*/native
	"$repo"/packages/graph-runtime/export-plan
	"$repo"/packages/core/ts
	"$toolchain"
	"$repo"/cmake
	"$repo"/CMakeLists.txt
	"$repo"/deps/mquickjs
)
# Each package whose manifest declares a script pack: the pack is bundled from its own ts/ tree.
for manifest in "$repo"/packages/*/package.json; do
	if grep -q '"script"' "$manifest"; then
		roots+=("${manifest%/package.json}/ts")
	fi
done
# A path this checkout does not hold yet (a package without a native tree, a manifest read before ts/ exists) is not a
# source to compare: find would only report it missing.
existing=()
for root in "${roots[@]}"; do
	if [ -e "$root" ]; then existing+=("$root"); fi
done

newer=$(find "${existing[@]}" \
	-path '*/test' -prune -o -path '*/node_modules' -prune -o -type f \
	\( -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.hpp' -o -name '*.h' -o -name '*.c' -o -name CMakeLists.txt -o -name '*.ts' \
	-o -name '*.mjs' -o -name '*.cmake' \) -newer "$stamp" -print -quit)
[ -z "$newer" ] || { echo "$newer"; exit 1; }
exit 0
````

(The `TinyUSB submodule has not been initialized` hint above it is `/opt/pico-sdk`'s own: the check needs no USB, which is why it uses that SDK.) (the size table is identical to the design commit's, the `bliptoaster` pack's rows included: the pack's bytes are the same the harness bundles)

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f1pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f1-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f1-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/f1-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f1-img.bin'`

A different count or hash is a finding to report.
