git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(packages): give core, dsp and testing their TS halves

core's TS is packages/core/ts: defineNode with its descriptor and settings schema, graphDocument and canonicalJson, the
script register, definePackage, the role contract (systemRoles with RoleRegistry, RoleInstance, RomContext,
ConstructCaps), the offline job's shape (offlineJob, the engine's job API, beside the graph document a job runs) and the
midiRoute protocol node (span label 16) with the tick clock, the port capacities and the MIDI routing oracle it and the
other nodes read. dsp's is packages/dsp/ts: the kit chain and pack, the kit compiler contract (a format, its runner and
its result), with packageContributions augmenting core's. testing is packages/testing: the TAP harness and skip, and the
script-node rig published beside it as ./rig. Each package's manifest gains its exports, its dependencies (and
devDependencies: core's tests use @retroplug/testing and zod, n8's use @retroplug/testing) and, for core, its protocol
member; the workspace lockfile moves with them. The rig is testing's rather than core's because it is test support: a
package's node tests import @retroplug/testing/rig, and no package publishes a test module (testing depends on core and
core's tests take testing as a devDependency, which is no cycle: cycles are judged over dependencies alone).

Prototype question 1 (the role contract naming the shell's ConstructSpec): ConstructSpec moves DOWN, into
core/ts/constructSpec.ts, with Platform and Core as types in core/ts/platform.ts (the shell's platform.ts keeps the
detection, the console-to-node table and the battery rules, and re-exports the two types, so they are defined once). A
narrower interface was the other choice; moving the type is smaller and honest because ConstructSpec is already TS's own
data description of a boot (the shell's backend re-exports it), it names no shell module, and it keeps onConstruct's
promise that a role transforms and returns the store's spec unchanged. The generated registry and the stores need no
other shell type.

Prototype question 4 (the kit-compile driver): the driver STAYS the shell's, with only the formats registered.
compile.ts (262 lines) reaches four shell modules (audioDriver's four spec types, offline's error class and job shape,
lsdj's buildKit and constants, risa's kit and constants), and two of those carry the carts' ROM assemblers, which are
the carts' own code; moving the driver would make dsp depend on the carts. The chain and pack (419 lines) reach one
type slice and two pure functions, so that slice moves down (packages/dsp/ts/kitEffect.ts, kitContract.ts) and the
shell's offline.ts and audioDriver.ts re-export it. The job shape itself goes to core rather than dsp: it is the
engine's job API (the backend's offlineRun, native's OfflineJobs) and imports nothing, so a package that runs a job
needs only what it has anyway. Counts: 4 shell modules and 2 cart modules for the driver, 1 type slice and 0 modules
for the chain.

The midiRoute node takes the MIDI routing enum with it (core/ts/midiRouting.ts; the shell's settingsEnums.ts re-exports
MIDI_ROUTING_VALUES and MidiRouting), and ticks.ts, clock.ts and ports.ts move with it. The midi-route, tick-clock,
routing, ticks, defineNode, settings-schema and register tests move to core/ts/test (their subjects moved wholly;
canonical-json, graph-document and conformance stay in the shell because their oracle is
packages/native/test/graph/golden, which is the shell's). No moved file skips, so the skip baseline is untouched; the
case counts are identical per file.

A package's own program is what its boundary means, so every package with a ts/ carries the same two-line tsconfig
extending a new root tsconfig.base.json, which holds the options the shell's tsconfig used to duplicate (the shell now
extends it too), and whose `files` gives every program core's ts/runtime.d.ts: the ambient console, TextEncoder and
TextDecoder, moved out of the shell's src/env.d.ts as @retroplug/core's declared runtime contract. `pnpm typecheck` is
`pnpm -r typecheck`, so each package is checked with its own tsconfig as well as inside the shell's program, which is
where a package's undeclared global would surface. esbuild discovers those tsconfigs when it bundles a package's TS, so
the base sets alwaysStrict off: strict implies it, and it makes esbuild head a device pack's iife bundle with a "use
strict" directive, which is bytes of the pack's bytecode; the shell opts back in, because the iife bundle built from it
(the built-in script pack) has carried that directive all along.

The generator imports a package's app or protocol module by the export key its manifest publishes the file at (ts/app.ts
published at "./app" is "@retroplug/core/app", "./" is the name alone), and refuses a contribution no export publishes,
one outside the package's ts/, a manifest whose name is not its directory's, and a contributing package the shell does
not declare in its dependencies (pnpm links it into the shell only then). The configure checks the same link, because a
pull without `pnpm install` otherwise fails in the bundler with a bare "Could not resolve".

The boundary checker's EXCEPTIONS list is now empty: every reach is a declared package import. It judges the two
triple-slash directives a reference is (a `reference path` reaches a file as a relative import does, a `reference types`
names a type package as a bare import does), refuses an `exports` target under ts/test/ or outside ts/, walks a
package's whole directory for #include reaches, and refuses an absolute include into another package. The native
gatherer unwraps $<BUILD_INTERFACE>, $<LINK_ONLY> and $<TARGET_NAME> and judges what they name, reads
INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES and INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES as it reads the target's own, judges a package's sources that
lie outside its tree, and refuses what no generator-expression form it evaluates (an unjudged item) unless the target
carries RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP. The gather fixture has five cases more and the rule fixtures three. pico/n8-host/loop.sh's
staleness comparison moved out to exporter-stale.sh beside it, which names packages/core/ts (the portable node SDK the
device packs bundle) and every path the exporter and a pack are built from, and derives the SDK from
build-device-pack.mjs's own list so the two cannot drift.

Every hand-written importer now names the package (@retroplug/core/defineNode, /settingsSchema, /register, /systemRoles,
/ticks, /midiRouting, /offlineJob; @retroplug/dsp/chain, /pack, /kitContract, /packageContributions;
@retroplug/testing, /rig), in src, ui, cli, tools-src, test, test-native and test-ui, and the three device-mode fixture
packs import @retroplug/core as any pack does (packages/native declares it as a devDependency). The C++ comments and the
docs that named a moved TS file name its new path.

One path-only fix in a record: docs/launchpad-plan.md's three source links now name core/ts (their visible text is
unchanged), so `pnpm check:docs` stays clean; every other doc link to a moved file was fixed the same way.

F1 changes no behaviour. The script bundle is byte-identical to the baseline's, the generated protocol tables are
byte-identical, and the bliptoaster pack's three bytecodes are byte-identical (066c7980, fd1daf9b, b5017c7c) - which is
what the alwaysStrict setting above is for. `pnpm test` gives 182 files and 1897 cases (base 177 / 1850, the added ones
this commit's new checker and generator cases), `pnpm test:ui` 42 files with the same 2 skips, check:docs 87 files, and
the device check's image hashes the baseline's (rp-device-check 8cc7ae7d).

### Task 4: the console packages, the tracker layer, and a tsconfig that does not move a bundle

Design sections 2 to 4 and section 8's fourth commit. `sameboy` and `mesen` become packages: each owns its role kind and
its settings enums (a tuple's position is still the native enum's integer), and each is TS-only until F2 moves its native
half. `tracker` becomes the cart-neutral layer the design's middle-level decision asked for: the playback model, the two
catalog contracts, the tracker integration contract, `workingSongBlob`, the `ritAssets` override contract that used to be
the shell's `ritAssetsRole`, and the neutral NES ROM helpers risa's code had grown (`find`, `font`, `chrImage`, `theme`,
the formats' constants and the 8 KB kit-bank codec). `settingsEnums.ts` splits to its owners, one enum at a time, with
every zod schema and role-config golden byte-equal. And `core` gains the zod field builders a role's schema is made of
(`configFields.ts`), because a role's config schema is part of the contract and a package may not import the shell.

**Then the bundles.** Giving a package its own `tsconfig.json` in Task 3 was right, and it is why this task must pin the
bundlers' options: esbuild reads the nearest tsconfig per input file, and the six bundle builds must not let that decide
their output. `tools/ts-options.js` spells the options out and each build passes them as `tsconfigRaw`, stating its own
`alwaysStrict` (on for the iife bundles that carry the directive, off for the device packs, whose toolchain prepends its
own); the UI bundle keeps discovery, because its modules come from two trees with different tsconfigs. The device pack's
bytes and the images are the proof, and this task quotes both.

This task also takes the two TS oracles that read the sources as text with it: the C++ `[settings]` case's source list
becomes one glob over the packages (`RP_SETTINGS_TS_PATHS`, refusing an enum two files declare), and
`test/script/bundle-no-zod` stops naming modules by path and denies the product's `app` modules by manifest instead.

 // grayscale tile-grid image, edit a glyph in any image editor, and encode it back to CHR bytes to memWR over

+// (decodeTile/encodeTile) and lays tiles out row-major exactly like the LSDj font-image layer.
 //
 // Each CHR pixel is a 2bpp value 0-3 (a palette index, not a brightness). We render it to a fixed 4-level gray
 // ramp - pixel 0 = white "paper" .. 3 = black "ink" - so the roundtrip is lossless (dump then patch is a no-op)

- [ ] **Step 2: `sameboy` and `mesen`**

Each package is a barrel (`ts/index.ts`), the enum tuples with their types (`ts/enums.ts`), the role and its
`definePackage` (`ts/app.ts`), a manifest with `app` and an explicit `exports` list, and the two-line tsconfig.
SameBoy's four: model, highpass, colour correction, DMG palette. Mesen's four: console region, channel export,
cartridge accuracy, FIFO profile; plus `N8_LINK_VALUES`, which the brief's list did not name and which is a field of
the Mesen role (it configures the emulated EverDrive FIFO in Mesen's NES core, not the physical cart), so a role's own
enum moved with its role. Both depend on `@retroplug/core` alone, and both declare `zod`, which they import directly:
`core` no longer re-exports it, so the boundary check sees every use.

Create `packages/sameboy/ts/app.ts`:

````ts
// SameBoy's app contribution: the core-config "system" role whose kind IS the core (platform.ts's `Core` value), so
// the generic registry attaches it to every SameBoy system. A core's tunable emulator settings ride a role rather than
// the generic system config (so SameBoy's `highpass` never sits in config every core reads), and the role's config is
// one zod schema (core's configFields): shape, defaults and clamping in one place. Its fields' ranges mirror the
// native enums the core reads (SameBoyConfig.hpp: model 0..13, highpass 0..2).
//
// The display group is additive and every default reproduces what the core did when these were
// hardcoded (SameBoySystem.cpp), so an existing project loads pixel-identical and needs no migration.
// Which one bites is decided by the model, and the split is exact rather than a guess: the core
// applies colour correction and light temperature only when GB_is_cgb (model >= GB_MODEL_CGB_0) and
// the DMG palette only when it isn't. `auto` is not ambiguous here - RetroPlug maps it to CGB-C
// (toSameBoyModel), so it counts as CGB. The menu gates the palette row on that (the app's menuDefs.ts).
//
// The native side is the shell's still: `rp_sameboy_package` registers the Game Boy node from packages/native until
// F2 gives this package its native half, and graph/buildGraph.ts's systemKnobs turns these labels into the node's
// settings. linkGroupId is the graph's own, turned into the Game Boy's link wires by buildGraph.ts (linkGroupOf),
// never a core setting.

import type { RoleType } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { z } from "zod";
import { clampedInt, clampedNumber, boolField, enumField } from "@retroplug/core/configFields";
import { MODEL_VALUES, HIGHPASS_VALUES, COLOR_CORRECTION_VALUES, DMG_PALETTE_VALUES } from "./enums";

// model, highpass, colorCorrection and dmgPalette are string enums; the system node's settings spell them as labels
// (knobs::Label), so the store hands them over as they are.
export const SAMEBOY_ROLE: RoleType = {
  kind: "sameboy",
  category: "system",
  schema: z.object({
    model: enumField(MODEL_VALUES, "cgbC"),
    highpass: enumField(HIGHPASS_VALUES, "accurate"),
    linkGroupId: clampedInt(0, 255, 0),
    fastBoot: boolField(true),
    // --- display ---
    colorCorrection: enumField(COLOR_CORRECTION_VALUES, "disabled"),
    dmgPalette: enumField(DMG_PALETTE_VALUES, "grey"),
    // Ambient light tint, CGB only. SameBoy's own range: -1 (cool/blue) .. +1 (warm/red), 0 neutral.
    lightTemperature: clampedNumber(-1, 1, 0),
  }),
};

export default definePackage({ roles: [SAMEBOY_ROLE] });
````

````ts
// The SameBoy core's string-valued settings enums. Each is an index-ordered value tuple whose position EQUALS the
// native enum integer the core's own knob reads: the tuple feeds `z.enum(...)` (core's configFields' enumField) and
// indexes the menu cycler's display-name array, and the system node's settings name a label, which
// graph/buildGraph.ts's systemKnobs hands to the C++ type as that label. The tuples are the app's and the native
// enum's shared definition, so their order and their members are load-bearing: reordering one changes what a stored
// project means.
//
// They live here because SameBoy's role schema reads them and this package owns that role; the shell reads them from
// here for its project schema and its menu cyclers.

// SameBoy model (SameBoyModel 0..13; index 9 = CgbC, the default). Index == the native model int.
export const MODEL_VALUES = [
  "auto", "dmgB", "mgb", "sgb", "sgbPal", "sgb2", "cgb0", "cgbA", "cgbB", "cgbC", "cgbD", "cgbE", "agb", "gbp",
] as const;
export type SameBoyModel = (typeof MODEL_VALUES)[number];

// SameBoy high-pass filter (SameBoyHighpass 0..2).
export const HIGHPASS_VALUES = ["off", "accurate", "removeDcOffset"] as const;
export type SameBoyHighpass = (typeof HIGHPASS_VALUES)[number];

// SameBoy CGB colour correction - index == GB_color_correction_mode_t (Core/display.h). Acts on the
// 15-bit -> RGB conversion, so it only bites on a CGB-family model; a DMG/MGB core ignores it.
// `disabled` is the historical RetroPlug behaviour (raw, oversaturated) and stays the default so no
// existing project changes appearance.
export const COLOR_CORRECTION_VALUES = [
  "disabled",
  "correctCurves",
  "modernBalanced",
  "modernBoostContrast",
  "reduceContrast",
  "lowContrast",
  "modernAccurate",
] as const;
export type SameBoyColorCorrection = (typeof COLOR_CORRECTION_VALUES)[number];

// SameBoy DMG palette - the four built-ins SameBoy exports (Core/display.h). The mirror image of
// colour correction: it only bites in DMG rendering, and a CGB-family core ignores it. `grey` is
// SameBoy's own fallback when no palette is set (GB_update_dmg_palette), i.e. today's behaviour.
export const DMG_PALETTE_VALUES = ["grey", "dmg", "mgb", "gbl"] as const;
export type SameBoyDmgPalette = (typeof DMG_PALETTE_VALUES)[number];
````

Create `packages/mesen/ts/enums.ts`:

````ts
// The Mesen core's string-valued settings enums. As in every settings enum, each is an index-ordered value tuple whose
// position EQUALS the native enum integer the core's knob reads: the tuple feeds `z.enum(...)` (core's configFields'
// enumField) and indexes the menu cycler's display-name array, and the system node's settings carry the label
// graph/buildGraph.ts's systemKnobs hands to the C++ type. Their order and members are load-bearing: reordering one
// changes what a stored project means.
//
// They live here because Mesen's role schema reads them and this package owns that role. `n8Link` and `fifo` are the
// emulated EverDrive N8 cart inside the Mesen NES core (packages/native's src/transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp and the
// FIFO the role's config builds), so they are the core's settings; @retroplug/n8 owns the physical cart.

// NES console region (ConsoleRegion 0..4).
export const REGION_VALUES = ["auto", "ntsc", "pal", "dendy", "ntscJapan"] as const;
export type ConsoleRegion = (typeof REGION_VALUES)[number];

// NES per-channel export mode (spec/10 §5/§5b): mix=0, stereoModPins=1, pinsPlusRef=2, individualMono=3.
export const CHANNEL_EXPORT_VALUES = ["mix", "stereoModPins", "pinsPlusRef", "individualMono"] as const;
export type ChannelExportMode = (typeof CHANNEL_EXPORT_VALUES)[number];

// Cartridge-accuracy switches. "chip" is the documented hardware behaviour and the default; "n8" matches
// an Everdrive N8 Pro's FPGA cores, which measurably differ, so software developed against that cartridge
// (BlipToaster) sounds the same in the emulator as on the console. Both are per-system and live.
//   s5bNoise "n8"       - the 5B has no noise generator there, so tone-AND-noise mutes the channel
//   mmc5PhaseReset "n8" - a $5003/$5007 write does not restart the pulse duty sequencer there
export const CARTRIDGE_ACCURACY_VALUES = ["chip", "n8"] as const;
export type CartridgeAccuracy = (typeof CARTRIDGE_ACCURACY_VALUES)[number];

// How faithfully the emulated EverDrive N8 cart FIFO behaves like the real one.
//   "instant"  - unbounded and delivered immediately. The DEFAULT, and what every existing test was
//                written against: nothing can ever be lost and a pushed chunk is readable at once.
//   "hardware" - 2048 bytes deep, dropping when full, delivered at the wire's ~150 KB/s. Both of
//                those hide bug classes when they are absent: a ROM that cannot lose a byte never has
//                its recovery path exercised, and one handed a whole chunk atomically is never
//                starved mid-structure the way a real wire starves it.
// Construct-time (the FIFO is built when the core activates): setRoleConfig rebuilds the system for an edit.
export const FIFO_PROFILE_VALUES = ["instant", "hardware"] as const;
export type FifoProfile = (typeof FIFO_PROFILE_VALUES)[number];

// BlipToaster's reliable link (packages/native's src/transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp): MIDI to a ROM that advertises it
// (SIG capability bit 0) goes out framed and is re-sent when an NTSC DMC-DMA halt loses a byte, exactly as on a
// physical N8.
//   "auto" - on whenever the ROM advertises it. The DEFAULT: the emulator should lose and recover bytes the way
//            the cartridge does, not be quietly better than it.
//   "off"  - raw MIDI, unframed - for tests that drive the protocol (or a malformed stream) by hand.
// Construct-time (the FIFO role is built when the core activates): setRoleConfig rebuilds the system for an edit.
export const N8_LINK_VALUES = ["auto", "off"] as const;
export type N8LinkMode = (typeof N8_LINK_VALUES)[number];
````

// The iNES asset formats the NES tracker carts share: the header and PRG bank sizes, the 8 KB DMC kit bank, the CHR
// font bank and its 16x16 tile grid, the 7-role theme record and the 64-entry NES master palette, and the PAL DPCM
// playback rates. Ported from risa's own tools/rom_patcher/src (rom.js + theme/constants.js + theme/palette.js +
// font_editor/constants.js), and shared verbatim with BlipToaster, whose ROM bakes the same banks, fonts and theme
// records (its own kit-metadata mirror and theme-table STRIDE are its own, in its package).
//
// These are FORMAT numbers, not one ROM's layout: offsets are DERIVED from the iNES header at runtime by whoever reads
// a ROM (risa's rom.ts computeLayout, BlipToaster's rom.ts), and a cart's own bank counts and mirror sizes stay with
// that cart. Anything here that changed would change what a stored ROM patch means.

export const HEADER_SIZE = 0x10;
export const PRG_16K_SIZE = 0x4000;
export const PRG_8K_SIZE = 0x2000;

// --- Kit bank (DPCM) - tools/rom_patcher/src/kit_editor/constants.js ---
export const KIT_BANK_SIZE = 0x2000; // one kit bank = 8 KB
export const KIT_SAMPLE_REGION = 0x1ec0; // 7872 B of packed DPCM at the bank head
export const KIT_NAME_OFFSET = 0x1ec0;
export const KIT_NAME_SIZE = 16;
export const KIT_NAME_MAX_CHARS = 6; // kit name is uppercased A-Z/0-9/'-', kept to <=6 chars then NUL-padded
export const KIT_SAMPLE_NAMES = 0x1ed0; // 16 x 3-char sample names
export const KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN = 3;
export const KIT_INDEX_OFFSET = 0x1f00; // 16 x 4-byte index entries [addr, lenReg, rate, flags]
export const KIT_INDEX_ENTRY = 4;
export const KIT_SLOT_COUNT = 16;
export const KIT_MAGIC = 0xa5; // "populated" marker
export const KIT_MAGIC_OFFSET = 0x1f40;
export const KIT_SLOT_EMPTY = 0xff;
export const KIT_FLAG_LOOP = 0x01;
export const SAMPLE_ALIGN = 64; // DPCM start-address granularity (addr reg = offset / 64)
export const LENGTH_STEP = 16; // byte length = lenReg * 16 + 1

// PAL DPCM playback rates (Hz), index 0..15 (wav2dmc.py PAL_DPCM_RATES_HZ). Default index 12.
export const PAL_DPCM_RATES_HZ = [
  4177.4, 4696.63, 5261.41, 5579.22, 6023.94, 7044.94, 7917.18, 8397.01,
  9446.63, 11233.8, 12595.5, 14089.89, 16965.4, 21315.52, 25191.0, 33252.09,
];

export const CHR_BANK_SIZE = 0x2000; // one font slot = one 8 KB CHR bank
export const TILE_COUNT = 512;
export const TILE_BYTES = 16;

// --- Themes (NES palette) ---
export const THEME_VERSION = 1;
export const THEME_COUNT = 16;
export const THEME_NAME_SIZE = 4;
export const THEME_RECORD_SIZE = 7;
export const THEME_META_MAGIC = [0xa5, 0x5a, 0x54, 0x48, 0x4d, 0x45]; // "·ZTHME"
// Role order is LOAD-BEARING - each theme record is 7 bytes, one 6-bit NES palette index per role.
export const ROLES = ["bg", "normal", "shaded", "alternate", "status", "cursor", "selection"] as const;
export type ThemeRole = (typeof ROLES)[number];

// The 64-entry NES master palette (compiled into the tool, not read from ROM); index 0x00..0x3F -> #rrggbb.
export const NES_PALETTE: string[] = [
  "#656764", "#002b89", "#1512a7", "#3901a0", "#5c007d", "#71003a", "#6d0504", "#5f1900",
  "#323500", "#0b4900", "#005200", "#004f08", "#00404c", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000",
  "#b8b8b8", "#155fd8", "#4140fe", "#7627fe", "#a019cb", "#b71d7b", "#b13422", "#9a4e00",
  "#6b6d00", "#368800", "#0c9404", "#008f33", "#027b8e", "#000000", "#000000", "#000000",

  "#fefefe", "#c0dffe", "#d3d2fe", "#e9c8ff", "#fcc2ff", "#fec4ea", "#feccc5", "#f7d7a4",

Create `packages/tracker/ts/nes/kitBank.ts`:

````ts
// The DPCM kit-bank format the NES tracker carts share: read an 8 KB bank back (bankToModel), say whether it is
// populated (isBankPopulated), pack slots into one (assembleKitBank, whose fit rule is the kit compiler's own per-slot
// reason), and decode a DPCM stream to audio (dpcmDecode) for round-trip verification. A bank is produced by the kit
// compiler (dsp's chain, over the offline jobs) or re-packed here; risa's own addition - the rows its resident
// metadata mirror carries - stays with risa (packages/retroplug/src/risa/rom/kit.ts). Ported from risa's
// tools/rom_patcher/src/{kit_bank_parser.js, kit_editor/decoder.js}.

import {
  KIT_BANK_SIZE,
  KIT_NAME_OFFSET,
  KIT_NAME_SIZE,
  KIT_NAME_MAX_CHARS,
  KIT_SAMPLE_NAMES,
  KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN,
  KIT_INDEX_OFFSET,
  KIT_INDEX_ENTRY,
  KIT_SLOT_COUNT,
  KIT_MAGIC,
  KIT_MAGIC_OFFSET,
  KIT_SLOT_EMPTY,
  KIT_FLAG_LOOP,
  KIT_SAMPLE_REGION,
  SAMPLE_ALIGN,
  LENGTH_STEP,
} from "./constants";

/** One populated kit slot decoded from a bank. `dpcm` is the raw DMC bytes. */
export interface KitSlot {
  addr: number; // $4012 register (sample offset = addr * 64)
  lenReg: number; // $4013 register (byte length = lenReg * 16 + 1)
  rate: number; // PAL DPCM rate index 0..15
  loop: boolean;
  name: string; // 3-char sample name (trimmed)
  dpcm: Uint8Array;
}

/** A decoded kit bank: its name + 16 slots (null where empty). */
export interface KitModel {
  name: string;
  slots: (KitSlot | null)[];
}

function ascii(bytes: Uint8Array, off: number, len: number): string {
  let s = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {
    const b = bytes[off + i];
    if (b === 0) break;
    s += String.fromCharCode(b);
  }
  return s.replace(/\s+$/, "");
}

/** Parse an 8 KB kit bank into its name + populated slots (index table + sample names + DPCM bytes). */
export function bankToModel(bank: Uint8Array): KitModel {
  const slots: (KitSlot | null)[] = [];
  for (let slot = 0; slot < KIT_SLOT_COUNT; slot++) {
    const pos = KIT_INDEX_OFFSET + slot * KIT_INDEX_ENTRY;
    const addr = bank[pos];
    if (addr === KIT_SLOT_EMPTY) {
      slots.push(null);
      continue;
    }
    const lenReg = bank[pos + 1];
    const sampleOff = addr * SAMPLE_ALIGN;
    const byteLen = lenReg * LENGTH_STEP + 1;
    slots.push({
      addr,
      lenReg,
      rate: bank[pos + 2] & 0x0f,
      loop: (bank[pos + 3] & KIT_FLAG_LOOP) !== 0,
      name: ascii(bank, KIT_SAMPLE_NAMES + slot * KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN, KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN),
      dpcm: bank.slice(sampleOff, Math.min(sampleOff + byteLen, KIT_SAMPLE_REGION)),
    });
  }
  return { name: ascii(bank, KIT_NAME_OFFSET, KIT_NAME_SIZE), slots };
}

/** True if a bank is populated (the 0xA5 magic is present). */
export function isBankPopulated(bank: Uint8Array): boolean {
  return bank[KIT_MAGIC_OFFSET] === KIT_MAGIC;
}

/** One slot to pack into a bank: its raw DPCM bytes + the index-entry metadata. */
export interface AssembleSlot {
  dpcm: Uint8Array;
  rate: number; // PAL DPCM rate index 0..15
  loop: boolean;
  name: string; // 3-char sample name
}

const utf8 = new TextEncoder();

// A name's bytes (its UTF-8), with a-z uppercased and every other byte left as it is: the bank's ASCII-only uppercase,
// byte by byte, so one name gives one bank.
function upperAsciiBytes(name: string): Uint8Array {
  const bytes = utf8.encode(name);
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) if (bytes[i] >= 0x61 && bytes[i] <= 0x7a) bytes[i] -= 0x20;
  return bytes;
}

// A 3-char, uppercased, right-space-padded sample name, as the bank's sample-name field stores it.
function writeSampleName(bank: Uint8Array, off: number, name: string): void {
  const bytes = upperAsciiBytes(name);
  for (let i = 0; i < KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN; i++) bank[off + i] = i < bytes.length ? bytes[i] : 0x20;
}

/** Pack DPCM slots into an 8 KB kit bank. Greedy 64-byte-aligned packing into the 7872 B sample region, a 4-byte
 *  index entry per slot ([addr, lenReg, rate, flags]), 3-char sample names, the ≤6-char kit name, and the 0xA5
 *  populated magic. A null slot stays EMPTY with its index preserved (NOT compacted); a slot whose DPCM won't fit the
 *  remaining region is left empty. Because a slot's encode carries no cross-sample state, this is byte-identical to
 *  compiling the same samples together via compileDmc - so it losslessly re-packs existing slots' DPCM alongside a
 *  new one. */
export function assembleKitBank(kitName: string, slots: (AssembleSlot | null)[]): Uint8Array {
  return assembleKitBankPlaced(kitName, slots).bank;
}

/** A bank and which slots landed in it: `placed[i]` is false for a slot given no bytes (null or empty) and for one
 *  that did not fit the sample region after the slots before it. Only the first KIT_SLOT_COUNT slots are listed. */
export interface PlacedRisaKitBank {
  bank: Uint8Array;
  placed: boolean[];
}

/** assembleKitBank, saying which slots landed: the kit compiler's per-slot reason for a slot that did not fit comes
 *  from here, so it cannot drift from the assembler's own fit rule. */
export function assembleKitBankPlaced(kitName: string, slots: (AssembleSlot | null)[]): PlacedRisaKitBank {
  const placed: boolean[] = [];
  const bank = new Uint8Array(KIT_BANK_SIZE);
  // Sample-name region defaults to spaces (kit_bank_parser modelToBank).
  bank.fill(0x20, KIT_SAMPLE_NAMES, KIT_SAMPLE_NAMES + KIT_SLOT_COUNT * KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN);

  let cursor = 0;
  for (let slot = 0; slot < KIT_SLOT_COUNT; slot++) {
    const idx = KIT_INDEX_OFFSET + slot * KIT_INDEX_ENTRY;
    bank[idx] = KIT_SLOT_EMPTY; // default: empty entry [0xFF, 0, 0, 0]

    const s = slot < slots.length ? slots[slot] : null;
    if (slot < slots.length) placed.push(false);
    if (!s || s.dpcm.length === 0) continue;

    if (cursor % SAMPLE_ALIGN) cursor += SAMPLE_ALIGN - (cursor % SAMPLE_ALIGN);
    if (cursor + s.dpcm.length > KIT_SAMPLE_REGION) continue; // doesn't fit - leave the slot empty
    placed[slot] = true;

    bank.set(s.dpcm, cursor);
    bank[idx] = Math.floor(cursor / SAMPLE_ALIGN) & 0xff; // $4012 address
    bank[idx + 1] = Math.floor((s.dpcm.length - 1) / LENGTH_STEP) & 0xff; // $4013 length reg
    bank[idx + 2] = s.rate & 0x0f;
    bank[idx + 3] = s.loop ? KIT_FLAG_LOOP : 0;
    writeSampleName(bank, KIT_SAMPLE_NAMES + slot * KIT_SAMPLE_NAME_LEN, s.name);
    cursor += s.dpcm.length;
  }

  // Kit name: uppercased, keep A-Z 0-9 '-', up to 6 chars, NUL-padded to KIT_NAME_SIZE. Byte by byte over the
  // name's UTF-8 by that rule, so a non-ASCII character is dropped whole rather than uppercased into a letter.
  let w = 0;
  for (const c of upperAsciiBytes(kitName)) {
    if (w >= KIT_NAME_MAX_CHARS) break;
    if ((c >= 0x41 && c <= 0x5a) || (c >= 0x30 && c <= 0x39) || c === 0x2d) bank[KIT_NAME_OFFSET + w++] = c;
  }
  void KIT_NAME_SIZE;

  bank[KIT_MAGIC_OFFSET] = KIT_MAGIC; // populated marker, stamped last
  return { bank, placed };
}

/** Decode a DPCM byte stream to float32 audio in ~[-1, 1] - the exact inverse of the native ±2 delta
 *  encoder (counter starts 64, ±2 with <127 / >0 guards, LSB-first), for round-trip verification. */
export function dpcmDecode(bytes: Uint8Array): Float32Array {
  const out = new Float32Array(bytes.length * 8);
  let counter = 64;
  for (let b = 0; b < bytes.length; b++) {
    const byte = bytes[b];
    for (let j = 0; j < 8; j++) {
      if (byte & (1 << j)) {
        if (counter < 127) counter += 2;
      } else {
        if (counter > 0) counter -= 2;
      }
      out[b * 8 + j] = (counter - 64) / 63.5;
    }
  }
  return out;
}
````

Create `packages/core/ts/configFields.ts`:

````ts
// The shared zod field builders a role config or a settings block is made of: shape, defaults and clamping in one
// schema, so a config is validated and coerced declaratively (a malformed, partial or stale value snaps to a sane one
// rather than being ad-hoc guarded). They live here because a role's schema is part of the role contract, which lives
// in this package: a console package owns its own role and builds it from these, and a package may not import the
// shell. The write-side half of the shell's config persistence (stringifyConfig) stays there - it is the app's file
// format, not a contract a pack contributes.
//
// Config object schemas are STRICT (z.object - unknown keys stripped). Forward-tolerance across config versions comes
// from field `.default()`s (an old config missing a newly-added field gets the default) plus the version-stamp /
// refuse-newer detection, NOT from passthrough: an older reader never sees a newer writer's fields (they're refused),
// and additive fields are filled by defaults. The only other writer is native C++ (a richer/different shape) - that's
// a translation concern for the real adapter, not loose passthrough. Breaking format changes bump the version and get
// an explicit raw migration at the load seam.
//
// These fields CLAMP rather than throw (a settings knob shouldn't reject an overflow value - it snaps to the nearest
// bound), and default when missing or the wrong type, so `schema.parse({})` yields a full default config.
//
// `z` itself is NOT re-exported. A package that builds a schema imports zod in its own file and declares it in its own
// manifest, which is what lets the boundary check (packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs) see every zod use:
// reached through a re-export here it would be this package's dependency and nobody's refusal. Every module of a build
// resolves `zod` to the one install, so the schemas share one instance whichever file imported it from.

import { z } from "zod";

/** An integer field: missing/non-number → `def`, out-of-range → nearest bound, a fraction → the nearest whole.
 *  A fraction means nothing for any of these fields (a level, an index, a duration, a percentage of unity), and for
 *  `expansionVolume`, the one that reaches the engine as an int param, rounding is also what `ParamType::Int` does.
 *  Where 0 is a sentinel (`zoom` 0 inherits the user default, a controller's `systemId` 0 is the first system, an
 *  ungrouped `linkGroupId` 0), a hand-edited fraction in [0.5, 1) rounds up to 1, the first real value; such a value
 *  is a hand edit the integer contract does not allow. */
export function clampedInt(min: number, max: number, def: number) {
  return z.preprocess((v) => {
    const n = typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) ? Math.round(v) : def;
    return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, n));
  }, z.number());
}

/** A (non-integer) number field: missing/non-number → `def`, out-of-range → bound. */
export function clampedNumber(min: number, max: number, def: number) {
  return z.preprocess((v) => {
    const n = typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : def;
    return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, n));
  }, z.number());
}

/** A boolean field: non-boolean → `def`. */
export function boolField(def: boolean) {
  return z.preprocess((v) => (typeof v === "boolean" ? v : def), z.boolean());
}

/** A string field: non-string → `def`. */
export function stringField(def: string) {
  return z.preprocess((v) => (typeof v === "string" ? v : def), z.string());
}

/** A string-enum field: value must be one of `values`; missing/unknown → `def` (same tolerance as
 *  clampedInt's clamp - a stale/garbage enum snaps to the default rather than failing the parse). */
export function enumField<T extends readonly [string, ...string[]]>(values: T, def: T[number]) {
  return z.enum(values).catch(def).default(def);
}

- [ ] **Step 4: The checker's two new rules**

The fix pass added what a review reproduced: a source file importing its own package's `ts/test/` module is refused (a
test file may use devDependencies, so a published or imported test module hands them to whoever imports it), and an
`exports` entry may publish only what lies inside the package's `ts/` and is not a test module - a literal target
outside `ts/`, a pattern whose `*` can name one, a pattern that can name a test module, and a target naming no file
each get their own sentence. The unused-dependency warning learned that a declared `typescript` a package's
`typecheck` script runs counts as used, which is why the nine packages' new `typescript` declarations do not warn.
Each new rule's fixture is a tree that breaks exactly that rule and nothing else (`fixtures/source-into-test`, and
`fixtures/exports/{zeta, eta, missing}`), and its case asserts the whole `refused:` list, so a rule that refused twice
or not at all fails it: that is the red, since a rule and its fixture land together. And the generator reads a
contribution's module through the manifest's `exports` (the key whose target is the file), refusing one the package
does not publish, plus a manifest whose `name` is not its directory's and a contributing package the shell does not
declare; and the fixture tree's `retroplug` manifest declares the packages its app modules import, which every
existing case now depends on.

- [ ] **Step 6: The bundlers' options, pinned**

`tools/ts-options.js` is the options every artifact-producing bundle states, and each call site passes it as esbuild's
`tsconfigRaw`: `tools/build-session.js` (the script-node bundle, the render worker, the CLI dispatcher and its
sessions, the script test bundle: on), `tools/build-controlplane.js` (on), `tools/build-cli-sdk.mjs` (on),
`tools/build-ts-stripper.mjs` (off), `tools/bundle-native-test.mjs` (off) and the device-pack toolchain
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs`: off). `tools/build-ui.js` names no pin and keeps discovery, with
the reason written into the file: its modules come from the shell's tsconfig (`target: ES2020`, so a class field is
assigned) and `lv_binding_js`'s (no target, so define semantics with esbuild's `__publicField` helper), and one pin
would change how every dpf.js component class initialises. `tsconfig.base.json` no longer carries `alwaysStrict` and
`packages/retroplug/tsconfig.json` no longer opts back in: the base says what `tsc` accepts and nothing else.
`pico/n8-host/exporter-stale.sh` names `tools/ts-options.js` and each pack manifest as inputs, and says the tsconfigs
are not inputs, because the toolchain pins its options.

Create `tools/ts-options.js`:

````js
// The TypeScript options the bundled artifacts of this repo are compiled with, spelled out so that the bytes a bundle
// carries never depend on which tsconfig.json esbuild happened to find.
//
// esbuild reads the NEAREST tsconfig.json above each entry point when a build names none, so the compiler options of
// whatever package an entry lives in decide the output of a bundle that gets embedded in a binary or shipped to a
// consumer. One option shows up in the output as bytes directly: `alwaysStrict` makes esbuild head an iife bundle with
// a `"use strict";` directive, which is inside a script pack's bytecode (the packbytes and device-image legs are that
// byte proof) and inside every iife bundle the native build embeds. A pack whose package does not extend the
// workspace's tsconfig.base.json, or a later edit to that base, would then move those bytes with no bundler edit at
// all. So each build names the options it compiles with, and no bundle's bytes are anyone's tsconfig accident.
//
// What is pinned is what esbuild reads out of a tsconfig and nothing else: `target` (every build already passes it to
// esbuild itself; naming it here keeps the class-field lowering of a bundle fixed) with the `useDefineForClassFields`
// the ES2020 target implies, and `alwaysStrict`, which each caller states because the bundles genuinely differ - the
// iife bundles built from the shell's TS carry the directive today, and the device packs, which their toolchain wraps
// in a directive of their own, carry exactly one.
//
// A package's own tsconfig.json stays what `tsc` checks that package with; this file decides only what a bundler emits.
// That separation is why tsconfig.base.json sets no `alwaysStrict` at all (its `strict` implies one for the type
// checker, which changes no bytes): a bundle's directive is spelled here, so a compiler-settings edit moves no pack's
// and no bundle's bytes. The remaining typechecking options (`noUnusedLocals`, `lib`, `types`) change no output either,
// and nothing here resolves a module: a build that needs an alias passes it to esbuild as `alias`
// (tools/esbuild-shared.js), and no bundled module reaches a tsconfig `paths` entry.
function tsOptions({ alwaysStrict = false } = {}) {
    return {
        compilerOptions: {
            target: "ES2020",
            useDefineForClassFields: false,
            alwaysStrict,
        },
    };
}

module.exports = { tsOptions };
````

-//   "instant"  - unbounded and delivered immediately. The DEFAULT, and what every existing test was
-//                written against: nothing can ever be lost and a pushed chunk is readable at once.
-//   "hardware" - 2048 bytes deep, dropping when full, delivered at the wire's ~150 KB/s. Both of
-//                those hide bug classes when they are absent: a ROM that cannot lose a byte never has
-//                its recovery path exercised, and one handed a whole chunk atomically is never
-//                starved mid-structure the way a real wire starves it.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/_coreRoles.ts`:

````ts
// The two core-config "system" roles, for the tests that want a registry holding just those. They are
// @retroplug/sameboy's and @retroplug/mesen's own (each package's app module contributes it to the product's registry,
// which buildAppRegistry builds); a test that is about one role's config, or about the graph that config feeds,
// registers the roles here rather than the whole app's registry, so a feature role's schema cannot leak into what it
// asserts.
import type { RoleRegistry } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { SAMEBOY_ROLE } from "@retroplug/sameboy";
import { MESEN_ROLE } from "@retroplug/mesen";

/** Register SameBoy's and Mesen's roles, in the order the product's registry takes them. */
export function registerCoreRoles(registry: RoleRegistry): void {
  registry.registerRole(SAMEBOY_ROLE);
  registry.registerRole(MESEN_ROLE);
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/bundleInputs.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The driver behind test/script/bundle-no-zod.test.ts: builds the script-node bundle the way
// packages/native/cmake/bundles.cmake builds it (tools/build-session.js with its own options, an iife) and prints one
// JSON line - the modules that went in, the bundle's size, and the modules the product's packages contribute as their
// `app` member. Those are the role registrations, each built on zod, and the bundle must carry none of them: reading
// them from the manifests is what makes a cart package that contributes a role denied here the moment it is listed in
// the product, with no edit to the test. A package's `protocol` member is deliberately NOT among them: those are script
// nodes, which the bundle exists to carry (the test asserts core's midiRoute.ts is in it).
//
// The paths are printed as esbuild's metafile spells them - relative to this process's working directory, which is
// packages/retroplug when the test suite runs - so the test compares like with like.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { bundleInputs } from "../../../../tools/build-session.js";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = resolve(HERE, "../../../..");

/** Every `retroplug.app` member in the desktop product's packages, as a path from the working directory. */
function appModules() {
  const products = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(REPO, "package.json"), "utf8")).retroplug.products.desktop;
  if (!Array.isArray(products)) throw new Error(`${REPO}/package.json has no retroplug.products.desktop list`);
  const out = [];
  for (const name of products) {
    const dir = resolve(REPO, "packages", name);
    const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(dir, "package.json"), "utf8"));
    const app = manifest?.retroplug?.app;
    if (typeof app !== "string") continue;
    out.push(relative(process.cwd(), resolve(dir, app)).split(sep).join("/"));
  }
  return out;
}

const built = bundleInputs("src/script/bundle.ts", "iife");
console.log(JSON.stringify({ inputs: built.inputs, bytes: built.bytes, appModules: appModules() }));
````

+// The script-node bundle's inputs, size and the packages' contributed role modules, built and listed by
+// test/script/bundleInputs.mjs (the suite runs from packages/retroplug, which is where that driver resolves its entry).
+async function scriptBundle(): Promise<{ inputs: string[]; bytes: number; appModules: string[] }> {
+  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "test/script/bundleInputs.mjs"], {
+    stdout: "pipe",
+    stderr: "pipe",
+  });
   // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
   const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);

+  return JSON.parse(out) as { inputs: string[]; bytes: number; appModules: string[] };
 }

- [ ] **Step 8: The C++ side: the `[settings]` oracle's sources, and the native check's last doors**

`packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake` globs `packages/*/ts/**/*.ts` (test files excluded), appends the shell's
`settingsEnums.ts`, `systemSettings.ts` and `buildGraph.ts`, sorts them and passes one comma-joined
`RP_SETTINGS_TS_PATHS`; `SystemNode.test.cpp`'s `tsValues` reads all of them and requires exactly one declaration (a
second fails the case, naming both files), and `tsNumbers`/`tsRange`/`tsConstant`/`tsConstructFields` take a path
**fragment** resolved against the same list. The five per-file `RP_*_TS_PATH` defines are gone, so a Task 5 package
that takes an enum changes no CMakeLists. `cmake/packages.cmake`'s gatherer gains `ALIAS` resolution,
`COMPILE_OPTIONS` and `INTERFACE_COMPILE_OPTIONS` (the `-I` family, a relative one read from the target's
`SOURCE_DIR`) and the unjudged refusal; the gather project's three new cases and its two manifests hold them. Six C++
comments that named `packages/retroplug/src/coreRoles.ts` as a range's authority name the two packages' `app.ts`.

+# The shell imports every workspace package it declares BY PACKAGE NAME (its sources, and the modules the generator
+# writes into packages/retroplug/src/generated), and pnpm links a workspace package into the shell's node_modules only
+# when the shell declares it. A missing link is esbuild's bare "Could not resolve" with no hint of the cause, so
+# configure says what to do: the declaration and the link must both be there, for every @retroplug/* the shell names -
+# including a package that contributes no registration and so never appears in a product list, which the generator's
+# own refusal only covers for packages that contribute.
+file(READ "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/package.json" _rp_shell_manifest_json)

+             "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/package.json")

+if(_rp_shell_error)
+    message(FATAL_ERROR "packages/retroplug/package.json has no dependencies object (${_rp_shell_error}): every "
+                        "@retroplug/* it imports must be declared, or this configure cannot check the links")
+endif()
+# Read from the packages' side, because CMake's JSON reader enumerates an array's members and not an object's keys:
+# every workspace package, kept when the shell declares it. A declaration of a name that is no package here is the
+# boundary check's to refuse.
+file(GLOB _rp_workspace_dirs LIST_DIRECTORIES TRUE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/*")
+foreach(_rp_dir IN LISTS _rp_workspace_dirs)
+    if(NOT EXISTS "${_rp_dir}/package.json")
+        continue()
+    endif()
+    get_filename_component(_rp_declared "${_rp_dir}" NAME)
+    string(JSON _rp_dep_kind ERROR_VARIABLE _rp_dep_error TYPE "${_rp_shell_manifest_json}"
+           dependencies "@retroplug/${_rp_declared}")
+    if(_rp_dep_error)
+        continue()
     endif()
+    if(NOT EXISTS "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/node_modules/@retroplug/${_rp_declared}")
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "packages/retroplug/node_modules/@retroplug/${_rp_declared} is missing: the shell "
+                            "declares and imports @retroplug/${_rp_declared} by name, so run `pnpm install`")
+    endif()
+endforeach()
+
+# Every package a desktop product lists is registered by iterating that list, so a new package's registration is its
+# manifest plus the list entry and no CMake edit a third-party pack can forget. The two lists around it are the packages
+# no product lists and a device build needs, placed where the loop's own ordering requires them: the node SDK first,
+# because every other package's library is built on it; a device host's own I/O (rp.device.midi-in, the plan exporter's
+# and the devices') and the device check's test types (rp.devtest.plan) last, because registering a script pack needs
+# the
+# MicroQuickJS host the graph-runtime package adds. packages/native is in the product list and registers the node types
+# not yet carved into packages of their own (sameboy, mesen, host.io, launchpad); its targets are defined below, where
+# the root adds the engine's own tree. @retroplug/tracker is in neither list: it contributes no registration of any
+# kind, only modules the shell and the cart packages import, so CMake is never told about it.
+set(_rp_first_packages node-sdk)          # first: every other package's library is built on it
+set(_rp_last_packages device-io devtest)  # after the list: a script pack needs graph-runtime's host
+foreach(_rp_package IN LISTS _rp_first_packages RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES _rp_last_packages)
+    retroplug_package(${_rp_package})
 endforeach()
 
+# The device check's case generator, a desktop tool listing what the RP2350 check registers (a device product of the
+# packages above); the check itself is packages/graph-runtime/device-check, a Pico SDK project of its own.
+add_subdirectory(packages/graph-runtime/device-check/cases "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/device-check/cases")
+# The plan exporter, the desktop tool a device image's build runs to embed its built-in plan (a device product of the

+add_subdirectory(packages/graph-runtime/export-plan "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/export-plan")
+# Every package's native targets, held to what its manifest declares, deferred to the end of this directory as the

+# later package or to the shell below would pass unseen. Every target is attributed to the package whose directory holds
+# its SOURCE_DIR, so a helper no manifest names is still that package's.
+cmake_language(DEFER DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}" CALL retroplug_check_package_boundaries)

                     if(NOT TARGET ${_item})

+                    # it

+            # A -I (or -isystem, or MSVC's /I) in the compile options is an include directory by another door, so it is
+            # judged like one. What a generator expression hides is left alone HERE, unlike a link or a directory:
+            # this property legitimately holds configuration expressions (retroplug_package_library's
+            # $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:/bigobj>), and refusing those would refuse a build that declared nothing.
+            set(_flag_dir "")

+                get_target_property(_value ${_target} ${_property})

+                endif()

+                        set(_dir "${_item}")
+                        set(_flag_dir "")

+                        set(_dir "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
+                    elseif(_item MATCHES "^-isystem(.+)$")
+                        set(_dir "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
+                    elseif(_item MATCHES "^/I(.+)$")
+                        set(_dir "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
+                    elseif(_item STREQUAL "-I" OR _item STREQUAL "-isystem" OR _item STREQUAL "/I")
+                        set(_flag_dir TRUE)
+                        continue()
+                    else()
+                        continue()
+                    endif()

+                    # directory is: the one below the target's own, which no package of another's can be.
+                    if(NOT IS_ABSOLUTE "${_dir}")

PNG editing loop: `--dump-chr x.png` / `--patch-chr 0 x.png` round-trip an editable grayscale tile grid (`packages/retroplug/src/risa/rom/chrImage.ts`) - edit a glyph, push it live. `--dump-chr x.png --color [--palette N]` renders the game's REAL colours via the live sniffer palette |

 | **Load FPGA mapper core** | `CMD_FPG_USB` (0x1E) / `ed_cmd_fpg_init_usb` | swap cartridge hardware personality over USB |
 | **RTC get/set/cal** | `CMD_RTC_GET/SET/CAL` (0x14/15/21) | read/set the console clock |
 | ✅ **Device info** | `CMD_SYS_INF` (0x26) + `CMD_GET_VDC` (0x13) | DONE + HW-verified (`n8-load --info`, hwtest `info`, `packages/n8/ts/sysInfo.ts`): serial, boot/sw/hw versions, MCU-core build date, flash size, counters, board voltages, and NES-vs-Famicom form factor. This unit: EverDrive-N8 PRO, NES, boot 0x0100, core 2025-11-08 |

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f1pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf build-box/pio/n8_host.elf build-box/native/n8_host.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f1-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f1-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  4 2026/" /tmp/f1-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f1-img.bin'`

A different count or hash is a finding to report.

  catch. @retroplug/tracker is in neither list: it contributes no registration, only modules, so it would be a
  manifest member with nothing to say.

  stays in the shell undivided: every entry point is orchestration over a running system (readSram, resolveSavPath,

  schedules are already SongCatalog's, which did move. Its header says so, with the names it needs.

  the shared formats and risa's own bank counts and kit-metadata mirror; kit split between the 8 KB bank codec and
  risa's mirror-row derivation. src/ritAssetsRole.ts becomes tracker/ts/ritAssets.ts: the override shape, its schema
  and its patcher, naming no cart. src/bliptoaster/rom/rom.ts now reads those from @retroplug/tracker and nothing from
  risa, so stage 5 can move BlipToaster with no dependency on risa; risa's barrel re-exports the formats for its own
  consumers, which the rule permits.
- @retroplug/core gains ts/configFields.ts: the clampedInt, clampedNumber, boolField, stringField and enumField
  builders, moved out of the shell's src/configSchema.ts, which keeps only stringifyConfig (the app's file formatter).
  A role's schema is part of the role contract, and a package may not import the shell. `z` is NOT re-exported: a
  package that builds a schema imports zod in its own file and declares it in its own manifest (sameboy, mesen and
  tracker now do), which is what lets the boundary check see every zod use, and every module of a build resolves the
  one install anyway.
- settingsEnums.ts is the app's own enums only - layout, controller target, audio routing, LSDj sync mode - and
  re-exports nothing at all: the project schema, buildGraph's knob tables, the parameter map, the stores and the menu
  cyclers name @retroplug/sameboy, @retroplug/mesen and core's midiRouting for what a package owns. n8Link moved with
  the role that carries it: it configures the emulated N8 FIFO and reliable link inside Mesen's NES core, which
  @retroplug/n8's package is the physical twin of.
- The C++ oracle that reads the TS sources followed the enums, and its source list stopped being a list of defines:
  tests.cmake globs every package's TS (the app's settingsEnums, systemSettings and buildGraph beside them) into one
  RP_SETTINGS_TS_PATHS, the oracle reads whichever source declares a name, and a name two sources spell fails the case
  naming both - the stale copy of a moved enum is the thing that would otherwise be compared silently. The range
  checks name a source by a path fragment out of that same list. It failed red, 11 assertions, before the move. Six
  native comments that named src/coreRoles.ts as a range's authority name the package now.
- Bundled artifacts now name the TypeScript options they compile with (tools/ts-options.js, passed to esbuild as
  tsconfigRaw by tools/build-session.js, build-controlplane.js, build-cli-sdk.mjs, build-ts-stripper.mjs,
  bundle-native-test.mjs and the device-pack toolchain), so no pack's or bundle's bytes depend on whichever
  tsconfig.json esbuild discovers for the entry: the same option that decides whether an iife carries a "use strict"
  directive, which is inside a script pack's bytecode. tsconfig.base.json therefore sets no alwaysStrict of its own
  (strict still implies one for the type checker, which emits nothing) and the shell's opt-back-in is gone. The UI
  bundle is the one that keeps discovery, and says why: its modules come from this workspace and from dpf.js's
  lv_binding_js, whose tsconfigs differ in class-field semantics, so one pin would flatten a real difference.
- The boundary check (packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs) gained the two rules the split makes live: a
  non-test file of a package may not import (or reference) a test file of its own package, because a test file's
  devDependencies would reach that package's importers; and a package may publish only what lies inside its ts/ and is
  not a test module, judged for exports patterns as well as literals. The native gatherer sees through ALIAS targets
  and refuses a package's include directory or source handed over by INTERFACE_COMPILE_OPTIONS (-I/-isystem//I) or an
  unresolvable generator expression, so a helper of one package can no longer be reached by another without a
  declaration; three gather fixtures cover them, and source paths are compared lexically, not through symlinks.
  test/script/bundle-no-zod denies every role module the desktop product's manifests contribute as their app member
  rather than a hardcoded pair, so a cart package that contributes a role is denied the moment it is listed.
- Every package declares the compiler the shell uses (typescript ^7.0.2 as a devDependency, so pnpm -r typecheck runs
  one tsc everywhere) and configure refuses a stale checkout over every @retroplug/* the shell declares, not only the
  packages that contribute a registration. pico/n8-host/exporter-stale.sh names the pack inputs the split created:
  each script pack's manifest, the pack toolchain and tools/ts-options.js; the tsconfigs are deliberately off the list,
  since a pack is bundled with options that file spells.
- test/risa/chrImage.test.ts, wholly about the moved CHR codec, moves to packages/tracker/ts/test (slug
  risa/chrImage -> tracker/chrImage, its case count unchanged); test/system-settings/registry.test.ts gains the
  registration-order case (8 -> 9).

### Task 5: the six cart packages, their tests and goldens, and the docs

Design sections 2 and 8's fifth commit. Every console and cart whose code is TypeScript gets its own package: `lsdj`
with its codecs, model, HD model, playback, ROM asset codec, runtime reader, catalogs, roles, kit format, ROM provider
and its two protocol nodes; `mgb` with its role, provider and `rp.mgb.midi`; `risa` with its codec, ROM layer, runtime
reader, catalogs, three roles, DMC kit format and `rp.risa.sync`; `smsggdj` with its battery codec, detector, runtime
reader, catalogs, integration (with the inline `songWrites` a live load pokes into work RAM), role and `rp.sms.sync`;
`bliptoaster` widened from its device pack to the cart's whole app half; and `n8` widened to the `nes-n8-midi` role and
`rp.n8.midi-to-fifo` beside the ROM provider it took in Task 3's fix pass. Their tests and goldens move with them.

**The registration order is the last thing the product list cannot express, and it does not have to.** A dependency
order of packages cannot reproduce today's interleaved role list (`risa-sync` sits between `n8`'s and `smsggdj`'s
roles), so the first cut of this task added an explicit `retroplug.order` to the root `package.json`. The review found it
dropped a registration silently, and that only a ROM provider's place is observable; so the order is the product list,
the NES provider moved into `n8` (this task's first run, before that package's widening) so no shell block sits in the middle of the
providers, and the generated module refuses a duplicate role kind, kit format id and tracker marker role, which is where
the real hazard was. The role and tracker integration lists' order changes with nothing able to observe it, and the
registry test pins what can be observed: the twelve role kinds as a set, and `defaultRoles` over eight fixtures.

The move count is what makes this task long: a hundred and sixty-five files change directory, and four hundred and
thirty-three files change. It ends with the docs: AGENTS.md's package rule, spec/06 and spec/07, the README, the six
manifests' descriptions, and the design's own sections 1 to 10 corrected in place with section 11 recording the build.

````ts
// LSDj's contribution to the app: its two roles (the sync role whose work is rp.lsdj.sync and rp.lsdj.serial-out, and
// the asset-override role), the ROM provider that attaches them, its Songs/Assets tracker integration and its kit bank
// format. The lists' order within a package is the order they register in where one list carries several.
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import type { RoleType, ConstructCaps } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { ConstructSpec } from "@retroplug/core/constructSpec";
import { z } from "zod";
import { clampedInt, boolField, enumField } from "@retroplug/core/configFields";
import { LSDJ_MODE_VALUES } from "./enums";
import { LSDJ_ASSETS_ROLE } from "./lsdjAssetsRole";
import { LSDJ_ROM_PROVIDER } from "./romProvider";
import { lsdjIntegration } from "./lsdjIntegration";
import { LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT } from "./kitFormat";
// The keys the owner packages add to the contract (their modules augment PackageContributions): type-only, so nothing
// loads at run time.
import type {} from "@retroplug/tracker/packageContributions";
import type {} from "@retroplug/dsp/packageContributions";

// lsdj-sync load-time hook: a fresh LSDj cart with no SRAM runs a 12-15 s cartridge self-test on boot.
// When nothing else will seed the battery (no savestate, no sram blob, no on-disk .sav for native to
// load), hand it a valid empty sav (savFromJson stamps the jk/rb validity markers LSDj checks) so it
// boots straight to the song screen. Additive: return the spec untouched when real save data is present.
const lsdjSeedSav = (spec: ConstructSpec, caps: ConstructCaps): ConstructSpec => {
  const willLoadData = !!spec.stateBytes || !!spec.sramBytes || (spec.savPath != null && caps.fileExists(spec.savPath));
  if (willLoadData) return spec;
  return { ...spec, sramBytes: caps.savFromJson("{}") };
};

export const LSDJ_SYNC_ROLE: RoleType = {
  kind: "lsdj-sync",
  category: "feature",
  // mode: LsdjSyncMode ("off", "midiSync", … "midiOut", "masterSync"). tempoDivisor subdivides the
  // 24-PPQN clock (24/divisor) for MidiSync + MidiSyncArduinoboy; the menu offers 1/2/4/8. autoStart
  // taps START on the host transport rise to auto-arm a SYNC=MIDI (MidiSync) cart, needed for a
  // headless DAW render, off by default so normal MidiSync keeps its manual-arm behaviour. rp.lsdj.sync
  // runs each mode.
  schema: z.object({
    mode: enumField(LSDJ_MODE_VALUES, "midiSync"),
    tempoDivisor: clampedInt(1, 8, 1),
    autoStart: boolField(false),
  }),
  onConstruct: lsdjSeedSav,
};

export default definePackage({
  roles: [LSDJ_SYNC_ROLE, LSDJ_ASSETS_ROLE],
  romProviders: [LSDJ_ROM_PROVIDER],
  trackerIntegrations: [lsdjIntegration],
  kitFormats: [LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT],
});
````

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/kitFormat.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's kit bank format (docs/modular-graph-phase-d2-design.md section 5): a 16 KB bank of up to 15 rotated 4-bit
// samples, each compiled from its source as a chain of offline graph jobs. The shared half of that compile - the window,
// the effects passes, the guard and non-finite refusals, every slot started at once - is @retroplug/dsp/kitJobs'; what
// is here is the slot: an LSDj sample resampled, optionally rotated, quantised to 4 bits and packed as nibbles, then the
// bank assembled by the ROM codec (./rom/buildKit). A kit compiled here is the bank the goldens record, byte for byte.
//
// What a slot is when a chain comes out empty is settled here rather than run, since a job can neither take an input of
// no frames nor record one: a window that is empty (an offset at or past the source's end) is an LSDj slot of no bytes,
// which is also what trimming to whole 32-sample frames leaves of it.
import type { KitCompileResult, KitFormat, KitJobRunner, KitSampleSpec } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitContract";
import { compileSlots, load, recorded, runEffects, type Compiled } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitJobs";
import { quantiseJob, resampleJob, resolveEffects } from "@retroplug/dsp/chain";
import {
  LSDJ_KIT_BITS,
  LSDJ_KIT_RATE,
  LSDJ_MAX_SAMPLE_FRAMES,
  packNibbles,
  resampledLength,
  trimToFrames,
} from "@retroplug/dsp/pack";
import type { OfflineCap } from "@retroplug/core/offlineJob";
import { buildKitBankPlaced } from "./rom/buildKit";
import { KIT_MAX_SAMPLES, KIT_MAX_SAMPLE_SPACE } from "./rom/constants";

/** One sample of an LSDj kit: a source file, a 3-character slot name, an optional source-frame window and an effect
 *  chain. */
export type { KitSampleSpec } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitContract";

/** A whole-kit compile: a 6-char kit name + up to 15 samples. `rotate` = the LSDj 9.2.0+ frame rotation, set from the
 *  target ROM's version (omitted -> true / 9.2.0+). */
export interface KitCompileSpec {
  name: string;
  samples: KitSampleSpec[];
  rotate?: boolean;
}

// The window cap: at most a kit's worth of frames at the kit rate, scaled to the decoded rate in LSDj's own arithmetic
// (float with the ratio first: OfflineJobs' offlineWindow).
const LSDJ_CAP: OfflineCap = { frames: LSDJ_MAX_SAMPLE_FRAMES, rate: LSDJ_KIT_RATE, arithmetic: "float-ratio" };

async function lsdjSlot(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: KitSampleSpec, rotate: boolean): Promise<Compiled> {
  const source = await load(runner, spec, LSDJ_CAP);
  const chain = resolveEffects(spec.effects ?? [], source.rate, true);
  if (source.samples.length === 0) {
    const where = `offset ${spec.offset ?? 0}, at or past the source's ${source.decodedFrames} frames`;
    const empty = `the window holds no frames (${where})`;
    return { bytes: new Uint8Array(0), empty };
  }
  const length = resampledLength(source.samples.length, source.rate, LSDJ_KIT_RATE);
  if (trimToFrames(length) === 0) {
    const empty = `the window resamples to ${length} frames at ${LSDJ_KIT_RATE} Hz, under one 32-sample wave frame`;
    return { bytes: new Uint8Array(0), empty };
  }
  const effected = await runEffects(runner, source, chain);
  const resampled = await recorded(runner, resampleJob(effected, source.rate, LSDJ_KIT_RATE, length), "the resample");
  const quantise = quantiseJob(resampled, LSDJ_KIT_RATE, chain.dither ?? "none", LSDJ_KIT_BITS);
  const levels = await recorded(runner, quantise, "the quantise");
  return { bytes: packNibbles(levels, rotate), empty: null };
}

/** An LSDj kit: the 16 KB bank (its 15 slots, the rest dropped), and each sample's reason. */
export async function compileKit(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: KitCompileSpec): Promise<KitCompileResult> {
  const rotate = spec.rotate ?? true;
  const compile = (s: KitSampleSpec): Promise<Compiled> => lsdjSlot(runner, s, rotate);
  const { results, dropped } = await compileSlots(spec.samples, KIT_MAX_SAMPLES, compile, "LSDj kit");
  const samples = results.map((r, i) => ({ name: spec.samples[i].name, bytes: r.bytes }));
  const { bank, written } = buildKitBankPlaced(spec.name, samples);
  const errors = results.map((r, i): string | null => {
    if (r.error !== null) return r.error;
    const n = r.bytes.length;
    const landed = written[i];
    if (landed === null)
      return `the kit's ${KIT_MAX_SAMPLE_SPACE} bytes of sample space are full, so none of this sample's ${n} ` +
        "bytes fit";
    if (landed < n) return `the kit's sample space ran out, so ${landed} of this sample's ${n} bytes fit`;
    return null;
  });
  return { bytes: bank, errors: [...errors, ...dropped] };
}

/** The LSDj kit: a 16 KB bank of 15 rotated 4-bit samples. */
export const LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT: KitFormat<KitCompileSpec> = { id: "lsdj", compile: compileKit };
````

````ts
// LSDj's tracker integration: its Songs catalog (the battery's projects, the shared song menu and recent-song names) and
// its Assets catalog (the ROM's replaceable kits/palettes/fonts), with the ROM name read from the cartridge title. The
// contract is @retroplug/tracker's; the catalog objects are this package's, beside the codecs they read.
import type { TrackerIntegration } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerIntegration";
import { identifyLsdj } from "./runtime/identify";
import { lsdjSongCatalog } from "./lsdjSongCatalog";
import { lsdjAssetCatalog } from "./lsdjAssetCatalog";

export const lsdjIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "lsdj",
  label: "LSDj",
  markerRole: "lsdj-sync",
  songs: lsdjSongCatalog,
  assets: lsdjAssetCatalog,
  romName: (rom) => {
    const v = identifyLsdj(rom); // parses the GB cartridge title at 0x134 ("LSDJ-Vx.y.z")
    return v ? `LSDj v${v.major}.${v.minor}.${v.patchLabel}${v.build ? ` ${v.build}` : ""}` : null;
  },
};
````

````ts
// LSDj's ROM provider: a stock or Arduinoboy build gets the lsdj-sync role (defaulting to MidiSync) plus the
// lsdj-assets role that carries any non-destructive kit/palette/font overrides (empty until the user replaces one).
// Matched on the cartridge title, case-insensitively, so both "LSDj-v9.4.2" and older "LSDJ" uppercase titles match
// the same prefix.
import type { RomProvider } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { cartridgeTitle } from "@retroplug/sameboy/cartridge";
import { LsdjSyncMode } from "./enums";

export const LSDJ_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) =>
  cartridgeTitle(rom.header).startsWith("LSDJ")
    ? [
        { kind: "lsdj-sync", config: { mode: LsdjSyncMode.MidiSync } },
        { kind: "lsdj-assets", config: { overrides: [] } },
      ]
    : [];
````

// mGB's ROM provider: the embedded synth (marker "mgb") or a file-backed mGB cart gets the `mgb` MIDI-to-serial
// passthrough role. Matched by ROM identity, as every provider is: the embedded ROM's bytes never reach TS, so its
// marker alone says which cart it is.
import type { RomProvider } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { cartridgeTitle } from "@retroplug/sameboy/cartridge";

export const MGB_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) =>
  rom.embeddedRom === "mgb" || cartridgeTitle(rom.header).startsWith("MGB") ? [{ kind: "mgb", config: {} }] : [];
````

The kit-compile driver splits here, which is prototype question 4's answer: the chain half (`load`, `recorded`,
`runEffects`, `settle`, `compileSlots`, `guardWords`, `NO_SLOT_REASON` and their types) is `@retroplug/dsp/kitJobs`, a
slot's source spec is dsp's kit contract, `OfflineRunError` is `@retroplug/core/offlineJob`, and each cart's format is
its own `ts/kitFormat.ts` with the specs it compiles. `src/kit/compile.ts` becomes a door that re-exports.

Create `packages/dsp/ts/kitJobs.ts`:

````ts
// What a kit compiler does around a format's own slot, apart from the slot itself
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-d2-design.md section 5): decode and window a source natively, run its effect chain and each
// pass, hold every pass and every slot to "the bytes are the kernels'", and start every honoured slot's chain at once
// so the engine's offline pool runs them in parallel. A cart's format (its package's kitFormat.ts) supplies the slot:
// which chain to resolve, what to quantise and how to pack it, then assembles the bank.
//
// A slot that fails is left empty and the kit still compiles, never refusing the kit as a whole: a source that cannot be
// read or decoded, a window with a sample that is not finite, a spec the nodes cannot carry (chain.ts's refusals), a
// pass that makes a sample that is not finite, or a pass a node's guard stepped into (`recorded` says why that last one
// keeps every compiled kit byte-identical). Empty means no bytes: LSDj's assembler still names the slot, with a length
// of zero; risa's leaves its index entry empty.
import { OfflineRunError, type OfflineCap, type OfflineRunRequest } from "@retroplug/core/offlineJob";
import { KitSpecError, effectsJob, loadJob, windowFrames, type SlotChain } from "./chain";
import type { KitJobRunner, KitSampleSpec } from "./kitContract";

/** What a slot the compiler left empty with no reason is: the compile result's contract makes that a compiler bug, not
 *  a full bank, so a caller's message says so instead of guessing at a cause. */
export const NO_SLOT_REASON = "the compiler left the slot empty without saying why";

/** A slot's source, decoded and windowed natively. */
export interface Source {
  samples: Float32Array;
  rate: number;
  decodedFrames: number;
}

// The slot's source, decoded and windowed natively. A window holding a sample that is not finite is refused: a NaN or
// an infinity is where a node's guard and the kit kernel part ways, so no compile could promise the kit path's bytes.
// A file that cannot be read or decoded is the job's failure, said without the job's own input numbering.
export async function load(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: KitSampleSpec, cap: OfflineCap): Promise<Source> {
  let result;
  try {
    result = await runner.offlineRun(
      loadJob(spec.path, windowFrames(spec, "offset"), windowFrames(spec, "length"), cap),
    );
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof OfflineRunError) throw new Error(e.message.replace(/^input 0: /, ""));
    throw e;
  }
  const [report] = result.inputs;
  if (report.nonFinite) throw new KitSpecError(`${spec.path} has a sample that is not finite in the window`);
  return { samples: result.buffers[0].samples, rate: report.decodedRate, decodedFrames: report.decodedFrames };
}

// What a guard's report says, in a slot error's words: which node stepped in, and what that means for the pass.
function guardWords(reason: string, times: number): string {
  const count = `${times} time${times === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
  if (reason.startsWith("rp.dsp.biquad")) return `overflowed a filter, which rp.dsp.biquad reset (${count})`;
  if (reason.startsWith("rp.dsp.dither"))
    return `overflowed the dither's state, which rp.dsp.dither restarted (${count})`;
  return `needed a node's guard (${count}: ${reason})`;
}

// A pass run, and the one buffer it recorded; refused (naming the pass, `what`) when a node's guard stepped in during
// the run or the recording holds a sample that is not finite.
//
// The two refusals keep a compiled kit byte-identical to the kit kernels when a finite source overflows somewhere in
// the chain. Every pass's input is finite: the window's, checked at the load, or an earlier pass's recording, checked
// here. In an effects pass, a gain or a normalise has neither a guard nor a clamp, so a non-finite value it makes goes
// on to the recording or to a biquad; the biquad clamps its output, the one place an effects pass could hide such a
// value, but a non-finite input or output leaves its state non-finite, which its guard resets and reports. The
// resample has no guard or clamp either, so what it makes is in its recording. The quantise and the DMC encode only
// ever get checked inputs: the dither reports any restart, and on finite input the dither's quantiser and the DPCM
// encoder are their kernels. So a node departs from its kernel only where a guard reports it (rp.host.guards/1, counted
// in the completion), and every other non-finite value is in a recording; refusing both refuses every way a kit could
// part from the kernels, as a source with a non-finite sample is refused. Native reads the non-finite flag as it copies
// the buffer out; a scan here would cost several times the job in a script runtime (380 ms of a 450 ms compile of
// fifteen capped 96 kHz slots).
export async function recorded(runner: KitJobRunner, request: OfflineRunRequest, what: string): Promise<Float32Array> {
  const result = await runner.offlineRun(request);
  if (result.guardsFired > 0) throw new KitSpecError(`${what} ${guardWords(result.guardReason, result.guardsFired)}`);
  const [buffer] = result.buffers;
  if (buffer.nonFinite) throw new KitSpecError(`${what} made a sample that is not finite`);
  return buffer.samples;
}

// The effects passes in order, each recording the whole buffer for the next.
export async function runEffects(runner: KitJobRunner, source: Source, chain: SlotChain): Promise<Float32Array> {
  let buffer = source.samples;
  for (const segment of chain.segments) {
    const what = `the pass running effect${segment.effects.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} ${segment.effects.join(", ")}`;
    buffer = await recorded(runner, effectsJob(buffer, source.rate, segment), what);
  }
  return buffer;
}

/** A slot's compiled bytes, and why they are empty when they are without a failure. */
export interface Compiled {
  bytes: Uint8Array;
  empty: string | null;
}

/** One slot's outcome: its bytes (none on a failure) and the reason it has none or is short, if it has one. */
export interface SlotResult {
  bytes: Uint8Array;
  error: string | null;
}

/** A slot compiled to its bytes or to the reason it could not be: a failure never fails the kit. */
export async function settle(compile: Promise<Compiled>): Promise<SlotResult> {
  try {
    const { bytes, empty } = await compile;
    return { bytes, error: empty };
  } catch (e) {
    return { bytes: new Uint8Array(0), error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) };
  }
}

/** Each honoured slot's chain started at once; a sample past the bank's `capacity` is not compiled (the bank layout
 *  holds that many), and its reason says so. */
export async function compileSlots<S>(
  samples: readonly S[],
  capacity: number,
  compile: (s: S) => Promise<Compiled>,
  bankName: string,
): Promise<{ results: SlotResult[]; dropped: string[] }> {
  const results = await Promise.all(samples.slice(0, capacity).map((s) => settle(compile(s))));
  const why = `the ${bankName} bank holds ${capacity} samples, so this one is dropped`;
  return { results, dropped: samples.slice(capacity).map(() => why) };
}
````
