Create `packages/sameboy/ts/cartridge.ts`:

````ts
// The Game Boy cartridge title field (0x134..0x143), decoded the way a ROM provider matches a cart by its title: to
// uppercase ASCII, stopping at the first NUL. A provider reads the ROM's header prefix, never the whole ROM, so this is
// all a headless cart identity is.
//
// It is deliberately not @retroplug/lsdj's runtime/identify's romTitle: that one stops at the first non-printable byte
// (a 15-character title runs up to 0x142, leaving 0x143's CGB flag, which must not reach a version parse), where a
// prefix match reads through it. Two decoders, each for the one question it answers.

/** The cartridge title, uppercased, up to the first NUL. */
export function cartridgeTitle(header: Uint8Array): string {
  let s = "";
  for (let i = 0x134; i < 0x144 && i < header.length; i++) {
    const c = header[i];
    if (c === 0) break;
    s += String.fromCharCode(c);
  }
  return s.toUpperCase();
}
````

````ts
// risa's contribution to the app: its three roles (the menu-gating marker, the asset-override role and the sync role
// whose work is rp.risa.sync), the ROM provider that attaches them, its Songs/Assets tracker integration and its DMC
// kit bank format. A list's order within the package is the order it registers in where one list carries several;
// where it sits among the product's other lists is the product list's order, which is behaviour for the ROM
// providers alone (roles, kit formats and integrations are looked up by kind, id or an exclusive marker).
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { RISA_ROLE, RISA_SYNC_ROLE } from "./risaRole";
import { RISA_ASSETS_ROLE } from "./risaAssetsRole";
import { RISA_ROM_PROVIDER } from "./romProvider";
import { risaIntegration } from "./risaIntegration";
import { RISA_KIT_FORMAT } from "./kitFormat";
// The keys the owner packages add to the contract (their modules augment PackageContributions): type-only, so nothing
// loads at run time.
import type {} from "@retroplug/tracker/packageContributions";
import type {} from "@retroplug/dsp/packageContributions";

export default definePackage({
  roles: [RISA_ROLE, RISA_ASSETS_ROLE, RISA_SYNC_ROLE],
  romProviders: [RISA_ROM_PROVIDER],
  trackerIntegrations: [risaIntegration],
  kitFormats: [RISA_KIT_FORMAT],
});
````

Create `packages/risa/ts/kitFormat.ts`:

````ts
// risa's kit bank format (docs/modular-graph-phase-d2-design.md section 5): an 8 KB bank of 16 PAL DPCM samples, each
// compiled from its source as a chain of offline graph jobs. The shared half of that compile - the window, the effects
// passes, the guard and non-finite refusals, every slot started at once - is @retroplug/dsp/kitJobs'; what is here is
// the slot: a sample resampled to the PAL DPCM rate, encoded to 7-bit levels (optionally peak-normalised) and packed
// with the DPCM header, then the bank assembled by the ROM codec (@retroplug/tracker/nes/kitBank). BlipToaster's kits
// are the same 8 KB format, which its package assembles from the same helpers.
//
// What a slot is when its window comes out empty is settled here rather than run, since a job can neither take an
// input of no frames nor record one.
import type { KitCompileResult, KitFormat, KitJobRunner, KitSampleSpec } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitContract";
import { compileSlots, load, recorded, runEffects, type Compiled } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitJobs";
import { dpcmJob, resampleJob, resolveEffects } from "@retroplug/dsp/chain";
import { DMC_MAX_BYTES, packDmc, palDmcRate, resampledLength } from "@retroplug/dsp/pack";
import type { OfflineCap } from "@retroplug/core/offlineJob";
import { assembleKitBankPlaced, type AssembleSlot } from "@retroplug/tracker/nes/kitBank";
import { KIT_SAMPLE_REGION, KIT_SLOT_COUNT } from "@retroplug/tracker/nes/constants";

/** One source sample for the risa DMC compiler: a kit sample plus the PAL DPCM playback-rate index (0..15,
 *  default 12), a loop flag, and whether to peak-normalize into the 7-bit domain (default true). */
export interface RisaDmcSampleSpec extends KitSampleSpec {
  rate?: number;
  loop?: boolean;
  normalize?: boolean;
}

/** A whole risa DMC kit compile: a 6-char kit name + up to 16 samples. */
export interface RisaKitCompileSpec {
  name: string;
  samples: RisaDmcSampleSpec[];
}

// The DMC window cap: at most a kit's worth of frames at the rate, scaled to the decoded rate in double with the
// product first (OfflineJobs' offlineWindow).
const dmcCap = (rate: number): OfflineCap => ({ frames: DMC_MAX_BYTES * 8, rate, arithmetic: "double-scale" });

async function dmcSlot(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: RisaDmcSampleSpec): Promise<Compiled> {
  const rate = palDmcRate(spec.rate ?? 12);
  const source = await load(runner, spec, dmcCap(rate));
  const chain = resolveEffects(spec.effects ?? [], source.rate, false);
  const length = resampledLength(source.samples.length, source.rate, rate);
  if (length === 0) return { bytes: packDmc([]), empty: null };
  const effected = await runEffects(runner, source, chain);
  const resampled = await recorded(runner, resampleJob(effected, source.rate, rate, length), "the resample");
  const levels = await recorded(runner, dpcmJob(resampled, rate, spec.normalize ?? true), "the DMC encode");
  return { bytes: packDmc(levels), empty: null };
}

/** A risa DMC kit: the 8 KB bank (its 16 slots, the rest dropped), and each sample's reason. */
export async function compileDmc(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: RisaKitCompileSpec): Promise<KitCompileResult> {
  const compile = (s: RisaDmcSampleSpec): Promise<Compiled> => dmcSlot(runner, s);
  const { results, dropped } = await compileSlots(spec.samples, KIT_SLOT_COUNT, compile, "risa kit");
  const slots = results.map((r, i): AssembleSlot | null => {
    const s = spec.samples[i];
    return r.bytes.length ? { dpcm: r.bytes, rate: (s.rate ?? 12) & 0x0f, loop: s.loop ?? false, name: s.name } : null;
  });
  const { bank, placed } = assembleKitBankPlaced(spec.name, slots);
  const errors = results.map((r, i): string | null => {
    if (r.error !== null) return r.error;
    if (placed[i]) return null;
    return `this sample's ${r.bytes.length} bytes do not fit the ${KIT_SAMPLE_REGION}-byte sample region after the ` +
      "slots before it";
  });
  return { bytes: bank, errors: [...errors, ...dropped] };
}

/** The risa DMC kit: an 8 KB bank of 16 DPCM samples, which BlipToaster's kits are too. */
export const RISA_KIT_FORMAT: KitFormat<RisaKitCompileSpec> = { id: "risa", compile: compileDmc };
````

````ts
// risa's tracker integration: what a risa system's Songs and Assets menus are built over. The song catalog reads the
// RSav battery (its records, the working song and the catalog layout), the asset catalog reads the ROM's replaceable
// kits, themes and fonts, and the two ROM questions - which build this is ("RISA V<major>.<minor>.<patch>" in the PRG)
// and whether it can be driven (only the versions with a bundled RAM layout can) - come from the runtime reader.
//
// The menus themselves are the shell's (ui/screens/menu); an integration is the data they are built from, resolved by
// a system's markerRole (the shell's trackerRegistry).
import type { TrackerIntegration } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerIntegration";
import { risaSongCatalog } from "./risaSongCatalog";
import { risaAssetCatalog } from "./risaAssetCatalog";
import { identifyRisaVersion } from "./runtime/identify";
import { resolveRisaLayout } from "./runtime/layout";

export const risaIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "risa",
  label: "Risa",
  markerRole: "risa",
  songs: risaSongCatalog,
  assets: risaAssetCatalog,
  romName: (rom) => {
    const v = identifyRisaVersion(rom); // scans the PRG for the ASCII "RISA V<major>.<minor>.<patch>" marker
    return v ? `risa v${v}` : null;
  },
  // Only versions with a bundled RAM layout (2.2.0 / 2.2.1 / 2.3.0) are driveable; an unknown / unmarked version
  // resolves no layout. See supportedRisaVersions() in ./runtime/layout.
  isVersionSupported: (rom) => resolveRisaLayout(identifyRisaVersion(rom)) !== null,
};
````

````ts
// risa's two config-free feature roles: the `risa` marker role, which gates the Songs and Assets menus
// (`sys.roles.find(r => r.kind === "risa")`, exactly as `lsdj-sync` gates the LSDj menu), and `risa-sync`, whose work
// is the rp.risa.sync protocol node (./risaSyncNode) that drives the cart's N8-FIFO host-sync receive path from the
// DAW transport. Both are control-plane registrations only (the package's app module, ts/app.ts); the ROM provider
// that attaches them by ROM identity is ./romProvider.
//
// The asset-override role is its own module (./risaAssetsRole), because it carries an onConstruct hook.
import { z } from "zod";
import type { RoleRegistry, RoleType } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";

/** The `risa` marker role: a risa cart's presence, and nothing else. */
export const RISA_ROLE: RoleType = { kind: "risa", category: "feature", schema: z.object({}) };

/** risa-sync: the DAW transport into a sync-capable risa cart's host-sync receive path. No config. */
export const RISA_SYNC_ROLE: RoleType = { kind: "risa-sync", category: "feature", schema: z.object({}) };

/** Register the marker role into `registry`, for a registry a test or a host builds by hand. */
export function registerRisaRole(registry: RoleRegistry): void {
  registry.registerRole(RISA_ROLE);
}
````

Create `packages/risa/ts/romProvider.ts`:

````ts
// risa's ROM provider: a risa cart gets the `risa` marker role that gates the Songs menu and the `risa-assets` role
// holding its non-destructive theme/font/kit overrides, plus - on a sync-capable build - the `risa-sync` role that
// drives its N8-FIFO host-sync receive path. Detected by the iNES 2.0 header fingerprint (MMC5 + 64 KB PRG-NVRAM),
// since NES ROMs carry no title field; the "RISAxyz" marker in the header prefix says the build is sync-capable, and
// older risa builds without it are unaffected.
import type { RoleInstance, RomProvider } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { isRisaRomHeader, isRisaSyncRom } from "./romDetect";

export const RISA_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom): RoleInstance[] => {
  if (rom.platform !== "nes" || !isRisaRomHeader(rom.header)) return [];
  const roles: RoleInstance[] = [{ kind: "risa", config: {} }, { kind: "risa-assets", config: { overrides: [] } }];
  if (isRisaSyncRom(rom.header)) roles.push({ kind: "risa-sync", config: {} });
  return roles;
};
````

````ts
// smsggdj's contribution to the app: the `sms-sync` role whose work is rp.sms.sync, the ROM provider that attaches it
// (by the cart's build marker, not by platform) and its Songs/Assets tracker integration. The role's schema is what the
// stores parse, persist and hand the node as its settings; `machine` is additive with a default, so no migration step:
// an existing project stamped before it existed parses as "sms", which is what those projects were.
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import type { RoleType } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { z } from "zod";
import { SMSGGDJ_ROM_PROVIDER } from "./romProvider";
import { smsggdjIntegration } from "./smsggdjIntegration";
// The key the tracker package adds to the contract (its module augments PackageContributions): type-only, so nothing
// loads at run time.
import type {} from "@retroplug/tracker/packageContributions";

// sms-sync: clocks smsggdj by holding a 2-bit counter on controller port 2 (TR + TH) at 24 PPQN, or a Game Gear's EXT
// port for `machine: "gg"`. `rp.sms.sync` runs it (./smsSyncNode).
export const SMS_SYNC_ROLE: RoleType = {
  kind: "sms-sync",
  category: "feature",
  schema: z.object({ machine: z.enum(["sms", "gg"]).default("sms") }),
};

export default definePackage({
  roles: [SMS_SYNC_ROLE],
  romProviders: [SMSGGDJ_ROM_PROVIDER],
  trackerIntegrations: [smsggdjIntegration],
});
````

````ts
// smsggdj's ROM provider: the cart gets the `sms-sync` role that clocks it from the DAW transport. Matched on the
// ROM's build MARKER, not the platform: on SMS the transport rides Player 2's button lines, so attaching this to every
// SMS cart would inject phantom presses into any game that reads the port.
//
// `machine` carries the wire format, because the two builds read different pins - SMS controller port 2 ($DD)
// versus the Game Gear EXT parallel port ($01). Both work: the GG path needs Mesen to honour the $02 direction
// mask on an $01 read rather than looping the port straight back, which is the vendored SmsMemoryManager edit.
import type { RomProvider } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { isSmsggdjRom } from "./smsSync";

export const SMSGGDJ_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) => {
  if ((rom.platform !== "sms" && rom.platform !== "gg") || !isSmsggdjRom(rom.header)) return [];
  return [{ kind: "sms-sync", config: { machine: rom.platform } }];
};
````

````diff
--- a/packages/risa/ts/fixtures.ts
+++ b/packages/risa/ts/fixtures.ts
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
-// GENERATED — do not hand-edit. See scripts note in packages/retroplug/scripts (M1 risa save codec).
+// The base64 table below is GENERATED - do not hand-edit it (see the scripts note in packages/retroplug/scripts, the
+// M1 risa save codec). The synthetic ROM builders at the end of the file are hand-written.
 // Real risa battery saves, base64-embedded, for the risa catalog-reader golden tests.
 //   v2_blumarbl    — blumarbl.srm migrated to the current v2 catalog (0x8000) via
 //                    tools/migrate_legacy_sav.py; oracle-verified by tools/analyze_save.py
@@ -6,7 +7,11 @@
 //   legacy_4xtreme — website/play/demos/infu-4xtreme.srm, the legacy v1 catalog (0x6000).
 //   multi_legacy   — tools/tests/test_save_corruption_fixture.sav; a valid 5-record legacy
 //                    catalog (multi-record walk coverage; payloads are the corruption target, not the headers).
-// Goldens live in ./golden/<key>.json, produced by risa's own SaveImage reader.
+// Goldens live in ./test/golden/<key>.json, produced by risa's own SaveImage reader.
+//
+// Below them are the synthetic risa ROMs the ROM codec and provider tests read (risaRom, risaRomFull,
+// setRisaVersionMarker): a cart's theme table, kit bank and version marker are that cart's own knowledge, so the
+// builders live here rather than in the shell's fixture tree, which re-exports them.
 
 const B64: Record<string, string> = {
   v2_blumarbl: "",
@@ -37,3 +42,70 @@ export const FIXTURE_KEYS = Object.keys(B64) as FixtureKey[];
 export function savBytes(key: FixtureKey): Uint8Array {
   return decodeB64(B64[key]);
 }
+
+/** A minimal ROM carrying the real risa 2.2.1 iNES 2.0 header fingerprint (NES 2.0, mapper 5 / MMC5,
+ *  battery, 512 KB PRG, 32 KB CHR, 64 KB PRG-NVRAM) so the risa ROM provider attaches the `risa` role.
+ *  Detection reads only the header; the body is padding (the mock ignores it). */
+export function risaRom(): Uint8Array {
+  const b = new Uint8Array(0x200); // >= ROLE_HEADER_LEN so the provider sees a full header prefix
+  b.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a, 0x20, 0x04, 0x53, 0x08, 0x00, 0x00, 0xa0], 0);
+  setRisaVersionMarker(b, "2.2.1"); // a supported version, so the tracker submenu is live (not greyed out)
+  return b;
+}
+
+/** Write the ASCII "RISA V<version>" marker identifyRisaVersion() scans for, at a fixed PRG offset (0x20,
+ *  clear of the iNES header). Lets a synthetic fixture pose as a specific risa app version. */
+export function setRisaVersionMarker(rom: Uint8Array, version: string): void {
+  const s = `RISA V${version}`;
+  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) rom[0x20 + i] = s.charCodeAt(i);
+}
+
+/** A full-size synthetic risa ROM (16 + 512 KB PRG + 32 KB CHR = 0x88010) carrying a THEME_META_MAGIC
+ *  theme table (16 distinct themes) in the fixed bank + a distinct CHR region per font slot. Enough for
+ *  RisaRom.isRisa + theme/font read/patch (the on-ROM asset layer); the PRG body is otherwise zeros. */
+export function risaRomFull(): Uint8Array {
+  const PRG = 0x80000; // 32 × 16 KB
+  const CHR = 0x8000; // 4 × 8 KB
+  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x10 + PRG + CHR);
+  rom.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a, 0x20, 0x04, 0x53, 0x08, 0x00, 0x00, 0xa0], 0);
+  setRisaVersionMarker(rom, "2.2.1"); // a supported version → the tracker submenu is live
+
+  // Theme table at the fixed bank (lastPrgBank 63): magic + 16×7 records + 16×4 names.
+  const fixedOffset = 0x10 + 63 * 0x2000;
+  rom.set([0xa5, 0x5a, 0x54, 0x48, 0x4d, 0x45], fixedOffset);
+  const recordBase = fixedOffset + 6;
+  const namesOff = recordBase + 16 * 7;
+  for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
+    for (let r = 0; r < 7; r++) rom[recordBase + i * 7 + r] = (i * 7 + r) & 0x3f; // distinct role indices
+    const nm = `TH${i.toString(16).toUpperCase()}`.slice(0, 4);
+    for (let c = 0; c < 4; c++) rom[namesOff + i * 4 + c] = c < nm.length ? nm.charCodeAt(c) : 0x20; // space-padded
+  }
+
+  // CHR: 4 × 8 KB slots, each filled with a slot-distinct pattern.
+  const chrOffset = 0x10 + PRG;
+  for (let s = 0; s < 4; s++)
+    for (let b = 0; b < 0x2000; b++) rom[chrOffset + s * 0x2000 + b] = (s * 13 + b) & 0xff;
+
+  // Kit region: banks 31..62 (kitOffset 0x3E010). One populated kit in slot 0 ("TEST" with a "KIK" sample),
+  // the other 15 index entries marked empty (0xFF). All 32 banks are otherwise zero (unpopulated).
+  const kitOffset = 0x10 + 31 * 0x2000;
+  rom[kitOffset + 0] = 0xff; // slot-0 DPCM data (1 byte)
+  rom.fill(0x20, kitOffset + 0x1ed0, kitOffset + 0x1ed0 + 16 * 3); // sample-names region = spaces
+  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("TEST").entries()) rom[kitOffset + 0x1ec0 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // kit name
+  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("KIK").entries()) rom[kitOffset + 0x1ed0 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // sample 0 name
+  rom.set([0, 0, 12, 0], kitOffset + 0x1f00); // index[0] = [addr 0, lenReg 0, rate 12, flags 0]
+  for (let slot = 1; slot < 16; slot++) rom[kitOffset + 0x1f00 + slot * 4] = 0xff; // empty index entries
+  rom[kitOffset + 0x1f40] = 0xa5; // populated magic
+
+  // Kit-metadata mirror, placed at 0x30000 — PAST both hint offsets (0x20010, 0x10010) so the locator's
+  // bounded scan is exercised (as in real risa 2.2.1). Magic + kit_names[32][16] + kit_sample_names[32][48]
+  // + kit_slot_present[32][16]; slot 0 mirrors the populated kit, the present sub-table is all 0/1.
+  const metaBase = 0x30000;
+  rom.set([0xa5, 0x5a, 0x4b, 0x54, 0x4d, 0x45], metaBase);
+  const base = metaBase + 6;
+  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("TEST").entries()) rom[base + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // kit_names[0]
+  rom.fill(0x20, base + 512, base + 512 + 48); // kit_sample_names[0] = spaces
+  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("KIK").entries()) rom[base + 512 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0);
+  rom[base + 512 + 1536] = 1; // kit_slot_present[0][0] = 1 (the rest stay 0)
+  return rom;
+}
````

````ts
// BlipToaster's contribution to the app: the two roles its ROM provider attaches, the provider itself and its
// asset-only tracker integration. BlipToaster is an NES MIDI synth rather than a tracker, so it has no song battery:
// the roles are a marker (which build of the cart, for the parameter map) and the cart's ROM overrides, and the
// integration carries assets alone.
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { BLIPTOASTER_ROLE } from "./bliptoasterRole";
import { BLIPTOASTER_ASSETS_ROLE } from "./bliptoasterAssetsRole";
import { BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PROVIDER } from "./romProvider";
import { blipToasterIntegration } from "./bliptoasterIntegration";
// The keys the owner packages add to the contract (their modules augment PackageContributions): type-only, so nothing
// loads at run time.
import type {} from "@retroplug/tracker/packageContributions";

export default definePackage({
  // The marker role first, then the asset role: the provider attaches them in that order, and the app's role list
  // registers every kind where buildAppRegistry always did.
  roles: [BLIPTOASTER_ROLE, BLIPTOASTER_ASSETS_ROLE],
  // The provider attaches both roles by the ROM's baked marker, in the order the registry offers it.
  romProviders: [BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PROVIDER],
  // The Songs and Assets menus' consoles, in the order they are searched (a system's first match wins).
  trackerIntegrations: [blipToasterIntegration],
});
````

````ts
// BlipToaster's tracker integration: an NES MIDI synth (not a tracker), so it has NO song battery - only ROM assets (a
// baked DMC kit plus the CHR font). An asset-only integration: `songs` is omitted, so only the asset submenus are built.
// The `bliptoaster` marker role its provider attaches is the menu's gate, exactly as "risa" gates risa's menu.
import type { TrackerIntegration } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerIntegration";
import { bliptoasterAssetCatalog } from "./bliptoasterAssetCatalog";
import { blipToasterInfo, BLIPTOASTER_MARKER } from "./romDetect";

export const blipToasterIntegration: TrackerIntegration = {
  id: "bliptoaster",
  label: "BlipToaster",
  markerRole: "bliptoaster",
  assets: bliptoasterAssetCatalog,
  romName: (rom) => {
    const info = blipToasterInfo(rom); // decoded bliptoaster SIG block (null when the marker is absent)
    if (!info) return null;
    return `${BLIPTOASTER_MARKER} v${info.semver.join(".")}`; // marker doubles as the display name
  },
};
````

````ts
// Synthetic BlipToaster ROM images: a full-size flat NROM cart and the banking (mapper 69, FME-7) shape the shipped
// builds use, each carrying the "bliptoaster" marker at the ROM head, the interleaved theme table + settings block and
// a populated DMC kit + CHR fonts. A fixture is the cart's own knowledge (its SIG block, its table stride, its bank
// geometry), so it lives here and the shell's test tree re-exports it for its store, menu and registry tests.

const CHR_BANK_BYTES = 0x2000; // one font slot = one 8 KB CHR bank

// The real ROM's 16 theme names, in table order (`g_themeTable`, the bliptoaster repo's src/core/sys.c). The
// fixtures carry them verbatim so a menu / inventory test asserts the labels a user actually reads.
const BLIPTOASTER_THEME_NAMES = [
  "DFLT", "DARK", "NEON", "LITE", "CRT ", "ICE ", "FIRE", "GB  ",
  "AQUA", "MONO", "PLSM", "MTRX", "FOG ", "SUN ", "MOON", "AMBR",
];

/** The BlipToaster theme table as the ROM bakes it: the `\xA5\x5ATHME` magic, then `count` INTERLEAVED entries
 *  of [7 role bytes + a 4-char name] - 11 bytes each, the name right behind its own record. That stride is
 *  BlipToaster's own and is NOT risa's layout (16 records, then 16 names), so a fixture written risa-style
 *  reads only entry 0 correctly. Role 0 (bg) is per-slot so a test can tell the entries apart; slot 0 is the
 *  real DFLT's 0x0D/0x30. `count` below 16 is for the table-bound check. */
export function blipToasterThemeTable(count = 16): Uint8Array {
  const ENTRY = 7 + 4;
  const out = new Uint8Array(6 + count * ENTRY);
  out.set([0xa5, 0x5a, 0x54, 0x48, 0x4d, 0x45], 0); // THEME_META_MAGIC
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const off = 6 + i * ENTRY;
    out.set([0x0d + i, 0x30, 0x00, 0x10, 0x30, 0x21, 0x11], off); // bg, normal, shaded, alternate, status, cursor, selection
    for (const [k, c] of Array.from(BLIPTOASTER_THEME_NAMES[i % 16]).entries()) out[off + 7 + k] = c.charCodeAt(0);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The baked settings block as the ROM bakes it (src/core/settings.c): the `\xA5\x5ASETT` magic, the format
 *  byte, then the rig fields; +8 and +13..15 stay reserved 0xFF. Defaults are the power-on ones the ROM bakes -
 *  all zero except `ppu`, which is 1 (the screen draws), i.e. the block of a ROM straight out of the build. */
export function blipToasterSettingsBlock(
  fields: { version?: number; baseChannel?: number; ppu?: number; velCurve?: number; theme?: number; font?: number } = {},
): Uint8Array {
  const out = new Uint8Array(16);
  out.set([0xa5, 0x5a, 0x53, 0x45, 0x54, 0x54], 0); // "\xA5\x5ASETT"
  out[6] = fields.version ?? 1;
  out[7] = fields.baseChannel ?? 0;
  out[8] = 0xff; // reserved - held the default kit slot before the kit became CC-only
  out[9] = fields.ppu ?? 1; // the one non-zero power-on default: PPU enabled
  out[10] = fields.velCurve ?? 0;
  out[11] = fields.theme ?? 0;
  out[12] = fields.font ?? 0;
  out.fill(0xff, 13);
  return out;
}

// The theme table + settings block, spliced at `at` exactly as the ROM lays them out: ADJACENT, the settings
// magic starting the byte after the table's last entry. That adjacency is load-bearing for the fixtures - it
// is the case that bounds the theme count (countThemes stops on the $A5 it cannot read as a palette index),
// so a fixture that left slack there would not exercise it.
function splicePrgBlocks(rom: Uint8Array, at: number, themeCount = 16): void {
  const table = blipToasterThemeTable(themeCount);
  rom.set(table, at);
  rom.set(blipToasterSettingsBlock(), at + table.length);
}

/** A full-size synthetic BlipToaster ROM (16 + 32 KB PRG + 8 KB CHR = 0xA010, NROM) carrying the "bliptoaster"
 *  marker at the ROM head + the theme table + settings block + one populated DMC kit at $C000 (PRG offset
 *  0x4000) + a distinct CHR font region. The flat single-kit, single-font cart: every SHIPPED build banks
 *  (see blipToasterMultiKitRom), so this one exists to hold the NROM read path - capacity 1, fonts 1 - which
 *  BlipToasterRom still derives from the header rather than assuming. */
export function blipToasterRom(): Uint8Array {
  const PRG = 0x8000; // 2 × 16 KB (NROM, 32 KB)
  const CHR = 0x2000; // 1 × 8 KB
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x10 + PRG + CHR);
  rom.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a], 0); // "NES\x1A"
  rom[4] = 0x02; // 2 × 16 KB PRG
  rom[5] = 0x01; // 1 × 8 KB CHR
  rom[6] = 0x01; // vertical mirroring, mapper 0 (NROM)

  // The BlipToaster SIG block at the ROM head ($8000 = file offset 0x10), as the SIG segment bakes it:
  // the "bliptoaster" marker (also the display name) + semver(0.1.0).
  const MARK = "bliptoaster";
  for (let i = 0; i < MARK.length; i++) rom[0x10 + i] = MARK.charCodeAt(i);
  let p = 0x10 + MARK.length;
  rom[p++] = 0x00; rom[p++] = 0x01; rom[p++] = 0x00; // semantic version 0.1.0

  // The theme table + settings block in the code region (before the kit at 0x4010), at a fixed offset for
  // tests - the code region is exactly where the ROM puts them, and where both magic scans look.
  splicePrgBlocks(rom, 0x100);

  // One populated DMC kit at $C000 (PRG offset 0x4000): a "TEST" kit with a "KIK" sample-0 name, one index
  // entry, the other 15 empty (0xFF), and the 0xA5 populated magic - the same 8 KB bank layout risa uses.
  const kitOffset = 0x10 + 0x4000;
  rom[kitOffset + 0] = 0xff; // slot-0 DPCM data (1 byte)
  rom.fill(0x20, kitOffset + 0x1ed0, kitOffset + 0x1ed0 + 16 * 3); // sample-names region = spaces
  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("TEST").entries()) rom[kitOffset + 0x1ec0 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // kit name
  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("KIK").entries()) rom[kitOffset + 0x1ed0 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // sample 0 name
  rom.set([0, 0, 12, 0], kitOffset + 0x1f00); // index[0] = [addr 0, lenReg 0, rate 12, flags 0]
  for (let slot = 1; slot < 16; slot++) rom[kitOffset + 0x1f00 + slot * 4] = 0xff; // empty index entries
  rom[kitOffset + 0x1f40] = 0xa5; // populated magic

  // CHR: one 8 KB font slot, filled with a distinct pattern (for font read/patch tests).
  const chrOffset = 0x10 + PRG;
  for (let b = 0; b < CHR; b++) rom[chrOffset + b] = (b * 7 + 3) & 0xff;
  return rom;
}

/** A full-size synthetic BlipToaster BANKING ROM - the SHIPPED shape: 16 + 256 KB PRG + 32 KB CHR, mapper 69
 *  (FME-7), carrying the "bliptoaster" marker + the 16-entry theme table + the settings block + one populated
 *  DMC kit in slot 0, with slots 1..15 reserved (unpopulated). The banking header (PRG 16 × 16 KB, mapper != 0)
 *  drives BlipToasterRom.kitBankCapacity() to 16, so the assets menu goes addable/16-slot; the 4 declared CHR
 *  banks give it the real build's 4 fonts. Kit slot k sits at PRG offset 0x4000 + k*0x2000 (banks 2..17), and
 *  the geometry throughout is the real cfg/nes-banked.cfg's. */
export function blipToasterMultiKitRom(): Uint8Array {
  const PRG = 0x40000; // 16 × 16 KB (256 KB banking build)
  const CHR = 0x8000; // 4 × 8 KB - one font each
  const rom = new Uint8Array(0x10 + PRG + CHR);
  rom.set([0x4e, 0x45, 0x53, 0x1a], 0); // "NES\x1A"
  rom[4] = 0x10; // 16 × 16 KB PRG (256 KB)
  rom[5] = 0x04; // 4 × 8 KB CHR (32 KB)
  rom[6] = 0x51; // vertical mirroring, mapper 69 low nibble (Sunsoft 5B / FME-7)
  rom[7] = 0x40; // mapper 69 high nibble

  const MARK = "bliptoaster"; // marker (also the display name)
  for (let i = 0; i < MARK.length; i++) rom[0x10 + i] = MARK.charCodeAt(i);
  let p = 0x10 + MARK.length;
  rom[p++] = 0x00; rom[p++] = 0x01; rom[p++] = 0x00; // semantic version 0.1.0

  // Theme table + settings block in the code region (same placement as blipToasterRom()).
  splicePrgBlocks(rom, 0x100);

  // Kit slot 0 populated at bank 2 (PRG offset 0x4000). Slots 1..15 (banks 3..17) stay unpopulated (their
  // magic byte is 0x00 ≠ 0xA5), matching the real ROM's reserved-fill banks.
  const kitOffset = 0x10 + 0x4000;
  rom[kitOffset + 0] = 0xff; // slot-0 DPCM data (1 byte)
  rom.fill(0x20, kitOffset + 0x1ed0, kitOffset + 0x1ed0 + 16 * 3); // sample-names region = spaces
  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("TEST").entries()) rom[kitOffset + 0x1ec0 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // kit name
  for (const [i, c] of Array.from("KIK").entries()) rom[kitOffset + 0x1ed0 + i] = c.charCodeAt(0); // sample 0 name
  rom.set([0, 0, 12, 0], kitOffset + 0x1f00); // index[0] = [addr 0, lenReg 0, rate 12, flags 0]
  for (let slot = 1; slot < 16; slot++) rom[kitOffset + 0x1f00 + slot * 4] = 0xff; // empty index entries
  rom[kitOffset + 0x1f40] = 0xa5; // populated magic (slot 0 only)

  // CHR: 4 × 8 KB font slots, each a distinct pattern whose FIRST byte is its own slot index - so a test that
  // reads or splices a font can say which bank it got rather than just "some 8 KB".
  const chrOffset = 0x10 + PRG;
  for (let b = 0; b < CHR; b++) rom[chrOffset + b] = (b * 7 + 3) & 0xff;
  for (let slot = 0; slot * CHR_BANK_BYTES < CHR; slot++) rom[chrOffset + slot * CHR_BANK_BYTES] = slot;
  return rom;
}
````

````ts
// BlipToaster's ROM provider: what gives a BlipToaster cartridge its feature roles. Attached by ROM identity, not by
// platform, because the cart is an NES ROM with no distinguishing iNES header - the "bliptoaster" ASCII marker baked
// into its head is the only thing that says what it is (romDetect.ts). It has no song battery, so there is no song
// marker either; the tracker integration is asset-only.
import type { RoleInstance, RomProvider } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { isBlipToasterRomHeader, blipToasterChip } from "./romDetect";

// BlipToaster (the NES MIDI synth) -> the `bliptoaster` marker role that gates its asset menu, plus the
// `bliptoaster-assets` role holding non-destructive DMC-kit/CHR-font ROM overrides.
export const BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom): RoleInstance[] =>
  rom.platform === "nes" && isBlipToasterRomHeader(rom.header)
    ? [
        { kind: "bliptoaster", config: { chip: blipToasterChip(rom.header) } },
        { kind: "bliptoaster-assets", config: { overrides: [] } },
      ]
    : [];
````

Create `packages/n8/ts/app.ts`:

````ts
// n8's contribution to the app: the `nes-n8-midi` role, the ROM provider that attaches it, and the rp.n8.midi-to-fifo
// node that runs it. The role is the always-on host-MIDI passthrough every NES gets, since the FIFO the node writes to
// is always there and a ROM that ignores $40F0 is undisturbed. That is also why the match is the PLATFORM and not a
// ROM marker.
//
// The role's schema is empty: the passthrough has no settings, and what it does is the node's (./n8MidiToFifoNode).
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import type { RoleType, RomProvider } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { z } from "zod";

// NES host-MIDI: routed MIDI to the core's MIDI input (to the always-attached N8 FIFO). A role on a Mesen NES, and
// feature-category with no config, so an existing project parses unchanged.
export const NES_N8_MIDI_ROLE: RoleType = { kind: "nes-n8-midi", category: "feature", schema: z.object({}) };

/** Any NES ROM -> the always-on host-MIDI passthrough to its core. */
export const NES_N8_MIDI_ROM_PROVIDER: RomProvider = (rom) =>
  rom.platform === "nes" ? [{ kind: "nes-n8-midi", config: {} }] : [];

export default definePackage({
  roles: [NES_N8_MIDI_ROLE],
  romProviders: [NES_N8_MIDI_ROM_PROVIDER],
});
````

The shell contributes nothing to the app's lists any more: `src/app.ts` is `definePackage({ roles: [], romProviders:
[], trackerIntegrations: [], kitFormats: [] })`, kept rather than deleted because the generated registry reads it and
because an empty contribution is where F3's controller adds its roles; `src/script/shellNodes.ts` carries
`controllerSessionNode` alone (label 22, until F3) and the shell manifest's `protocol.roles` is `{}`;
`src/dspRoles.ts`, `src/romProviderList.ts` and `src/tracker/integrations.ts` are deleted (they were single-cart files
by the end), and so are `src/lsdjSav.ts` and `src/risaRole.ts`. `src/tracker/index.ts`, `src/trackerRegistry.ts`,
`src/romProviders.ts` and `src/appHost.ts` keep their doors, re-exporting the packages' objects, with their comments
corrected; `kit/compile.ts` and `audioDriver.ts` are re-export doors only. Every other module in the shell names its
package.

````diff
-  if (reason.startsWith("rp.dsp.biquad")) return `overflowed a filter, which rp.dsp.biquad reset (${count})`;
-  if (reason.startsWith("rp.dsp.dither"))
-    return `overflowed the dither's state, which rp.dsp.dither restarted (${count})`;
-  return `needed a node's guard (${count}: ${reason})`;
-}
-
-// A pass run, and the one buffer it recorded; refused (naming the pass, `what`) when a node's guard stepped in during
-// the run or the recording holds a sample that is not finite.
-//
-// The two refusals keep a compiled kit byte-identical to the kit kernels when a finite source overflows somewhere in
-// the chain. Every pass's input is finite: the window's, checked at the load, or an earlier pass's recording, checked
-// here. In an effects pass, a gain or a normalise has neither a guard nor a clamp, so a non-finite value it makes goes
-// on to the recording or to a biquad; the biquad clamps its output, the one place an effects pass could hide such a
-// value, but a non-finite input or output leaves its state non-finite, which its guard resets and reports. The
-// resample has no guard or clamp either, so what it makes is in its recording. The quantise and the DMC encode only
-// ever get checked inputs: the dither reports any restart, and on finite input the dither's quantiser and the DPCM
-// encoder are their kernels. So a node departs from its kernel only where a guard reports it (rp.host.guards/1, counted
-// in the completion), and every other non-finite value is in a recording; refusing both refuses every way a kit could
-// part from the kernels, as a source with a non-finite sample is refused. Native reads the non-finite flag as it copies
-// the buffer out; a scan here would cost several times the job in a script runtime (380 ms of a 450 ms compile of
-// fifteen capped 96 kHz slots).
-async function recorded(runner: KitJobRunner, request: OfflineRunRequest, what: string): Promise<Float32Array> {
-  const result = await runner.offlineRun(request);
-  if (result.guardsFired > 0) throw new KitSpecError(`${what} ${guardWords(result.guardReason, result.guardsFired)}`);
-  const [buffer] = result.buffers;
-  if (buffer.nonFinite) throw new KitSpecError(`${what} made a sample that is not finite`);
-  return buffer.samples;
-}
-
-// The effects passes in order, each recording the whole buffer for the next.
-async function runEffects(runner: KitJobRunner, source: Source, chain: SlotChain): Promise<Float32Array> {
-  let buffer = source.samples;
-  for (const segment of chain.segments) {
-    const what = `the pass running effect${segment.effects.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} ${segment.effects.join(", ")}`;
-    buffer = await recorded(runner, effectsJob(buffer, source.rate, segment), what);
-  }
-  return buffer;
-}
-
-// A slot's compiled bytes, and why they are empty when they are without a failure.
-interface Compiled {
-  bytes: Uint8Array;
-  empty: string | null;
-}
-
-async function lsdjSlot(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: KitSampleSpec, rotate: boolean): Promise<Compiled> {
-  const source = await load(runner, spec, LSDJ_CAP);
-  const chain = resolveEffects(spec.effects ?? [], source.rate, true);
-  if (source.samples.length === 0) {
-    const where = `offset ${spec.offset ?? 0}, at or past the source's ${source.decodedFrames} frames`;
-    const empty = `the window holds no frames (${where})`;
-    return { bytes: new Uint8Array(0), empty };
-  }
-  const length = resampledLength(source.samples.length, source.rate, LSDJ_KIT_RATE);
-  if (trimToFrames(length) === 0) {
-    const empty = `the window resamples to ${length} frames at ${LSDJ_KIT_RATE} Hz, under one 32-sample wave frame`;
-    return { bytes: new Uint8Array(0), empty };
-  }
-  const effected = await runEffects(runner, source, chain);
-  const resampled = await recorded(runner, resampleJob(effected, source.rate, LSDJ_KIT_RATE, length), "the resample");
-  const quantise = quantiseJob(resampled, LSDJ_KIT_RATE, chain.dither ?? "none", LSDJ_KIT_BITS);
-  const levels = await recorded(runner, quantise, "the quantise");
-  return { bytes: packNibbles(levels, rotate), empty: null };
-}
-
-async function dmcSlot(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: RisaDmcSampleSpec): Promise<Compiled> {
-  const rate = palDmcRate(spec.rate ?? 12);
-  const source = await load(runner, spec, dmcCap(rate));
-  const chain = resolveEffects(spec.effects ?? [], source.rate, false);
-  const length = resampledLength(source.samples.length, source.rate, rate);
-  if (length === 0) return { bytes: packDmc([]), empty: null };
-  const effected = await runEffects(runner, source, chain);
-  const resampled = await recorded(runner, resampleJob(effected, source.rate, rate, length), "the resample");
-  const levels = await recorded(runner, dpcmJob(resampled, rate, spec.normalize ?? true), "the DMC encode");
-  return { bytes: packDmc(levels), empty: null };
-}
-
-interface SlotResult {
-  bytes: Uint8Array;
-  error: string | null;
-}
-
-async function settle(compile: Promise<Compiled>): Promise<SlotResult> {
-  try {
-    const { bytes, empty } = await compile;
-    return { bytes, error: empty };
-  } catch (e) {
-    return { bytes: new Uint8Array(0), error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) };
-  }
-}
-
-// Each honoured slot's chain started at once; a sample past the bank's `capacity` is not compiled (the bank layout
-// holds that many), and its reason says so.
-async function compileSlots<S>(samples: readonly S[], capacity: number, compile: (s: S) => Promise<Compiled>,
-                               bankName: string): Promise<{ results: SlotResult[]; dropped: string[] }> {
-  const results = await Promise.all(samples.slice(0, capacity).map((s) => settle(compile(s))));
-  const why = `the ${bankName} bank holds ${capacity} samples, so this one is dropped`;
-  return { results, dropped: samples.slice(capacity).map(() => why) };
-}
-
-/** An LSDj kit: the 16 KB bank (its 15 slots, the rest dropped), and each sample's reason. */
-export async function compileKit(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: KitCompileSpec): Promise<KitCompileResult> {
-  const rotate = spec.rotate ?? true;
-  const compile = (s: KitSampleSpec): Promise<Compiled> => lsdjSlot(runner, s, rotate);
-  const { results, dropped } = await compileSlots(spec.samples, KIT_MAX_SAMPLES, compile, "LSDj kit");
-  const samples = results.map((r, i) => ({ name: spec.samples[i].name, bytes: r.bytes }));
-  const { bank, written } = buildKitBankPlaced(spec.name, samples);
-  const errors = results.map((r, i): string | null => {
-    if (r.error !== null) return r.error;
-    const n = r.bytes.length;
-    const landed = written[i];
-    if (landed === null)
-      return `the kit's ${KIT_MAX_SAMPLE_SPACE} bytes of sample space are full, so none of this sample's ${n} ` +
-        "bytes fit";
-    if (landed < n) return `the kit's sample space ran out, so ${landed} of this sample's ${n} bytes fit`;
-    return null;
-  });
-  return { bytes: bank, errors: [...errors, ...dropped] };
-}
-
-/** A risa DMC kit: the 8 KB bank (its 16 slots, the rest dropped), and each sample's reason. */
-export async function compileDmc(runner: KitJobRunner, spec: RisaKitCompileSpec): Promise<KitCompileResult> {
-  const compile = (s: RisaDmcSampleSpec): Promise<Compiled> => dmcSlot(runner, s);
-  const { results, dropped } = await compileSlots(spec.samples, KIT_SLOT_COUNT, compile, "risa kit");
-  const slots = results.map((r, i): AssembleSlot | null => {
-    const s = spec.samples[i];
-    return r.bytes.length ? { dpcm: r.bytes, rate: (s.rate ?? 12) & 0x0f, loop: s.loop ?? false, name: s.name } : null;
-  });
-  const { bank, placed } = assembleKitBankPlaced(spec.name, slots);
-  const errors = results.map((r, i): string | null => {
-    if (r.error !== null) return r.error;
-    if (placed[i]) return null;
-    return `this sample's ${r.bytes.length} bytes do not fit the ${KIT_SAMPLE_REGION}-byte sample region after the ` +
-      "slots before it";
-  });
-  return { bytes: bank, errors: [...errors, ...dropped] };
-}
-
 export type { KitFormat } from "@retroplug/dsp/kitContract";
-
-/** The LSDj kit: a 16 KB bank of 15 rotated 4-bit samples. */
-export const LSDJ_KIT_FORMAT: KitFormat<KitCompileSpec> = { id: "lsdj", compile: compileKit };
-
-/** The risa DMC kit: an 8 KB bank of 16 DPCM samples, which BlipToaster's kits are too. */
-export const RISA_KIT_FORMAT: KitFormat<RisaKitCompileSpec> = { id: "risa", compile: compileDmc };
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The shell's tests**

The tests the design said move did, with two exceptions the build forced: a test that drives the shell's registry
stays (`test/risa/detect.test.ts`, `test/bliptoaster/romDetect.test.ts`, `test/system-settings/*`, and the catalog
tests, which resolve through `trackerRegistry` and `render`), and `canonical-json`, `graph-document` and `conformance`
stay for their native golden. The tests that moved are the carts' codec, ROM and runtime tests, the protocol node
units (`lsdjSync`, `lsdjSerialOut`, `lsdjArduinoboy`, `mgbMidi`, `risaSync`, `smsSync`, `n8MidiToFifo`) and the carts'
goldens; the three LSDj node and decoder tests moved in this task's fix pass after a first pass left them in the
shell. A cart's synthetic ROM fixtures are its package's when the shell's tests read them (`./testFixtures`), so
`test/systems/fixtures.ts` re-exports risa's and BlipToaster's. The rest of the shell's test tree changes an import
specifier and nothing else.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/_featureRoles.ts`:

````ts
// The feature roles that have a protocol node, for a registry a test builds by hand: every one is its package's own now,
// in the order the app's list always registered them (mgb, nes-n8-midi, risa-sync, sms-sync, lsdj-sync). Same as
// test/_coreRoles.ts: a helper for the test tree, not an app module, so a test that needs "a registry with the feature
// roles" keeps one list while the carts' roles live in their packages. lsdj-assets, risa-assets and bliptoaster's two
// have no protocol node and a test registers them by name (registerLsdjAssetsRole, registerRisaAssetsRole,
// registerBlipToasterRole).
import type { RoleRegistry } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import { NES_N8_MIDI_ROLE } from "@retroplug/n8/app";
import { MGB_ROLE } from "@retroplug/mgb/app";
import { RISA_SYNC_ROLE } from "@retroplug/risa/risaRole";
import { SMS_SYNC_ROLE } from "@retroplug/smsggdj/app";
import { LSDJ_SYNC_ROLE } from "@retroplug/lsdj/app";

/** Register the built-in feature roles that have a protocol node, in the app's registration order. */
export function registerFeatureRoles(registry: RoleRegistry): void {
  registry.registerRole(MGB_ROLE);
  registry.registerRole(NES_N8_MIDI_ROLE);
  registry.registerRole(RISA_SYNC_ROLE);
  registry.registerRole(SMS_SYNC_ROLE);
  registry.registerRole(LSDJ_SYNC_ROLE);
}
````

````diff
 //   contribution its exports do not publish, a manifest whose name is not its directory's, a contribution outside ts/
 //   and a contributing package the shell does not declare. A dependency that contributes nothing, and one whose

+// - the generated module itself refuses a duplicate key in the lists the registries look up rather than sequence: a

+test("the generated module refuses two roles of one kind", async () => {

-/** The BlipToaster theme table as the ROM bakes it: the `\xA5\x5ATHME` magic, then `count` INTERLEAVED entries
- *  of [7 role bytes + a 4-char name] — 11 bytes each, the name right behind its own record. That stride is
- *  BlipToaster's own and is NOT risa's layout (16 records, then 16 names), so a fixture written risa-style
- *  reads only entry 0 correctly. Role 0 (bg) is per-slot so a test can tell the entries apart; slot 0 is the
- *  real DFLT's 0x0D/0x30. `count` below 16 is for the table-bound check. */
-export function blipToasterThemeTable(count = 16): Uint8Array {
-  const ENTRY = 7 + 4;
-  const out = new Uint8Array(6 + count * ENTRY);
-  out.set([0xa5, 0x5a, 0x54, 0x48, 0x4d, 0x45], 0); // THEME_META_MAGIC
-  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
-    const off = 6 + i * ENTRY;
-    out.set([0x0d + i, 0x30, 0x00, 0x10, 0x30, 0x21, 0x11], off); // bg, normal, shaded, alternate, status, cursor, selection
-    for (const [k, c] of Array.from(BLIPTOASTER_THEME_NAMES[i % 16]).entries()) out[off + 7 + k] = c.charCodeAt(0);
-  }
-  return out;
-}
-
-/** The baked settings block as the ROM bakes it (src/core/settings.c): the `\xA5\x5ASETT` magic, the format
- *  byte, then the rig fields; +8 and +13..15 stay reserved 0xFF. Defaults are the power-on ones the ROM bakes -
- *  all zero except `ppu`, which is 1 (the screen draws), i.e. the block of a ROM straight out of the build. */
-export function blipToasterSettingsBlock(
-  fields: { version?: number; baseChannel?: number; ppu?: number; velCurve?: number; theme?: number; font?: number } = {},
-): Uint8Array {
-  const out = new Uint8Array(16);
-  out.set([0xa5, 0x5a, 0x53, 0x45, 0x54, 0x54], 0); // "\xA5\x5ASETT"
-  out[6] = fields.version ?? 1;
-  out[7] = fields.baseChannel ?? 0;
-  out[8] = 0xff; // reserved — held the default kit slot before the kit became CC-only
-  out[9] = fields.ppu ?? 1; // the one non-zero power-on default: PPU enabled
-  out[10] = fields.velCurve ?? 0;
-  out[11] = fields.theme ?? 0;
-  out[12] = fields.font ?? 0;
-  out.fill(0xff, 13);
-  return out;
-}
-
-// The theme table + settings block, spliced at `at` exactly as the ROM lays them out: ADJACENT, the settings
-// magic starting the byte after the table's last entry. That adjacency is load-bearing for the fixtures — it
-// is the case that bounds the theme count (countThemes stops on the $A5 it cannot read as a palette index),
-// so a fixture that left slack there would not exercise it.
-function splicePrgBlocks(rom: Uint8Array, at: number, themeCount = 16): void {
-  const table = blipToasterThemeTable(themeCount);
-  rom.set(table, at);
-  rom.set(blipToasterSettingsBlock(), at + table.length);
-}
````

The root `package.json`'s list becomes a dependency order of all twelve packages (`core sameboy mesen dsp mgb lsdj
graph-runtime n8 smsggdj risa native bliptoaster`), the root `CMakeLists.txt` calls `retroplug_package()` for each of
them from the list (one loop, with `node-sdk` first and `device-io` and `devtest` after them, because registering a
script pack needs the host `graph-runtime` adds), `cmake/packages.cmake`'s headers state what the checks cover and
what they do not, and the `[settings]` oracle's comment no longer says the shell holds LSDj's mode.
`packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`'s comment changes only. The lockfile follows the seven manifests this task
changed.

````diff
+# _retroplug_unwrap_option(<out> <item> <unwrapable>): an option as a literal when the generator expressions around it
+# are forms this check evaluates: the ones _retroplug_unwrap_item knows, and a condition's own value
+# ($<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-Ifoo>, $<$<CONFIG:Debug>:-Ifoo>), whose inner value is a literal. An option hidden behind
+# anything else (a target property, a configuration expression) is not evaluated, and the caller passes it unseen: a
+# compile option legitimately holds such an expression ($<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:/bigobj), and refusing every one would
+# refuse a build that declared nothing. The header says what that leaves unjudged.
+function(_retroplug_unwrap_option out item unwrapable)
+    set(_value "${item}")
+    set(_ok TRUE)
+    while(_value MATCHES "^\\$<")
+        if(_value MATCHES "^\\$<(BUILD_INTERFACE|LINK_ONLY|TARGET_NAME):(.+)>$")
+            set(_value "${CMAKE_MATCH_2}")
+        elseif(_value MATCHES "^\\$<\\$<(COMPILE_LANGUAGE|CONFIG):[^>]+>:(.+)>$")
+            set(_value "${CMAKE_MATCH_2}")
+        else()
+            set(_ok FALSE)

+        endif()

+    set(${unwrapable} "${_ok}" PARENT_SCOPE)

+

+# and whether that directory is the next item (a bare -I). The spellings the compilers take are all judged: -I, -iquote,
+# -idirafter and -isystem, attached (-Ifoo) or apart (-I foo), MSVC's /I and /external:I, and CMake's SHELL: form of the
+# separated ones (SHELL:-I foo). A SHELL: command that is none of these is no include flag.
+function(_retroplug_include_flag dir wants isFlag item)

+        set(_is TRUE)
+    elseif(item MATCHES "^(/external:I|-iquote|-idirafter|-isystem|-I|/I)(.+)$")
+        set(_dir "${CMAKE_MATCH_2}")
+        set(_is TRUE)
+    elseif(item STREQUAL "/external:I" OR item STREQUAL "-iquote" OR item STREQUAL "-idirafter"
+           OR item STREQUAL "-isystem" OR item STREQUAL "-I" OR item STREQUAL "/I")
+        set(_wants TRUE)
+        set(_is TRUE)
+    endif()
+    set(${dir} "${_dir}" PARENT_SCOPE)
+    set(${wants} "${_wants}" PARENT_SCOPE)
+    set(${isFlag} "${_is}" PARENT_SCOPE)

+# knows, or a bare flag whose value it cannot attribute), for a target that is not vouched for by RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP:

+# What this guards is ACCIDENT AND DRIFT, NOT A DETERMINED AUTHOR. It reads the target properties CMake has already
+# computed and the OWNERS table the build's target directories give it: a review's first pass, not a sandbox. The places
+# it deliberately does not look, so a later author does not read the list as a promise:
+#

+#     target's, and the cache flags that apply to every target (CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS and its sisters), which are the root's;
+#   - a generator expression whose value only the build generator knows ($<TARGET_PROPERTY:...>,
+#     $<TARGET_OBJECTS:...>, a condition with more than one operand such as $<$<AND:...>:-Ifoo>): a compile or link
+#     OPTION in one is passed unseen, as the comment in the gatherer says, because a build legitimately holds one that

+#   - a library name that matches no target of the build (a system library, a name a -L elsewhere resolves),

+#     owner table attributes a target by its SOURCE_DIR, which such a file does not move.

@@ -17,6 +17,15 @@
 #   alias        alpha links rp::beta, an alias of beta's target, which alpha does not declare: refused
 #   alias-declared  the same alias with beta declared: holds (an alias is judged as the target behind it)
 #   copt         alpha's compile options add -Ibeta's tree: refused like an include directory would be
+#   copt-genex   the same behind $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:...>: still the literal, so refused
+#   copt-relative  the same spelled relative to alpha's own directory: attributed there and refused
+#   copt-iquote  -iquote, and copt-idirafter -idirafter, copt-isystem -isystem, copt-external /external:I and copt-shell
+#                SHELL:-I: every spelling an include flag takes, each judged like -I
+#   link-path    alpha links a library by its path inside beta's tree: refused like a target of beta's
+#   link-path-shell  the same for a library in the shell's tree
+#   link-options-dir  alpha's LINK_OPTIONS add -L into beta's tree: refused like an include directory
+#   link-options-name  alpha's LINK_OPTIONS name a library of beta's with -l: refused
+#   link-options-name-shell  the same for a library of the shell's
 #   unjudged     alpha links a generator expression the check cannot evaluate: refused
 cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
 project(retroplug_package_gather NONE)

+        $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-I${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src>)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "copt-relative")
+    # A relative -I is not absolutised as an include directory is: the check reads it from this target's SOURCE_DIR,
+    # which is this directory, and it climbs into beta from there.
+    target_compile_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -I../beta/native/src)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "copt-iquote")
+    target_compile_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -iquote${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "copt-idirafter")
+    target_compile_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -idirafter${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "copt-isystem")
+    target_compile_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -isystem${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "copt-external")
+    # MSVC's spelling of -isystem.
+    target_compile_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE /external:I${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "copt-shell")
+    # CMake's SHELL: form of the separated flag, which is one item with a space in it.
+    target_compile_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE "SHELL:-I ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src")
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "link-path")
+    # A library linked by its file path: where it lies decides, as the target it comes from would.
+    target_link_libraries(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/native/src/libretroplug-beta.a)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "link-path-shell")
+    target_link_libraries(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../native/src/libretroplug-backend.a)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "link-options-dir")
+    # A search directory in beta's tree lets the linker find beta's library.
+    target_link_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -L${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../beta/lib)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "link-options-name")
+    # A library name the build's own target of that name attributes to beta.
+    target_link_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -lretroplug-beta)
+elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "link-options-name-shell")
+    target_link_options(retroplug-alpha INTERFACE -lretroplug-backend)
 elseif(RP_GATHER_CASE STREQUAL "unjudged")
````

````diff
+
+| Package | What |
+|---|---|
+| `@retroplug/core`, `@retroplug/dsp`, `@retroplug/tracker` | The TS libraries: the node contract and role contract, the DSP kernels and kit chain, the tracker layer's catalogs and neutral console helpers. |
+| `@retroplug/sameboy`, `@retroplug/mesen` | The consoles' roles and their settings enums (their native halves are still `packages/native`'s until F2). |
+| `@retroplug/lsdj`, `@retroplug/mgb`, `@retroplug/risa`, `@retroplug/smsggdj`, `@retroplug/bliptoaster` | The carts: their codecs, catalogs, roles, ROM providers, kit formats and protocol nodes. |

+| `@retroplug/graph-runtime`, `@retroplug/node-sdk`, `@retroplug/device-io`, `@retroplug/devtest` | The engine and node SDK, the box's device nodes, and the device check's test nodes. |
+| `@retroplug/testing` | The TAP harness, the script-node rig and the shared byte/deep-equal helpers. |

+A cart's or console's tests live in its own `ts/test/`, so the runner's slug for one is

+## The packages
+
+Every package under `packages/` is a workspace package: `@retroplug/<name>`, `private`, type `module`, a
+`package.json` whose `retroplug` member carries the contributions its language builds, and (where it has TypeScript) a
+`ts/` tree with a `tsconfig.json` that extends [tsconfig.base.json](../tsconfig.base.json). The members are `native`
+(a C++ target, [cmake/packages.cmake](../cmake/packages.cmake)'s), `script` (a device script pack),
+`app` (`ts/app.ts`, the module default-exporting `definePackage({ roles, romProviders, trackerIntegrations,
+kitFormats })`) and `protocol` (`ts/protocol.ts`, the module default-exporting the package's `DefinedNode`s, beside
+each node's `type` and span `label` and the role kinds it places). A package may have any combination; a manifest
+naming no member at all is refused at configure.
+
+**The registries are generated, not written.** [packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs](../packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs)
+writes the shell's `src/generated/{packages,protocol,scriptNodes}.ts` from the product list
+(`retroplug.products.desktop` in the root [package.json](../package.json)): `packages.ts` concatenates each package's
+`app` contribution, `protocol.ts` is the table `buildGraph` and the stores wire a role through, and `scriptNodes.ts`
+is the script-node bundle's entry, in span-label order. The product list is the **dependency order and the registration
+order both** (a package before the ones that use it, the shell last), and only a ROM provider's place in it is
+behaviour: the providers run in that order, and the first to match a ROM fixes a system's role-list order. A role's
+kind, a kit format's id and a tracker integration's marker role are looked up rather than sequenced (one package's
+roles interleave another's without consequence, and the markers are exclusive), so for those a duplicate is the
+hazard: the generated module refuses a role kind, a kit format id or a marker role declared twice, each with its own
+message. The generator itself refuses a list that puts a package before a dependency, a dependency the product does
+not carry whose contribution would be lost, a dependency on the shell, a duplicate product entry, a node type or span
+label declared twice, a label that is below 16 or leaves a gap, a role naming a node no package wires, a manifest that
+names a missing module or one its `exports` do not publish, and a contributing package the shell does not declare.
+The generated modules are gitignored and rewritten on every build (`retroplug-ts-packages`, which the three bundle
+targets depend on).
+
+**Fixtures are a package's, published for tests by name.** A cart's synthetic ROM images live in its `ts/fixtures.ts`
+and a manifest that publishes them names the subpath `./testFixtures`, never `./fixtures`: the name says what it is,
+and the boundary check still sees the file as the package's source (it is outside `ts/test`, so it may use no
+`devDependencies`). The shell's own tests ([test/systems/fixtures.ts](../packages/retroplug/test/systems/fixtures.ts))
+re-export the ones they share, so a store or menu test keeps one import.
+
+**The shell keeps four doors, until F4.** A shell module may re-export a name a package owns where the shell's own
+modules and tests import it through that module rather than the package's subpath: `src/kit/compile.ts` (each cart's
+compiler and kit format), `src/audioDriver.ts` (the kit effect and compile specs), `src/tracker/index.ts` (the tracker
+contracts and the carts' catalogs) and `src/trackerRegistry.ts` (the carts' integrations and the generated list). These
+are the shell's front door, not a package's: a pack imports `@retroplug/<name>` directly, and nothing else in the shell
+re-exports another package's name (the settings enums' door went in F1). They stay because their call sites are the
+shell's own - `menuDefs.ts`, `render.ts`, the stores and `test-native` - and retargeting them is the UI/store work F4
+does, not the split's.
+
+**The two boundary checks.** `pnpm check:boundaries`
+([check-boundaries.mjs](../packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs)) judges every file under a package's
+`ts/` tree, tests included, by TypeScript's own scanner: a relative import that leaves the package, an `@retroplug/x`
+or third-party module the manifest does not declare (a test may use `devDependencies`), any dependency on a shell
+(`@retroplug/retroplug` or `@retroplug/native`), a cycle in the declared dependencies, an `#include` that climbs out
+of the package, an `exports` entry that publishes a test module or names no file, and a `workspace:`/`npm:`/`link:`
+dependency whose spec names a shell or a package the workspace does not have (an alias of a package that exists is
+refused too: every other rule reads the key). A declared dependency no file uses is a warning, not a refusal. The
+native twin is `cmake/packages.cmake`'s: a package's targets may link, include and search only declared packages'
+trees, by target, by a library path, or through an include flag (`-I`, `-iquote`, `-idirafter`, `-isystem`,
+`/external:I`, a `SHELL:` list) or a link option (`-L`, `-l`), and the configure refuses anything else. Both run with an
+empty allowlist, and each has its own fixtures ([test/boundaries](../packages/retroplug/test/boundaries);
+`packages/native/test/packages`) that fail one rule each. They guard against accident and drift, not a determined
+author: each checker's header lists what it deliberately does not cover.
+
+**A package's tests are its own.** A test whose subject is wholly in a package lives in its `ts/test/`, runs on the
+package's `tsconfig` and keeps its fixtures and goldens beside it
+([packages/lsdj/ts/test/golden](../packages/lsdj/ts/test/golden) and the `.sav` corpus under `ts/test/savs`,
+[packages/risa/ts/test/golden](../packages/risa/ts/test/golden)); the runner's slug for one is `<package>/<path>`
+(`lsdj/sav`, `risa/record`, `bliptoaster/rom`, `smsggdj/rle`, `n8/n8MidiToFifo`), so a filter's spelling follows the
+move. Tests of the stores, the menus, `buildGraph`, the engine, `test-native` and `test-ui` stay with the shell, as do
+the ones that drive its registry (`test/system-settings/*`, `test/risa/detect`, `test/bliptoaster/romDetect`,
+`test/dsp/sms-sync`), whose subjects are the shell's provider dispatch and generated lists. The skip baseline
+([scripts/skip-baseline.json](../packages/retroplug/scripts/skip-baseline.json)) records nothing for the ts tier, so a
+move between it and the shell needs no entry.
+
 ## Hosts → test tiers
 
 Three of the C++ hosts (see [01-architecture.md](01-architecture.md)) each back a headless TS test
````
